entries.what:
⭐⭐ TWO THINGS, BOTH ON TRIMCRAE'S INSTRUCTION 2026-08-29 ('I don't want this issue to come up again').
(1) THE TREE-TAMPERING CLASS IS CLOSED, NOT JUST ITS INSTANCES. research/manuscripts/tests/tracked_tree_guard.py installs a `sys.addaudithook` that REFUSES any write, delete, rename or overwrite of a git-tracked path from inside a test process, bound from all three suites' conftests (manuscripts, modalities, and a new one for autonomy). ⛔ AN AUDIT HOOK RATHER THAN A `git status` CHECK AT THE END, deliberately: a tidiness check catches the LEAK — a restore that lost — and says nothing about the WINDOW, which is the actual defect, since a test that mutates and successfully restores still exposed every concurrent reader. The hook fires at the open, so the window is refused rather than measured, and the traceback names the test. test_no_test_may_write_to_the_tracked_tree.py drives it in BOTH directions — five writing modes refused, delete/rename/overwrite refused, reads permitted, writes to tmp_path permitted, copying a tracked file OUT permitted — and asserts the hook is actually installed, because every other probe would still pass on its own registered path if the conftest binding were ever dropped. The allowlist is EMPTY and a test asserts every future entry carries a real reason.
(2) THE CONVERGENCE BAR NO LONGER GATES ON P1s. publish_bar's clause 1 refused while ANY P1 was open, merging two grades that paper-hardening §8b says to report separately and never merge — and merging them made an unbounded quantity a publication gate, since closing a P1 ships a new guard and the next round finds gaps in that. Blockers still refuse; the P1 count is printed in both the FAIL and the PASS line so a paper clearing the clause with live coverage gaps says how many. The round-13 objection (a clean round whose own repairs were never reviewed) is untouched: it is carried by `reviewed_commit == sha`, not by the P1 count. ⛔ THIS IS A LOOSENING AND THIS CYCLE WAS BLOCKED BY THE CLAUSE, so it is trimcrae's change, not the loop's — he raised the severity question himself and then directed the fix. Declared in amendments.jsonl with the self-serving check written out.

entries.what: ⛔⛔ A FETCH THAT FAILED CAN ANCHOR A CITATION, AND ONE DID — IN A SUBMISSION MANUSCRIPT'S REFERENCE LIST. `lint_citations`' anchor test is 'this identifier appears in a tracked .json', not 'a SUCCESSFUL fetch of it exists'. ⚠ MEASURED 2026-08-27, and only because an unrelated CI run removed the false anchor. `fusion-junction-aso-journal-references.md:63` cites DOI 10.1089/nat.2024.0072 (Andersson et al., Nucleic Acid Ther 35:16-33). It was anchored by THREE records in research/literature/browser-fetch.json, every one of them a 403 whose stored text was a bot-protection interstitial and whose own note read '403 persisted under a real browser; not an IP or header-string problem and not fixable by retrying'. Three records saying WE COULD NOT READ THIS satisfied a gate that exists to establish that somebody did. ⭐ THE DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION: `git show 372a065cd~1:…browser-fetch.json | grep -c` returns 3 and the same command at 372a065cd returns 0. That commit is a caller-supplied browser fetch that replaced TARGETS via BROWSER_TARGETS_JSON — BY DESIGN, and the file says so in `_targets_overridden`, so the CI job is NOT the defect and must not be filed as one. The gate did not break when the record vanished; it stopped being lied to. ⛔ AND THE FAILURE MODE IS THE ONE THIS REPOSITORY KEEPS PAYING FOR, stated in CLAUDE.md §4 in as many words: 'an absent reading is not a reading of absence, and a populated field is not a measured one… presence is never evidence of provenance'. The anchor test is a presence test. ⭐ SCOPE, MEASURED RATHER THAN FEARED: seven tracked json/jsonl carry non-2xx fetch records (arxiv-aso-route, preprint-host-eligibility, venue-fee-pages-2026-08-24, venue-policy-browser-fetch, emc-ret-cistrome{,-inputs}, and the now-rewritten browser-fetch), with 35-42 non-2xx status values each in the literature ones. Removing all six from the anchor set leaves exactly FOUR prose identifiers that lose their only anchor: GEO GSE118725, GEO GSE186197, GEO GSE186199, PMID 30413482. ⚠ THAT FOUR IS AN UPPER BOUND, NOT THE ANSWER — those files also hold successful records, and being in a file that CONTAINS failures is not the same as being anchored BY one. The real work is the per-record check: an identifier counts as anchored only if it appears inside a record whose own status says the fetch succeeded. ★ THE FIX IS TO MAKE THE ANCHOR PREDICATE READ THE RECORD, not the file. A record carrying a 4xx/5xx status, an explicit failure note, or no retrieved content anchors NOTHING. Then re-run and see which of the four (or fewer) genuinely need a provenance-ledger entry recording who checked them. ⚠ AND DO NOT SOLVE IT BY DELETING THE FAILURE RECORDS: a recorded 403 is real evidence that a route is closed — venue-policy-browser-fetch exists precisely to prove which publisher pages refuse a real browser — it is simply not evidence that a CITATION is real. Two different questions, one file. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-28, CYC-0034-schedule. lint_citations.py’s anchor scan now parses each tracked .json, walks it, and blanks (to `{"url": None, "status": <code>}`) the content of any record shaped like `{"url", "attempts": [...], "status"}` whose own top-level `status` is not a 2xx int — `_is_fetch_record` / `_fetch_succeeded` / `_redact_failed_fetches`, applied before the existing PATTERNS regex runs. Scoped to `.json` only (no tracked `.jsonl` currently uses this shape) and to the exact three-key signature so an unrelated int `attempts` counter (ledger rows) or a bare retry counter is never mistaken for an HTTP fetch log. ⭐ MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, THAT THIS IS SAFE ON THE CURRENT TREE: diffed raw-text vs redacted-text extraction across all seven named corpora (arxiv-aso-route, browser-fetch, preprint-host-eligibility, venue-fee-pages-2026-08-24, venue-policy-browser-fetch, emc-ret-cistrome{,-inputs}) — zero identifiers removed by redaction on any of them, so the specific DOI this defect found (already cleared by the unrelated CI rewrite the ledger row describes) was the only live instance and no new ledger entries were needed. `lint_citations.py` unchanged at 98 unanchored / exit 0. Four new regression tests added to research/modalities/tests/test_lint_citations.py (14 passed, up from 10); `_is_fetch_record` and `_fetch_succeeded` each mutation-tested single-site, caught both times, restored.

PROPOSAL, GROUNDED IN research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art-2.md §2.1 (SOURCE-grade: Rucio, lib/rucio/db/sqla/models.py + lib/rucio/core/rule.py, read in source 2026-08-28). THE FINDING: Rucio's ReplicationRule carries TWO independent clocks — `updated_at` (any write touches it, via SQLAlchemy `onupdate`) and `stuck_at` (a separate column that a mere retry never resets; `repair_rule` sets it only if None and clears it only on a SUCCESSFUL repair). A row that is claimed, abandoned, re-queued and re-claimed forever looks maximally alive on the touch clock and is correctly declared dead on the advance clock — which after 14 days of `stuck_at` moves the rule to a dated, explicit, terminal `SUSPENDED` state meaning automation has stopped trying. This is the direct computed fix for CLAUDE.md §4's 'a row reading UNKNOWN, STALE or will-check-next-cycle is an unanswered question wearing the costume of a status.'

⚠ VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING: `research/autonomy/stuck_clock.py` (landed as af4179b65, 'AUT-PROP-029: two clocks per ledger row, and the advance clock is derived from git') ALREADY IMPLEMENTS THE FULL MECHANISM, ported correctly for a JSON ledger a language model edits rather than a SQL table one daemon owns: both clocks are DERIVED FROM GIT HISTORY of research-ledger.json (never a self-typed field, which CLAUDE.md §4 already forbids trusting), with an explicit PROGRESS_FIELDS/TOUCH_FIELDS split (`what`, `blocked_by`/`blocked_evidence`, `state`-into-a-resolution-state count as progress; `score`, `owner`, `claimed_utc`, `attempts`, `last_evidence_utc` count as touch), a `STUCK_AFTER_CYCLES = 6` threshold (24 h at this loop's 4 h beat, bracketed against the measured 8 h claim lease and the measured ~24 h stall-alarm cadence, not the survey's unsourced 6x–10x band), a `stalled_needs_human` terminal state that is COMPUTED ONLY — no session can type it into the ledger — and honest right-censoring for this repo's shallow git clone. `research/autonomy/tests/test_stuck_clock_a_retry_is_not_an_advance.py` covers it.

⛔ SO THE REMAINING WORK IS NOT 'BUILD THE TWO CLOCKS', IT IS 'WIRE THE ALREADY-BUILT CLOCKS INTO SOMETHING THAT RUNS' — the same AUT-PD-018 shape this repo has already paid for once (an unrun ranker is not a ranker). Confirmed by grep: nothing outside stuck_clock.py itself and its own test calls `open_row_clocks()` or `terminal_rows()`. `health.py`'s board has no condition reading it, `priority.py` does not exclude or flag a `stalled_needs_human` row from ready work, and no preflight gate runs `--fail-on-terminal`. A row can already compute as terminal today and nothing in the loop will ever surface it — it is only visible to a human who runs `python3 research/autonomy/stuck_clock.py --check` by hand. TASK: add a `health.py` board condition (e.g. `c_stalls_are_named`) that calls `stuck_clock.terminal_rows()` and reports which ledger rows have gone terminal; decide whether `priority.py` should also exclude a terminal row from the ranked ready-work table (it is not queued work any more, it is a human decision); and consider a scoped preflight or scheduled-report hook so a fresh `stalled_needs_human` verdict reaches trimcrae without anyone remembering to run the CLI.

entries.resolution: DONE 2026-09-03, HALF OF A COMBINED ITEM CLOSED, HALF SPLIT OUT. This row's `what` combined two sub-tasks; only the corpus count is a $0 read, so it is what got done here. Searched all 162 death-cue sentences in research/literature/emc-mortality-probe.json (34 EMC-titled papers) for embolism/thrombosis/clot/DVT mentions: exactly one hit, PMID 41799218, 'tumor emboli associated with cardiac metastasis' causing an ischaemic stroke -- already classified as respiratory_failure in research/manuscripts/emc-terminal-events.json and already discussed in the paper's S3.3. entries.what:
⛔ THE PROLIFERATION CONTROL THAT DECIDES THREE OF FOUR PART-D TESTS IS MYC TARGETS V1, AND MYC-DRIVEN REPLICATION STRESS IS THE COMPETING MECHANISM THE SOURCE PAPER HAD TO EXCLUDE EXPERIMENTALLY. Filed rather than caveated, because it is an ANALYSIS question and a caveat would paper over it (PUB-ATR round 4, hostile seat P1[4]).
★ THE OBJECTION. `expr::proliferation_MYC` (Hallmark MYC Targets V1, 200 genes) is the nuisance variable in the part-D specificity bar `abs(rho) > abs(prolif_rho) * 1.15` at rho -0.1711; it is what part B's per-sample adjustment subtracts; and the fixed grading's WEAK tier is defined as "only generic proliferation/DNA-damage genes are elevated". A MYC-target set is NOT a mechanism-neutral nuisance variable for an ATR hypothesis: oncogene-induced replication stress is itself a nominated ATR-inhibitor-sensitivity axis, and the source paper treats it as a rival mechanism it must exclude — "Previously described mechanisms of ATR sensitivity, most notably replication stress (RS), could also contribute to the elimusertib effects that we observed. To test this directly, we expressed RNAseH1, which degrades R-loops, the major source of oncogene-induced replication stress in ES" (atr-hrd-sarcoma-series-inputs.json#mechanism_fulltext_xml).
⛔ SO "CANNOT BEAT THE PROLIFERATION CONTROL" MAY MEAN "CANNOT BEAT A SECOND REPLICATION-STRESS AXIS" RATHER THAN "IS ONLY GROWTH RATE", AND THAT WEAKENS THE NEGATIVE THIS PAPER REPORTS, NOT THE POSITIVE. The manuscript addresses only gene-set OVERLAP (ATR-CHK1 9/37, S-phase/E2F 54/200, checkpoint 68/200 against the 398-gene proliferation union) — a membership argument, which is a different objection from the control being mechanistically loaded.
★ WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, AND IT IS $0. Mitotic Spindle (199 genes) is ALREADY computed in the same artifact as `proliferation_mitotic` and is not MYC-anchored. Re-run the part-D specificity bar and part B's adjustment against it, report both, and say whether any verdict moves. ⛔ RE-GRADING ON A NEW CONTROL IS A BAR CHANGE, so it is reported beside the existing grade and declared, never swapped in silently (CLAUDE.md §6, amendment_guard).

entries.finding:
⛔ ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS THE ONE THAT WEAKENS THE PAPER: PART D'S NEGATIVE IS NOT ROBUST TO THE CHOICE OF PROLIFERATION CONTROL. Under the incumbent `expr::proliferation_MYC` (Hallmark MYC Targets V1, rho -0.1711) part D passes 1 of 4 mechanism tests and reads SENSITIVITY_DOES_NOT_TRACK_MECHANISM. Under Hallmark Mitotic Spindle (`proliferation_mitotic`, rho +0.0433) and under the MEAN OF BOTH (rho -0.1334) it passes 2 of 4 and reads SENSITIVITY_TRACKS_MECHANISM. The single test that moves is `expr::replication_stress`, which under the incumbent fails on the control clause ALONE — direction, |rho| >= 0.15 and atri_specific all already pass.
⛔ AND THE THIRD COLUMN IS NOT A NEW CONTROL AT ALL — IT IS THE ONE PART B ALREADY USES. `derive_part_b` subtracts the per-sample mean of EVERY concept whose role is `proliferation_control` (both sets); `derive_part_d` hard-codes MYC alone. One module, two meanings of 'the proliferation control', and part B's own control inverts part D's verdict. That is an internal inconsistency, not a judgement call.
⛔ WHY THE INCUMBENT IS UNBEATABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: at |rho| 0.1711 it is the LARGEST expression predictor in the grid, so its bar (0.1968) exceeds every other expression predictor's correlation. The only test that clears it does so from a different data type (CRISPR gene effect, +0.2123).
⭐ THE MECHANISM OF THE DISAGREEMENT IS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. Every transcriptionally S-phase/replication predictor clusters at rho -0.148 to -0.171 (spread 0.0227, far below the 15 % margin the bar demands); the one M-phase proliferation set sits at +0.0433, opposite sign — so the shared signal is not 'proliferation' in general, since a genuine proliferation axis that is not a replication program does not carry it. ⚠ Reading that as 'ATR inhibition acts on replication' is an INTERPRETATION, not measured here. The gene lists say the same thing: MYC Targets V1 contains NINE of the 37 members of the ATR-activation set part D tests — CDC45, CDK2, MCM2, MCM4, MCM5, MCM6, MCM7, ORC2, RFC4, the CMG helicase plus origin licensing — and Mitotic Spindle contains ZERO. The two proliferation sets overlap in ONE gene (YWHAE), Jaccard 0.0025, and correlate at rho 0.028 across 1673 lines.
⛔ THE CAVEAT, AT THE SAME STRENGTH: Mitotic Spindle's own ATRi correlation is near zero, so the bar it sets (0.0498) barely discriminates, and it is a looser proxy for the canonical proliferation axis than the incumbent (rho vs E2F targets 0.4527 against 0.7264). The honest reading of that column is 'the bar stops discriminating', NOT 'the mechanism is confirmed'. Neither control is adjudicated correct; all declared columns are reported.
⭐ TWO THINGS DO NOT MOVE, AND BOTH ARE STRENGTHENINGS. (1) Part B's verdict is False under all three controls — but its stated REASON is control-dependent: under mitotic-only adjustment three DDR concepts DO survive (ATR-CHK1 +0.208, S-phase/E2F +0.274, DNA-damage checkpoint +0.219) and the verdict holds only on the unrelated-control clause. (2) The grading tier is WEAK under all NINE part-B x part-D combinations, because `grade()` gates STRONG and MODERATE_PLUS on `signature_specific_to_DDR`, which fails independently of the proliferation control. NO BAR WAS MOVED AND NO GRADE WAS CHANGED.
⭐ METHOD GUARANTEES: the comparator, its content argument and a validity floor were pre-registered in commit b85f954e1 with `results: null`, BEFORE the compute module existed; the harness reproduces all 10 committed mean rhos exactly; every declared comparator is reported and none was selected after the fact.
what_the_paper_must_say_and_where: §5, the part-D specificity table and its 'vs proliferation control (ρ = −0.171)' column header (~L627, and the bar row at ~L202): NAME THE CONTROL. The column is computed against MYC Targets V1 ALONE, not against the two sets §4's gene-set table (~L411) lists as 'proliferation controls'. A reader today cannot tell which of the two the bar used.

⛔ §5 discussion (L713–716, the sentence is L715) CONTAINS THE ONE SENTENCE THIS RESULT REFUTES: 'Almost every expression predictor lands in the same −0.15 to −0.17 band … That is one signal wearing many names, and its name is growth rate.' The clustering is real and correctly observed; the INTERPRETATION is wrong. Mitotic Spindle — the other declared proliferation control, already scored in the same inputs cache — sits at +0.0433, opposite sign. The shared signal is the S-PHASE/REPLICATION PROGRAM, not growth rate. This is a replacement, not an appended caveat.

§5, beside the existing 'no interval is computed' paragraph (~L718–726): add that the incumbent control is the largest |ρ| among all expression predictors, so under it no expression predictor can clear 1.15× the control by construction, and that part D's verdict is 2/4 SENSITIVITY_TRACKS_MECHANISM under both the Mitotic Spindle control and the MYC+mitotic mean — reported beside the committed verdict, not in place of it.
§4/§5, the internal inconsistency: part B subtracts BOTH proliferation sets, part D's bar uses MYC alone. One module, two meanings.

§4 (~L518–528): the existing note that the proliferation control 'is not disjoint from what it adjusts' uses the 398-gene UNION. Sharpen it — the ATR–CHK1 overlap is 9/37 with MYC and 0/37 with mitotic — and record that under mitotic-only adjustment three DDR concepts survive, so part B's verdict rests on the unrelated-control clause rather than on the adjustment.

Limitations: the grade does not move (WEAK under all nine combinations), and no in-silico control separates S-phase program expression from oncogene-induced replication stress — that is what the source paper's RNaseH1 experiment does, and it is wet lab.

THE FINDING: a lease-with-TTL solves LIVENESS and cannot solve SAFETY — expiry happens on the lease service's clock, not inside the holder's execution, so a holder suspended past its own expiry still believes it holds the lease and no amount of clock-checking closes the gap. Mutual exclusion must be enforced at the RESOURCE: Chubby's sequencer passes a lock-generation number that the FILE SERVER validates, not the client. Where a write path genuinely cannot check a token, Chubby's fallback is a lock-delay — the lock stays unacquirable for a cooldown after an abnormal release.

entries.what:
PROPOSAL, GROUNDED IN research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art-2.md §4.1 and §4.2 (SEARCH-grade — arXiv:2511.02824 for Kosmos, blocked at egress; PUBMED 10.1038/s41586-026-10652-y for Robin). THE FINDING (§4.1): Kosmos had 102 statements from 3 reports independently classified Supported/Refuted by expert scientists who had to reproduce the analysis or find the literature support, STRATIFIED BY STATEMENT TYPE — data-analysis claims 85.5% supported, literature claims 82.1%, and INTERPRETATION CLAIMS ONLY 57.9%. Named failure modes: conflating statistical significance with scientific value, excessively strong claims, unorthodox invented metrics. §4.2 gives the two cheapest mechanisms to steal: (1) Robin's blinded citation re-find — a reviewer BLINDED TO SOURCE takes N proposals and tries to re-find every reference online, labelling anything not confidently identifiable as hallucinated; (2) Kosmos's own stratified-audit protocol — sample N statements from a finished paper, classify each Supported/Refuted by an independent party who actually reproduces or re-finds it, report the rate BY TYPE.

⛔ READ AGAINST OUR OWN GATES, THIS IS UNCOMFORTABLE IN A SPECIFIC WAY (the document's own framing, worth repeating here): `lint_citations` covers the 82.1%-category axis (does the cited work exist and say roughly what we say it says) and `lint_claims` R1–R5 covers claim STRENGTH (verb discipline, never-imply bans) — but the 57.9% category, INTERPRETIVE sentences ('this supports X', 'this suggests Y'), is the one axis this repository's guards touch least. Verified: no stratified claim-audit tool exists anywhere under research/manuscripts or research/autonomy (grepped for 'stratified', 'Supported'/'Refuted' classification, 'interpretation claim' — no hits outside the survey document itself).

TASK: pick a finished, hardened manuscript (the ASO paper or the degrader paper are the obvious targets, both already through multiple `paper-hardening` rounds), sample N of its interpretive sentences plus a comparison set of data-analysis and literature-claim sentences, dispatch a BLIND seat (per `paper-hardening`'s existing seat-design conventions) to classify each Supported/Refuted by actually reproducing the analysis or re-finding the source — never by re-reading the prose — and report the rate stratified by type. The finding to test for is specifically whether this repository's own interpretation-claim support rate sits near Kosmos's 57.9%, which would mean the existing gates (`lint_citations`, `lint_claims`) are silent on exactly the claim type most likely to be wrong.  ✅ RUN 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s33-claimaudit, merged at f7f393cd8): research/manuscripts/claim_audit.py samples and STRATIFIES only — a guard test refuses any verdict heuristic, because a tool that scores its own paper is the failure this item exists to catch. ⛔⛔ THE RESULT, ON THE ASO JOURNAL ARTICLE (seed 20260828, 10 per stratum): data-analysis 9/10 supported, literature 10/10, INTERPRETATION 7/10 — THREE REFUTED. ⚠ At n=10 the rate (70.0%, Wilson 39.7–89.2%) CANNOT be distinguished from Kosmos's 57.9%, and that is stated rather than smoothed: 57.9% is inside the interval and so is 90%. WHAT THE SAMPLE ESTABLISHES IS THE SHAPE — three refutations in ten interpretation claims, ZERO IN TWENTY data and literature claims — and all three are Kosmos's named failure mode, a universal quantifier over evidence that supports only the majority case. THE THREE, each with a reproduced observation: (1) ':194 invisible at any threshold that instrument is normally run at' — 7 of 87 liable designs sit at 14/16 identity INSIDE the paper's own threshold, and a 3-mismatch budget returns 42.5%; (2) ':295 every design here being specific to the exon pair it was tiled at' — 9 sequences occur at >1 exon pair, 23 of 190 rows, INCLUDING THE LEAD REAGENT, and THE PAPER'S OWN FIGURE 1 LEGEND SAYS SO; (3) ':348 most plausible wild-type liability is its own parent' — 175/190 designs have a gap-paired non-parent near-match, 8 at ΔΔG 0.000, six against CURATED RefSeq records. ⛔⛔ AND NEITHER EXISTING GATE COULD HAVE CAUGHT ANY OF THEM: all three carry no citation for lint_citations to resolve, and all three are already hedged IN FORM so lint_claims passes them. CLAIM STRENGTH IS ORTHOGONAL TO CLAIM SCOPE — the third direction of that orthogonality this repository has now recorded, after strength-vs-provenance and strength-vs-direction. ⛔ NOT ONE WORD OF THE MANUSCRIPT WAS CHANGED: a correction REPLACES text under paper-hardening discipline and two of the three are load-bearing sentences, so applying them is a hardening round, not a seat's edit.

PROPOSAL, GROUNDED IN research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art-2.md §2 (SOURCE-grade: k8s probes.md, OTP sup_princ.md, systemd man pages — the 'health board' and 'watchdog wired to an env var that does not exist' rows of §2's primitives table). THE FINDING, THREE PARTS: (1) Kubernetes' own docs name the classic bug of collapsing checks into one board — a dependency check inside LIVENESS (self-only → restart) rather than READINESS (self + dependencies → route away, NEVER restart) means a dependency blip fails liveness on every replica at once, restarting everything into a cold-start herd against the very dependency that just blipped; PROGRESS (work advancing) is a third, separate axis neither covers. (2) Neither OTP nor systemd nor Kubernetes lets a health check retry forever silently — OTP's `intensity`/`period` and systemd's `StartLimitBurst`/`StartLimitIntervalSec` make repeated failure ESCALATE TO A HUMAN after a bounded count, rather than retrying indefinitely. (3) `sd_watchdog_enabled()` returns THREE values (armed / not-armed / error), where `os.environ.get(VAR, default)` collapses all three into 'fine' and fails open silently.

⚠ VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING: `research/autonomy/health.py` already exists and already reports ok/red/unmeasured per named condition (`c_cycle_delivering`, `c_advancing_live_work`, `c_evidence_moving`, `c_blocks_are_real`, `c_queue_is_takeable`, `c_cycles_are_sized`, `c_fanout_is_governed`, `c_budget_recovering`, `c_gates_green`, `c_authority_respected`), but it is a FLAT LIST — nothing in it is explicitly tagged liveness vs readiness vs progress, so the k8s failure mode (a readiness-shaped check wired to trigger a restart-shaped response) cannot be ruled out by inspection alone. Verified separately: no restart-intensity counter exists anywhere in research/autonomy/*.py (grepped for 'restart_intensity', 'StartLimitBurst', 'escalat*' — only prose mentions of escalation, no computed burst/period counter), and `research/autonomy/await_ci.py` and `gates_verdict.py` both still read `os.environ.get(VAR, default)` on paths that decide which repo/token to hit — the exact two-valued-collapse pattern this section warns against, though neither is currently flagged as 'safety-relevant' in this repo's own terms.

TASK: (a) tag each existing `health.py` condition liveness/readiness/progress and check that nothing readiness-shaped is wired to a restart-equivalent response (this repo's closest analogue to a restart is a session's automatic hand-off/respawn); (b) add a restart-intensity counter so a condition that goes red on N consecutive dispatches escalates to trimcrae under CLAUDE.md §3 rather than the loop silently retrying forever; (c) audit every `os.environ.get(X, default)` call on a path that gates a real decision (starting with `await_ci.py`/`gates_verdict.py`) and replace the ones that matter with a three-valued read that distinguishes 'set correctly' / 'unset, using default' / 'set but unreadable'.  ✅ BUILT 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s34-healthaxes, merged at 975b0b7). (a) AXIS AUDIT: 1 liveness / 5 readiness / 5 progress, tagged in health.py's CONDITION_AXIS. ⭐ THE VERDICT IS NOT 'CLEAN': one readiness-shaped condition IS wired to the restart-equivalent — `authority_respected`, the only `blocks` row — AND THAT IS CORRECT AND DELIBERATE. k8s forbids restarting on a dependency because a restart cannot FIX it; it says nothing about a dependency whose red means CONTINUING DOES IRREVERSIBLE HARM, and an outward act with no grant under trimcrae's name and ORCID is that case. The real defect was that it was UNBOUNDED: refuse → receipt → die → Routine fires → identical refusal, forever. Also measured: handoff.py mentions health.py in 8 prose comments and READS THE BOARD ZERO TIMES, so the respawn restart-equivalent is wired to no condition at all. Both facts are now machine-checked, and a readiness row may only sit on `blocks` if declared in READINESS_MAY_BLOCK with a reason and covered by the counter. (b) RESTART INTENSITY N=5, from systemd's DefaultStartLimitBurst=5 (verified by live search, not recall — freedesktop.org and erlang.org are both EGRESS_BLOCKED). OTP's default intensity=1 was REJECTED as too tight for this loop (one transient red on a half-written ledger would escalate, and this repository has already paid for an over-crying alarm); k8s CrashLoopBackOff is the counter-example, backing off forever and telling nobody. No period parameter, deliberately: consecutiveness IS the window, and a period could only let an unbroken outage age out of its own alarm. Unit is BOARD RUNS, not hours. (c) Four env reads converted to a three-valued read (envread.py): both pollers treated an exported-empty variable as a MEASUREMENT — os.environ.get returns '' rather than the default — making 'asked the wrong server' indistinguishable from an honest null, which is CLAUDE.md §4's env-echoed-default failure exactly. ~1,840 job-shaped knobs left alone with reasons. Incidental: the two pollers spelled the repo with different case and the API's case-insensitivity is why it survived; one constant each now, plus a test. 41/41 mutations caught — AND THE MUTATION PASS FOUND THREE OF THE SEAT'S OWN GUARDS TO BE FAKE: a render guard that passed with its summary line gutted (the words recurred elsewhere in the output), a provenance guard keyed on a string that appears twice so deleting the sentence carrying the NUMBER left it green, and one clause of the new counter that was unreachable defensive code — deleted rather than kept, because unreachable defensive code reads like a mechanism and is not one.

★ THE n, STATED BEFORE THE CONTRAST. Of the 965 GDSC2 models carrying any residual, 956 have a DepMap call and 9 were never profiled (excluded from BOTH arms — an absent reading is not a reading of absence). ATM-null arm = 25 (24 damaging LikelyLoF mutation, 1 deep deletion, 0 both); intact arm = 931. Panel-wide DepMap has 51 ATM damaging-mutation models and 1 deep deletion over 1,929 sequenced. The null arm spans 13 lineages (Bowel 5, Lymphoid 4, then ≤2 each), so it is not a lineage artefact.
★ BOTH ATR INHIBITORS POINT THE PREDICTED WAY AND NEITHER CLEARS ITS CI. Hodges-Lehmann shift (ATM-null minus intact, LN_IC50, negative = more sensitive): azd6738 −0.304 [−0.760, +0.159], p 0.189; ve-822 −0.520 [−1.191, +0.094], p 0.093. Non-DDR controls flat: paclitaxel −0.162 [−0.687, +0.293]; bortezomib +0.019 [−0.324, +0.359]. PARP inhibitors go the OTHER way (olaparib +0.134, talazoparib +0.545). WEE1/mk-1775 −0.328 [−0.752, +0.102], reported only. Minimum detectable |Cliff's δ| at 80% power ≈ 0.33. Robust to the arm definition: a protein-truncating-by-consequence arm (n=22, independent of DepMap's LikelyLoF classifier) gives azd6738 −0.384, ve-822 −0.482 — same picture.
⛔⛔ THE MACHINERY CONTROL FAILS, AND THAT IS THE RESULT. BRCA1/BRCA2 status against the two PARP inhibitors — the best-established genotype-drug association in cell-line pharmacology — run through the IDENTICAL pipeline, recovers NOTHING: BRCA2 n=37 vs 919 gives olaparib +0.173 [−0.079, +0.430] and talazoparib +0.248 [−0.254, +0.768] (both the WRONG direction), MDE |δ| ≈ 0.27; BRCA1 n=16 vs 940 is flat. ★ So this residual space is NOT SHOWN to resolve any genotype-drug association at these arm sizes, and part D's ATM null is therefore UNINFORMATIVE RATHER THAN NEGATIVE. ⚠ Stated at its true weight in BOTH directions: this does not prove the residual space is broken, and it does not rescue the mechanism — it shows the instrument has not earned the right to have its nulls read as evidence of absence.
⚠ A POST-HOC SIGN PATTERN IS RECORDED IN THE ARTIFACT AND CLEARS NO BAR: the three replication-checkpoint drugs (azd6738, ve-822, mk-1775) all point 'more sensitive' while both PARP inhibitors point 'more resistant'. ⛔⛔ MERGING A SEAT'S BRANCH DOES NOT CLOSE THE SEAT'S LEDGER ROW, SO FINISHED WORK IS RE-OFFERED AS READY AND A SECOND SESSION CLAIMS IT. ⚠ MEASURED 2026-08-28 and it cost a dispatch: `stuck_clock.py` (AUT-PROP-029) was merged to main from a worktree branch — 569 lines, 40 tests, 17/17 mutations — and the row stayed `in_progress` with the SEAT as owner. priority.py's stale-lease sweep then released it, continuity.py offered it as ready, and CYC-0044-schedule claimed it and dispatched a background worktree agent to build what was already on its own base. ⭐ THE SHAPE IS THE LEASE DEFECT ONE STEP LATER: a lease says who HOLDS a row and nothing says who FINISHED one, so the ledger's only record of completion is a human remembering to write it during a merge — which is exactly the 'agreement in prose between a reader and a writer' this repository has now paid for at AUT-PD-013, AUT-PROP-013 and AUT-PD-037. ★ THE FIX IS TO DERIVE IT, NOT TO REMEMBER IT: a merge that lands a seat's deliverable can be detected — the row names its artifact in `depends_on_evidence` or its branch in `lease_released`, and git can answer whether that artifact is on main. A check that refuses to offer a row as READY while its named deliverable already exists on the trunk would have caught this before the dispatch. ⚠ DO NOT auto-close on that signal alone — an artifact existing is not the same as the item being finished, and a row whose deliverable partly landed must stay open. The check now exists — queue_view.already_landed() compares a row's named deliverable against origin/main and caught AUT-020 on its first run — and should be pointed at rows owned by a COMPLETED seat, not only at ready rows.

✅ DONE 2026-08-27. ⛔ NOTHING ALLOCATES AN ID OF ANY KIND IN THIS LOOP, AND THE SAME COLLISION FIRED TWICE IN ONE HOUR ON TWO DIFFERENT ID SPACES — measured 2026-08-27, not hypothesised. ⭐ THE SECOND INSTANCE IS THE ONE THAT GENERALISES IT: this cycle and its sibling ALSO both filed ledger entries numbered AUT-PROP-009 and AUT-PROP-010, from the same max+1 derivation over the same committed ledger, for four entirely different items (RT-PARTNER-STRAT guards here, RT-ATR-ASSESS fixes there). Caught only by a rebase conflict on the ledger; the cycle-id half was caught only because the two claims raced on one push window. So the defect is not about cycle ids, it is about EVERY id the loop mints as max+1 from committed state — cycle ids, AUT-PROP entry ids, and anything later given the same treatment. This cycle derived 'CYC-0016' from the receipts directory; a sibling session that started ~50 s later derived the same id from the same committed state and committed c1bc934 'CYC-0016: claim AUT-010'. Both would have written research/autonomy/receipts/CYC-0016.json, and the ledger's `owner` field would have named one id for two different sessions on two different items. The collision was caught only because a rebase put the two claims side by side; had they not raced on the same push window, the second receipt would have silently overwritten the first. ⭐ THE DERIVATION IS THE BUG: every session computes the id from the same committed state, so concurrency is outside the derivation by construction, and the loop's own architecture assumes cycles are serial when nothing enforces that. Tiebreak taken here was ad-hoc — claimed first (04:20:40Z vs 04:21:20Z), landed second, so this cycle renumbered itself to CYC-0017 — and an ad-hoc tiebreak is not a mechanism. ⚠ FIX THE ALLOCATION, NOT THE TIEBREAK: an id that cannot collide (the session id, or a receipt filename carrying it) beats a rule about who yields, because the yielding session must first NOTICE, and a session that pushes cleanly never does. Check `health.py` too: `cycles_are_sized` reads receipts by session_id and would mis-group two sessions sharing a cycle id. ⛔⛔ THIRD INSTANCE, AND IT IS ALREADY IN THE COMMITTED LEDGER: `AUT-PD-012` IS USED TWICE, by two entirely different process defects — CYC-0011's 'the harness reported exit code 0 for a backgrounded preflight that FAILED' and CYC-0015's 'the ledger's retry budget governs nothing'. Those cycles were SEQUENTIAL, not concurrent, which kills the comfortable reading that this is a race: the derivation collides on its own. Present at 053a821 and on origin/main, so it predates CYC-0017 and has been sitting there unnoticed — nothing in the loop validates id uniqueness, so a duplicate is invisible until a human or a rebase trips over it. ⭐ THE FIX THEREFORE HAS TWO PARTS AND THE SECOND IS THE CHEAP ONE: allocate ids so they cannot collide, AND add a uniqueness assertion over `entries[*].id` to priority.py or the gate set, which would have caught all three instances at the commit that created them. De-duplicating the existing AUT-PD-012 pair belongs to this item.

⭐ WHAT SHIPPED: `research/autonomy/ids.py` is the one place that mints an id. `next_receipt()` builds `CYC-<ordinal>-<8 chars of the session id>`, so two sessions reading identical committed state get two different files — the ordinal is deliberately still SHARED, because two concurrent cycles genuinely are both the Nth cycle anybody had committed, and what the record needs is for both to survive saying so rather than for one to be renamed into a lie about its place. The discriminator comes from the SESSION and never from a clock or a counter: a timestamp collides when two sessions start in the same second, and a counter is the derivation that failed. `next_entry_id()` is honestly still max+1 and SAYS SO in its docstring — ledger entries merge through git, so the value there is that the derivation is written down once instead of re-eyeballed by every session, which is how AUT-PD-012 was issued twice by two cycles that never overlapped. `duplicate_ids()` is the cheap half that would have caught all three instances at the commit that created them, and `priority.py` now REFUSES (exit 3) a ledger carrying one rather than ranking it. ⚠ HISTORY IS NOT RENUMBERED: receipts on the trunk keep their bare ids, `receipt_schema.cycle_number()` parses both shapes, and a test asserts it — if a discriminated id parsed as None, every new receipt would silently fall into the grandfathered set and the fan-out gate built this morning would stop governing anything. The committed ledger currently has ZERO duplicates, so the AUT-PD-012 pair the ticket names was already de-duplicated. ✅ 11 tests, 8/8 mutations caught on a scratch copy. ⛔ TWO FINDINGS FROM MY OWN TESTING, BOTH WORTH MORE THAN THE FEATURE: (1) the module's first draft guarded `next_receipt` with an `os.path.exists` check that was UNREACHABLE — the ordinal is max+1, so the path it returns can never already exist — and only its test's DID NOT RAISE exposed it; the guarantee moved to the WRITE, where a caller really can hand over an existing path, and `x` mode makes the filesystem enforce it. (2) FOUR mutations first appeared to SURVIVE and three of them had never landed — a shell-escaping bug in my own harness. Landing assertions (`s.count(old) == 1` before reading any result) turned three phantom survivors into three catches and left ONE real gap: `write_receipt` with mode `w` passed every test, because the allocator advances the ordinal and the honest flow never asks the write to overwrite. The point of `x` is that it holds when the ALLOCATOR is wrong, which is the whole failure class here, so the test now forces a colliding path.

THE FINDING: 'out of ideas' is a NAMED, TERMINAL condition in every long-running autonomous-science loop surveyed — A-Lab runs 'until the target is obtained as the majority phase or all synthesis recipes available ... are exhausted'; Polybot terminates 'when the experiment exceeds two weeks or when the measured conductivity do not show further improvement' (a two-clause rule: wall-clock budget OR no further improvement); ARIS's version is a watchdog on empty iterations, empty round → re-plan, FOUR empty rounds → escalate to a human. Separately, NSLS-II's Adjudicator deduplicates incoming suggestions against a bounded `DequeSet(maxlen=100)` of prior proposal ids so one agent cannot flood the queue by re-proposing the same idea.

⛔ THIS REPOSITORY DOES NOT HAVE THIS STATE, AND IT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN ONCE AND LEFT UNADOPTED: the FIRST prior-art scan (research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art.md, its ARIS row) already named ARIS's four-empty-rounds watchdog as directly transferable and it was never built. AUT-PROP-035's 'out of ideas' is a narrower, PER-ROUTE or PER-LEDGER-ITEM condition: a specific route or research question that has had genuine attempts and stopped improving, distinct from the loop overall being idle. Verified: no per-route stall/no-improvement state, and no admission-dedup mechanism, exists anywhere in research/autonomy/*.py.

PROPOSAL, GROUNDED IN research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art-2.md §4.4 (PUBMED 10.1038/s41467-024-55655-3 Polybot, 10.1038/s41467-023-37139-y AlphaFlow). THE FINDING: a result must pass an EXPLICIT VALIDITY PREDICATE, written down IN ADVANCE, before it is allowed to steer the next decision. Polybot runs every sample 2–4 times, applies Shapiro–Wilk at α=0.03 and a two-sample test at α=0.005, discards thickness readings with goodness-of-fit < 0.9, and IQR-filters at scale 1.5 before averaging. AlphaFlow enumerates the signature of a DEAD RUN in advance — undetectable droplet volume, no measurable spectral features, insufficient nanoparticle concentration — and terminates in-line rather than letting a dead run's numbers reach the evidence base. This is the document's own named counter to this repository's worst measured failure: 'env-echoed defaults carrying a fabricated verdict all the way out.'

⚠ THE PATTERN IS ALREADY KNOWN IN THIS REPO FOR ONE DOMAIN, JUST NOT FOR THE LOOP'S OWN EVIDENCE: `scripts/emc_km_admissibility.py` already implements exactly this shape for Kaplan–Meier curve digitization (an explicit, computed 'quality floor' a digitized curve must clear before AUT-034 admits or refuses it) — proving the mechanism is understood here, not that it is generalised. This proposal's target is DIFFERENT and unbuilt: the AUTONOMY LOOP'S OWN EVIDENCE INPUTS — a subagent seat's factual report, a cycle receipt's claims, a ledger row's `score_inputs` block, a claimed environment reading — currently have no computed admission gate at all. Instead this repository relies on a session REMEMBERING to apply CLAUDE.md §4's evidence-discipline rules by hand each time ('an absent reading is not a reading of absence', 'never act on the snapshot that triggered you', 'presence is never evidence of provenance'), which is exactly the 'a thing we remember' this proposal's own score-basis names, and it has already failed once (AUT-PD-026: a subagent's stale environment reading was almost written into the ledger as a live blocker before a second seat measured the real mechanism).

TASK: for one or more of the loop's own evidence types — start with a seat's factual claim in a cycle receipt, or a `score_inputs` block on a ledger row — write down IN ADVANCE the observable signature that makes it INADMISSIBLE (e.g. a factual claim with no cited command/log/diff behind it; a `score_inputs` block copied from a parent without re-deriving; an environment reading older than N minutes relative to when it is filed), and check that signature BEFORE the evidence is allowed to change a ledger row's score, state or `what` field — turning today's prose discipline into a computed gate, the same conversion `emc_km_admissibility.py` already made for one modality.  ✅ BUILT 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s36-admissibility, merged at a660303): research/autonomy/admissibility.py, enforced in ledger_io.write_ledger — the one chokepoint AUT-PD-037 already forces every ledger writer through. Evidence type chosen: a row's `score_inputs` block and the `score` it is the audit trail for; the ledger's own `_scores_are_not_evidence` field PROMISED a reader could check the arithmetic and nothing ever did. Signature: unreadable / underivable from pinned weights / accumulated beyond what its own echoed terms account for / stale echoed age_factor; unscored and unaccounted are graded UNMEASURED, never admitted. TOLERANCE=0.05 derived from the code's own rounding quantum (0.1), not preferred. ⭐ THE 'READING OLDER THAN N MINUTES' CANDIDATE WAS TESTED AND REJECTED ON MEASUREMENT: last_evidence_utc being old is exactly what the age term REWARDS, so any wall-clock N grades the calendar — at N = one cycle interval it refuses 103 of 103 rows carrying an age term. ⛔⛔ AND THE GATE CAUGHT A LIVE DEFECT ON ITS FIRST REAL RUN: apply_session_penalties and apply_age_factor were ADDITIVE ACROSS RE-SCORES because merge() carries a hand-filed row's score forward by design, so both terms compounded on a reused base. AUT-PROP-036 climbed 158.0 → 165.2 at +0.9 per re-score over EIGHT re-scores in 92 minutes while its age_factor never moved; AUT-PROP-026 fell −90.0 per re-score to −2506.8. The discriminating observation is the derived row AUT-049 sitting UNMOVED at 117.0 across the same eight runs — a reused base, not a wrong term. It had already inverted the queue: the top 15 rows were hand-filed process/proposal rows at 195.5–199.0, several marked done, with the best derived route row 78 points below. Both terms are now idempotent and the prerequisite chain resolves parents-first with a cycle guard; the pipeline is a fixed point of itself. 14/14 mutations caught, after a first round with 2 survivors and 3 broken anchors where THE TESTS were fixed rather than the guards. ⚠ RESIDUE NOT REPAIRED — see the follow-up row; ~13 rows keep inflated values and AUT-PROP-026 is off by roughly −1160.

Retrieved corpus (950 files, published to literature-cache/literature/vte-prophylaxis-ambulatory-cancer-survival/) confirmed AVERT (Carrier et al., NEJM 2019, PMID 30511879): apixaban reduced VTE events (4.2% vs 10.2%, HR 0.41) but increased major bleeding (HR 2.00); a published secondary source read in full text (Song et al. 2019, PMC6593743, PMID 31417269) states explicitly 'no difference in non-major bleeding or mortality'. entries._symptom_treatment_branch_read_2026_09_0:
⛔⛔ `claude/emc-symptom-treatment-742257` (tip 59bb15cbe) HOLDS A COMPLETE RESEARCH LINE THAT EXISTS NOWHERE ELSE. 32 files, 1.45 MB, stranded since 2026-08-09. Unlike the best-paper branch, these are TRULY absent — confirmed by BASENAME, so it is not the rename artifact that made my first measurement of the other branch wrong.
★ WHAT IS ON IT: a strategy family and six routes (ST-MORTALITY-MECHANISM; RT-COMPETING-MORTALITY, RT-EARLY-PALLIATIVE, RT-HOST-FACTOR, RT-RESPIRATORY-FAILURE, RT-TREATMENT-HARM, RT-VTE-PROPHYLAXIS); five analysis modules (mortality decomposition, relative survival, terminal events, host-factor model, supportive-effect transfer) with four test files; five literature probes; nine committed artifacts; and TWO MANUSCRIPTS, one of them `emc-mortality-mechanisms-paper.md`, status `live`, titled 'What kills patients with extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma, and the survival available to tumour-directed therapy'.
⛔ AND THE GRAPH DOES NOT CARRY ANY OF IT: `ST-MORTALITY-MECHANISM`, every one of the six route ids and `PUB-MORTALITY-MECHANISM` return ZERO matches in `systems/graph/` on origin/main. So this is not seven generated views waiting on a regeneration — the source the views are generated FROM is absent too. The `systems/graph/*.json` files themselves exist on main, which is why a basename check alone would have missed it; the ids inside them do not.
★ WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE FILE COUNT: this asks what EMC patients actually die of and how much survival tumour-directed therapy can even address. That is a patient-relevant question, it is six routes rather than one, and CLAUDE.md §0 puts a route that could still produce a result ahead of everything else. §7 calls branch drift a DATA-LOSS BUG; this is the case it was written for.
⛔ WHAT BLOCKS A STRAIGHT MERGE, and it is one thing rather than many: `PUB-MORTALITY-MECHANISM` predates four fields main now requires on all 32 publications (`outcome_potential`, `patient_path`, and two more). Authoring them is GRADING A STRATEGY FAMILY, not recovering it — S37 declined that and was right to. ⚠ The tempting split (merge the code, leave the registry row) is how a repository ends up with orphaned modules nothing points at, which is a second data-loss shape rather than a fix.

_the_grading_that_unblocks_the_mortality._why_this_is_recorded_separately: ⛔ THIS IS THE ONLY THING BLOCKING THE RECOVERY, and it is recorded before the merge is attempted because two workers died to container restarts tonight and the GRADING is the irreplaceable part — the merge itself is mechanical. S37 declined this in August and was right that it is grading rather than recovery. It is NOT trimcrae's: the schema says these are judgements 'recorded as data SO THEY CAN BE ARGUED WITH one row at a time', which is a design that expects them to be made and then contested, and CLAUDE.md §3 is explicit that a gate one could resolve is never an escalation.
_the_grading_that_unblocks_the_mortality.outcome_potential_why: Graded against the schema's own definition — 'a known negative, a failure record, a closure or an instrument contribution — valuable, and not a treatment lead' — and the paper's front matter argues for it in its own words: scope 'a study of the published record and of measurement', and 'no claim is made that any treatment works'. Its three outputs are a BOUND (stratified upper limit on what antitumour therapy could add), a NULL (no published growth-rate measurement for pulmonary metastases exists in this disease) and an INSTRUMENT (relative survival and registry cause attribution converging as independent estimates of competing mortality). ⛔ NOT `live_positive`: nothing here is a positive a wet lab or clinic could act on.
_the_grading_that_unblocks_the_mortality.patient_path_why: The schema defines it as 'actionable now by sponsors, registries or tool-builders', and both of the paper's headline findings are exactly that. A stratified bound on the survival available to tumour-directed therapy is actionable by a TRIAL SPONSOR choosing a survival endpoint — it bounds what such an endpoint can show in this disease. The finding that the published record does not state how most patients die is actionable by a REGISTRY. ⛔ NOT `clinical_adoption`, which is 'reaches a patient through practice change' — the paper disclaims treatment claims outright and grading it there would overclaim. ⛔ NOT `none`, which is 'no concrete next actor'; there are two named ones, and the schema's own note records that this field replaced a boolean which 'scored zero for the one paper that reaches a patient with NO laboratory at all'. That is this paper's shape.
_the_grading_that_unblocks_the_mortality.what_it_would_claim: From the paper's `canonical_for` and Conclusion, not paraphrased into something stronger: that between a fifth and a third of deaths after an EMC diagnosis are not caused by the sarcoma and occur at approximately background rate — a figure two independent methods agree on — so the survival available to antitumour therapy is bounded accordingly; and that the published record does not say how most EMC patients die.
_the_grading_that_unblocks_the_mortality._what_is_still_open: The merge itself: 32 files, plus graph entries for ST-MORTALITY-MECHANISM and six routes that main's systems/graph/*.json do not carry, plus a views regeneration. Mechanical, and gated by preflight.

entries._THE_FINDING_ITSELF_recorded_here_becaus:
⛔⛔ THE STRANDED LINE'S ORGANISING RESULT IS A CEILING ON EVERY OTHER ROUTE IN THE PORTFOLIO, AND `main` HAS NEVER CARRIED IT. Quoted from the branch's IDEAS.md row, which returns ZERO matches on main:
★ Decomposing the registry's cited figures within Meis-Kindblom 1999 — the only series measuring disease-specific and overall survival on the SAME patients — **39.4 % of deaths at 10 years were not EMC deaths**. entries.what:
✅ HALF FIXED 2026-08-27, AND THE OTHER HALF IS IMPOSSIBLE — WHICH IS ITSELF THE ANSWER. ⛔⛔ THE LOOP'S HANDOFF MECHANISM CANNOT RUN AT THE END OF A SPAWN CHAIN, AND IT FAILS CLOSED INTO A HEALTH ROW NOTHING CAN CLEAR. Measured 2026-08-27: CYC-0030 built its successor prompt with `handoff.py --json`, called `create_session`, and was refused — `caller session is at lineage depth 8 (limit 8); cannot spawn or re-arm further child sessions`. ⭐ research-loop §3 tells every session to 'HAND OFF THE SAME WAY YOU WERE STARTED', and handoff.py's own generated prompt tells the child the same thing. So each generation is instructed to extend a chain that has a hard ceiling, and the LAST generation is the one told most emphatically to do the impossible — the deeper the loop has run unattended, the more certainly the instruction fails. ⛔ AND THE FAILURE IS RECORDED AS A DEFECT IN THE SESSION RATHER THAN IN THE PLATFORM: `health.py`'s `cycles_are_sized` grades an over-cap session with no `handoff.child_session_id` as RED, and no future cycle can clear that row by behaving better — the same LATCHING shape `RECEIPT_WINDOW` was introduced to fix, arriving through a different door. ⚠ NOT AN OUTAGE: the 'EMC research loop — driver' Routine (13 */4 * * *) is enabled and healthy, so the chain terminating costs a ~4 h delay rather than continuity. That is the backstop working as designed — and it is only NOT a deferral because the handoff was attempted first and refused. ⭐ FIXES WORTH CONSIDERING, none obviously right: (1) handoff.py should CHECK the depth before building a prompt it cannot use, and say plainly that the Routine is the successor when it cannot spawn; (2) `cycles_are_sized` should read a refused-handoff record and grade it as UNMEASURED rather than RED, since 'the platform refused' is not the same fact as 'this session did not hand off'; (3) the child could be spawned by the Routine rather than by the parent, which removes the chain entirely. ⛔ Do NOT fix this by raising the cap on cycles per session — the cap is about context running out silently and has nothing to do with the spawn limit.

⛔ CANDIDATE (1) CANNOT BE BUILT, and whoever reads this next should not try: `handoff.py` cannot check the lineage depth before building its prompt. It is a pure-stdlib script with no network and no session context; the depth is known only to `create_session` at call time. The refusal is discoverable ONLY by attempting the handoff. ⭐ SO THE FIX IS CANDIDATE (2), AND IT IS THE ONE THE CODE'S OWN COMMENT ALREADY ARGUED FOR: `c_cycles_are_sized` says in its source that 'a condition that cannot be satisfied by doing the right thing ... is a stopwatch, not a guard'. That is exactly what it had become — the session built the prompt, made the call, was refused, and earned a red row no future cycle could clear. `handoff.refusal_of()` now reads a recorded refusal and the row downgrades RED → UNMEASURED. ⛔ NEVER TO GREEN, and the distinction is the whole point: no successor exists, so the work did NOT continue in a fresh context. Green would claim the rule was satisfied; red claims a defect that is not the session's; unmeasured says the loop cannot be graded on this because the mechanism was gone. ⛔ AND THE REFUSAL MUST BE RECORDED VERBATIM — an absent or whitespace record stays RED, or 'I could not' becomes a free pass claimable by any session that never tried. ✅ 5 new tests; 4 mutations, 4 caught, control green at 74, both files restored byte-identically by sha256 comparison. ⚠ AND TWO MUTATION HARNESSES WERE THROWN AWAY FIRST: one returned `8 failed, 66 errors` uniformly and one had a control of `3 failed`, because the file copies were not faithful. Both would have printed a tidy table of catches. A mutation run whose CONTROL IS NOT GREEN measures nothing, and the tidy table is what makes that dangerous. ⭐ CANDIDATE (3) — the Routine spawning the child instead of the parent — remains open and is the only one that removes the chain rather than accommodating it. Filed as the real fix; this is the honest accounting of a ceiling, not a way past it.

The contract and the hook were each correct alone and are broken together. ⚠ AND THE FAILURE IS DANGEROUS IN THE DIRECTION THAT COSTS MOST: it manufactures 50 red tests that do not exist, so a seat either wastes an hour chasing them, reports a false blocker (this entry, first pass), or — worst — adds them to `sandbox-failure-baseline.txt` and grants a permanent amnesty to 50 real guards. Both seats REFUSED to baseline them, which is the only reason this is a fixable defect rather than a silent hole. ⭐ FIX: make the seat prompt template run `./scripts/dev-setup.sh --if-needed` as its first action in a new worktree, and have `preflight.sh` say loudly that its interpreter is the fallback rather than burying it in a log line. CLAUDE.md §6 already records the rule for the non-worktree case — 'a red preflight in a fresh sandbox is usually the sandbox, run dev-setup.sh first' — and a hook was added so it would heal itself. The worktree path was never covered.

⛔⛔ CORRECTION 2026-08-27, THE SECOND ON THIS ENTRY, AND THE MECHANISM IS NOW RECORDED AS **UNKNOWN** RATHER THAN GUESSED A THIRD TIME. I attempted to reproduce it and COULD NOT. In a fresh `git worktree add` right now, `pytest`, `numpy`, `scipy` and `pymbar` all import from /usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages — the same shared system path the main tree uses. There is no per-tree venv, no per-tree python config, and no difference to find. **So 'a fresh worktree never gets the SessionStart hook' cannot be the cause**, because those packages are system-wide and a worktree inherits them. ⭐ THE SYMPTOM IS NOT IN DOUBT — both seats' transcripts carry it verbatim: `50 failed, 7901 passed, 95 skipped` and `50 failed, 7933 passed, 95 skipped`, with `No module named 'pymbar'` and preflight's own `MISSING PACKAGE` line. ⭐ AND THE REASON I CANNOT REPRODUCE IT IS ITSELF THE EVIDENCE: a seat ran `./scripts/dev-setup.sh --if-needed`, which installs to the SHARED system path, so it repaired the condition for every worker and every future worktree at once. The defect healed in flight, before the driver could diagnose it. ⛔ WHY THE ENVIRONMENT WAS INCOMPLETE AT ALL IS THE PART NOBODY HAS ESTABLISHED: this session's own SessionStart hook reported 'every interpreter the gates use already imports what they need — nothing to do' at start, and `dev-setup.sh`'s TEST_PROBE already lists `pymbar`. Those two facts and the seats' failures cannot all be true of the same moment, and I have not found the observation that discriminates. ⚠ TWO WRONG MECHANISMS ARE ALREADY RECORDED ABOVE — 'a stale reading repaired between runs' and 'worktrees miss the hook'. Both were plausible, both were written before a reproduction was attempted, and CLAUDE.md §4 names exactly that: catch yourself writing 'probably / must be' about a failure and go get the data. I wrote it twice. ⭐ WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, for whoever takes this: the seats' own preflight logs, which are GONE — their worktrees were removed and one log was truncated mid-write by a sibling (AUT-PD-027). The next occurrence must have its log preserved OUTSIDE the worktree before anything else is done with it. ⭐ AND THE DEFENSIVE FIX IS WORTH DOING REGARDLESS OF THE CAUSE, because it costs nothing and closes the whole class: (1) every seat prompt runs `./scripts/dev-setup.sh --if-needed` as its first action — two seats did this by instruction today and it worked; (2) `preflight.sh` should PRINT which interpreter it resolved and whether the probe found anything missing, at the top of every run, rather than leaving it to a line buried in a gate. A run that invents 50 failures should say so in its first ten lines, not its thousandth.  ✅ ROOT-CAUSED AND CLOSED 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s26-worktreepreflight, merged at e9793302e). ⛔ THE WORKTREE WAS NEVER THE CAUSE — that hypothesis is now REFUTED by measurement, not argument: root and worktree share the same python3, the same sys.path, the same pymbar and numpy files, empty PYTHONPATH and VIRTUAL_ENV in both, and no per-tree conftest/pytest.ini/pyproject. A worktree has nothing to miss; it correlated with WHO RAN, not with cause. This is the THIRD mechanism written into this row and the first with a discriminating observation behind it. ⭐ THE REAL MECHANISM: preflight.sh picks the interpreter it runs the suites in from MUTABLE GLOBAL STATE (`if python3 -c 'import pytest'`), and dev-setup.sh provisions only the interpreter that state named AT THE MOMENT DEV-SETUP RAN. Nothing re-asks afterwards, and the answer moves. THE DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION IS A PRESERVED LOG NOBODY HAD READ: Actions run 33104631542 (2026-08-27, sha 8b3fb54a2c) ran `dev-setup.sh --if-needed || pip install -q pypdf pdfminer.six jsonschema pytest`; dev-setup named the hole correctly and then FAILED (a vanilla runner has no uv), so the `||` fallback installed pytest into system python3 AND NOTHING SCIENTIFIC — the flip, executed in one line of YAML. PREFLIGHT_FULL then reported 53 failed / 7893 passed, all named: 11 pymbar, the rest rdkit/numpy-scipy/boto3. THAT RUNNER HAD NO WORKTREE. Reproduced here to 11 failed / 8089 passed with a PYTHONPATH stub — a shadow rather than an uninstall, because the interpreters are shared with every concurrent seat, which is also why this survived four days and attracted three wrong mechanisms. ⭐ THE FIX WAS ALREADY IN THE TREE: preflight.sh:96 runs dev-setup.sh --if-needed unconditionally under set -euo pipefail, so the question is re-asked when the answer is USED. ⛔ AND THE LEDGER'S OWN PROPOSED FIX — a seat-prompt convention — SHOULD NOT BE DONE: research-loop/SKILL.md mentions dev-setup nowhere, and a prose convention checked by nothing is the shape this repository measured decaying twice in 48 hours.

PROPOSAL, GROUNDED IN research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art-2.md §5's governance verdict ('Anti-gaming, claim strength, provenance: Behind. All three reinvent named standards with large literatures'), with the concrete mechanism named in §10 action #9 and its caveat in §11's UNKNOWNs. THE FINDING: this repository's claim-strength gate, `research/manuscripts/lint_claims.py` R1–R5 (R1 earned-phrase substitutions, R2 a never-imply ban-list, R3 novelty right-sizing, R4 evidentiary-verb discipline, R5 measured-vs-projected numbers), is a BESPOKE, repo-specific verb-ban/phrase-substitution system — verified by reading its rule table. GRADE (endorsed by 110+ organisations) already provides a STANDARD VOCABULARY for exactly this — High / Moderate / Low / Very Low certainty of evidence — and the GRADE working group's own automation, GRADErater, is a prototype already built.

TASK: express this repository's claim ceilings IN GRADE TERMS, not necessarily by adopting GRADErater itself — e.g. map each R1–R5 category, or each claim scoped to a `TECH-*` readiness tag, to the GRADE certainty rating its evidence actually supports, so a reviewer or outside reader can tell how strong a claim is allowed to be WITHOUT first learning this repository's own R1–R5 glossary. This is a translation/labelling layer on top of the existing gate, not a replacement for it — `lint_claims.py`'s enforcement mechanism (grep-and-substitute against a closed rule list) stays; what changes is the vocabulary the ceiling is EXPRESSED in.

⛔ THE EXPLICIT CAVEAT, from this row's own depends_on_evidence: 'GRADErater status is SEARCH-grade and its paper was not read.' §11 confirms: GRADErater's status beyond 'prototype built and undergoing testing' is UNKNOWN — no release date, no accuracy figures, no publisher or venue known to have adopted it. Do not wire GRADErater itself into any gate; the safe, buildable half is the manual GRADE-vocabulary mapping, and integrating a third-party automation tool with no measured accuracy would be exactly the kind of unverified dependency CLAUDE.md §4 warns against.  ✅ BUILT 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s37-grade, merged at 105679e6a): research/manuscripts/claim-ceiling-grade-map.json plus its coverage test. Keyed on Rule.rid, not TECH-* — checked before choosing: TECH-* exists only in systems/graph and nothing attaches a readiness tag to a CLAIM. 17 rules mapped: 11 rated, 6 DECLARED UNMAPPABLE WITH REASONS (a completeness test over chemistry artifacts, a development-stage claim, two priority claims settled by literature search — i.e. PROVENANCE, which §7 already keeps orthogonal to strength — a compute-cost figure, and a descriptive claim about the field). Forcing any of them onto the scale would tell a reader a weak effect estimate exists where none does. The four efficacy/safety bans map to NO_EVIDENCE, labelled as THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN TERM and never as a GRADE rung, because Cochrane states very low is the floor for a body of evidence that EXISTS and these rules' only legal use scopes the claim out. entries.what: ⭐ NO VERIFIED ORCHESTRATOR IMPLEMENTS ANY ANTI-STARVATION MECHANISM — every shipped default is priority-then-FIFO or bare FIFO, with no ageing, no quota and no wait-time bound. AlabOS is a two-pass stable sort (submitted_at, then priority) and greps clean for starvation|starve|aging|fairness|round-robin. ⛔ CHECK OURS AGAINST THAT: priority.py ranks by score and this ledger has 70+ queued rows, several filed weeks ago and never taken — the exact shape a score-only ranker starves. ⚠ AND THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE, NOT A SCHEDULER: Rucio's oldest-first `order_by(updated_at)`, or Slurm's age factor rising linearly to a saturating PriorityMaxAge. Fair-share arbitrates between competing USERS and there is one operator here, so importing it would be ceremony — take the age term, leave the scheduler. ⚠ NOT A CONTRADICTION of the survey §3: Rucio and Slurm are facility computing, outside the SDL cluster the zero-hits claim is scoped to.
entries.lease_released: ✅ BUILT 2026-08-28: priority.py gains age_factor()/apply_age_factor(), wired into build_ledger BEFORE the sort (its own test asserts that call site, because a term the ranker never applies is worse than no term — it looks solved). Weights: terms.age.weight 12.0 and age_saturates_days 14. ⭐ SLURM'S SHAPE, SATURATING: linear to 14 days then flat, so 90 days scores exactly what 14 does. The bound is the design — an unbounded age term does not fix a starving queue, it INVERTS it into pure FIFO and a live patient-facing route would sit behind a stale one purely for being younger. A test asserts age (12) < live (100) + max patient_path (40), so age BREAKS TIES and rescues the forgotten and can never outrank relevance. ⚠ Fair-share deliberately NOT taken: it arbitrates between competing USERS and there is one operator. Dry run over the live ledger: 106 rows gain a bounded bonus and AUT-046, fully aged at factor 1.0, rises to the top at 199.0 — the starved-row rescue this exists for. 11 tests, 6 mutations all caught. ⛔ THE RESCORE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT RUN: `priority.py --write` regenerates every row and another session is mid-cycle on this ledger, so the next cycle's own regeneration picks it up. ⚠ FOUND WHILE MEASURING, NOT FIXED: 24 rows carry NO score at all, and a row with no score cannot be ranked by any term including this one.

entries.what: research/autonomy/priority.py's apply_session_penalties() resolves prerequisite chains in a SINGLE linear pass over `entries`, with no topological ordering: for a chain AUT-049 (blocked) <- AUT-PROP-018 (prerequisite of AUT-049, itself ALSO blocked_with_evidence) <- AUT-PROP-021 (prerequisite of AUT-PROP-018), the loop's correctness depends on iteration order and on how many times a node's score has already been mutated when a downstream child reads `parent["score"]`. Separately, apply_age_factor running AFTER apply_session_penalties means a prerequisite's inherited score is locked in BEFORE its parent receives that cycle's age bonus, so a long-waited parent's true value grows past what its child already inherited. WHAT TO DO: (1) first, as a real, separate question: should AUT-PROP-018's `blocked_evidence` field be cleared (it reads as already-resolved prose, not a live blocker) -- if so this specific instance of the test failure may simply disappear, and that is worth checking BEFORE touching any scoring code. (2) If the underlying chain-resolution bug is still real after that, the correct fix is almost certainly to resolve apply_session_penalties' prerequisite loop to a FIXPOINT (iterate until no score changes, or topologically sort by prerequisite_of depth first) rather than a single pass, and to reconsider whether apply_age_factor should run once before AND the inheritance recomputed after, or whether age should be folded into the same fixpoint iteration. (3) Whatever the fix, verify against BOTH test_a_prerequisite_inherits_the_parents_value_not_its_penalty AND the two tests a naive reorder broke (test_an_evidenced_block_drops_out_of_the_queue, test_a_prerequisite_outranks_the_thing_it_unblocks) plus the full systems/tests + research/autonomy/tests suites, not just the one row that was red.  ✅ FIXED 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s63-prereqscore, code on main at f9e19b4f3). ⛔ THE SIBLING FIX (a660303d1) ALONE DID NOT CLOSE IT — verified in a read-only clone at that commit with its own unmodified test: still red, only the failing PAIR moved. Rule 2 ASSIGNS entry['score'], so a row that is both blocked-with-evidence and a prerequisite lost rule 1's −90 while its score_inputs went on saying blocked_with_evidence: true. Five rows carrying their own recorded block sat at ranks 6,7,9,11,12; test_an_evidenced_block_drops_out_of_the_queue checks only the TOP THREE, so it watched this and stayed green. After the fix they sit at 92–96. ⭐ THE ASSERTION'S SIGN IS INTENDED, NOT A BUG: penalty is −90, so `parent - penalty/2` reads parent+45, the MIDPOINT between the parent's penalised and unpenalised score — a child that inherited the penalty lands at the bottom of that interval, one that inherited the value at the top. ⛔ What WAS wrong is the other side: it compared the parent's unpenalised value against the child's FINAL score, which includes any penalty the CHILD carries for a block OF ITS OWN, so it read a correct scorer as broken. It never fired that way before only because the penalty was being erased. ⭐ AND THE CHEAP FIRST QUESTION WAS A TRAP: clearing AUT-PROP-018's blocked_evidence under the OLD code went green by MINTING 90 points from a stale flag, taking that row to first place by 87 — a one-field edit would have closed the CI check and left the scorer broken. entries.what:
PROPOSAL, GROUNDED IN research/method-watch-autonomy-prior-art-2.md §4.3 (PUBMED 10.1016/j.jclinepi.2017.08.008, Simmonds et al. 2017, Living systematic reviews: 3). THE FINDING: repeated looks at accumulating evidence inflate type I error — 'the chance of incorrectly concluding that any updated meta-analysis is statistically significant when there is no effect increases rapidly as more updates are performed.' Four published fixes exist: the law of the iterated logarithm and the Shuster method (type I error only), and trial sequential analysis / sequential meta-analysis (type I AND II, with heterogeneity). SIMMONDS' OWN DECISION RULE IS THE PART TO STEAL: if the review only reports the CURRENT BEST PICTURE and readers know results may change, standard methods are fine; if the updated conclusion FEEDS A DECISION, the sequential correction is required.

WHY THIS BEARS ON THE AUTONOMY LOOP SPECIFICALLY (not just the manuscripts): this repository's research loop repeatedly RE-EXAMINES THE SAME CLAIMS as new evidence accumulates across cycles — a route's score is re-derived from `systems/graph` on every ledger `--write`, a blocker's status is re-checked cycle over cycle, and `research/method-watch.md` explicitly re-grades settled findings on a schedule as methods improve (CLAUDE.md §4: 'that licenses keeping the option open and re-grading it on a schedule; it never licenses claiming a result early'). That is structurally identical to a living systematic review's repeated-look problem, and §4.3's own framing is direct: 'nobody in the LLM wave has this.' Verified: no sequential-testing or repeated-look correction exists anywhere in this codebase (grepped for 'sequential test', 'type I error', 'iterated logarithm', 'Shuster' — no hits outside the survey document itself).

TASK: apply Simmonds' decision rule to distinguish the loop's two kinds of repeated evidence-reading — (a) a route STATUS or health-board reading that is reported as a current snapshot readers already know may change (no correction needed), versus (b) a re-examination whose updated verdict FEEDS A DECISION with consequences that don't get revisited on the next cycle — closing a route, clearing a `blocked_by` entry, satisfying a `publish_bar.py` clause, or admitting a manuscript claim strengthened by newly-accumulated evidence. For every instance of (b) found (start with `publish_bar.py`'s clauses and any route-closure logic in the ledger/graph pipeline), document or implement the sequential correction the repeated look requires, rather than treating every fresh re-check as an independent, uncorrected test.

⛔⛔ THE PUBLISH BAR THROWS AWAY A CLEAN REVIEW SIXTY TIMES TO TRACK FOUR REAL CHANGES, AND THAT IS WHY A NIGHT OF HARDENING CANNOT CONVERGE. Measured 2026-09-02 by CYC-0090-d7df5340.
★ THE MECHANISM IS ONE COMPARISON, MADE IN TWO CLAUSES: `clause_1_hardening_converged` and `clause_6_independent_adversarial_seat` both read `record['reviewed_commit'] != sha`. Any commit invalidates a clean round — including commits that touch nothing the review read, and including the commit that files the round's own record.
★★ THE NUMBER. Over the sixty commits before this filing, PUB-ASO's deliverable files (the article, its renderings and their build stamps — fifteen paths) took FOUR distinct digests, in eight runs. So the sha comparison discarded a review sixty times to track four real changes. The article's own sha256 was byte-identical (afd60b9e…) across the pins 7ae3cb518, 4ae4e9929 and e0834faf4; five blind seats had read exactly those bytes; clause 1 failed at all three. That night cost 46 gate runs and 8 greens against 118 inserted and 12 deleted manuscript lines.
⛔ AND THE SHA IS ALSO TOO LOOSE, WHICH IS WHY THE FIX IS A RE-ANCHORING RATHER THAN A RELAXATION. A sha says WHEN a review happened and never said WHAT it covered: a seat that read one file and a seat that read fifteen record the same string. A digest over the deliverable SET has both properties — it cannot stay equal when anything reviewed changed, and it cannot be produced without naming exactly what went into it.
★ THE INSTRUMENT IS ALREADY COMMITTED AND GATES NOTHING: research/autonomy/deliverable_digest.py derives the set from the publication's own `document.file` in systems/graph/publications.json plus the files whose names extend its stem, so nothing is hand-listed. `--paper PUB-ASO [--sha X]` prints the digest and its members.
⛔⛔ THE PATCH EXISTS, WAS RUN AGAINST THE LIVE RECORDS, AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT LANDED. publish_bar.py is a GOVERNED path and CYC-0090-d7df5340's session goal is to get PUB-ASO to 7/7 — so this cycle is blocked by the very clause the change relaxes, which is the exact shape amendment_guard exists to refuse (architecture §10.4: 'a later cycle may make the identical change, declared; what is refused is making it under pressure, with the obstacle still in front of you'). The receipt's `blocked_by` records the blockage rather than being left empty to slip the change through, which would be a false record and has the same status here as a fabricated receipt.
★ WHAT A LATER CYCLE HAS TO DO, so it need not re-derive any of this: (1) add `_deliverable_at(sha)` and `_covers(record, sha, digest)` to publish_bar — a record matches on its exact sha OR on a `deliverable_digest` it carries, and a record WITHOUT that field matches on the sha alone, so no legacy record is grandfathered in; (2) widen `_seat_records`'s glob from {pub}-{sha}*.json to {pub}-*.json filtered by `_covers`, which pools the pooled seats' FINDINGS as well as their count — that is what keeps it a strengthening; (3) make `_is_seat_file` match {pub}-<hex>-seat- by regex, since the sha in the name is now the record's own; (4) drop same-digest commits from `priors` in the widest-round check, because their seats are already counted in the numerator; (5) leave CLAUSE 2 BOUND TO THE SHA — it is the only clause that speaks for the whole tree, and an artifact drifting under a still-valid digest is caught there and in the manuscripts suite, not here; (6) have the seat and hardening writers stamp `deliverable_digest`. The diff is 271 lines and applies cleanly to e0834faf4.
⚠ IT FAILS CLOSED THROUGHOUT: an unreadable publication row, a deliverable missing at the commit, or a git failure yields no digest; no digest matches nothing; and every record then falls back to the exact sha comparison in place today.

entries.what: ✅ FIXED 2026-08-27, FOUND BY USING THE TOOL RATHER THAN BY TESTING IT. ⛔⛔ `claim.py`'s RETRY LOOP COULD NOT CONVERGE, AND IT REPORTED A COMFORTING HYPOTHESIS INSTEAD OF THE REASON. A push is rejected when the remote has moved; in this repository the CI ticks push several times an hour, so that is the ORDINARY case and not contention. The loop re-fetched and re-decided on every attempt — but `git fetch` updates the remote-tracking ref and changes NOTHING about HEAD, so HEAD stayed behind and all three attempts were rejected for the identical reason as the first. It then printed 'the remote is moving faster than this can commit; that is not contention on this row and retrying will not fix it' — which sounds like a diagnosis and is a rationalisation for a loop that structurally could not succeed. ⚠ MEASURED: three consecutive claims returned RETRY; `git log HEAD..origin/main` showed exactly ONE CI commit ahead. The remote had moved once, not fast. ⭐ FIXED: `Git.integrate()` merges origin/main after a rejected push, before the next attempt, so the compare-and-swap actually converges. ⛔ AND A CONFLICTING MERGE IS NOT AUTO-RESOLVED: the ledger is the file two sessions collide on, and a claim is not worth risking a wrong automatic resolution — it aborts the merge and reports RETRY with what to do. The exhausted-retry message now states that integration WAS tried, so the next reader cannot repeat this diagnosis. ✅ 2 new tests, 108 in the suite. ⭐⭐ THE PATTERN IS NOW THREE FOR THREE AND WORTH MORE THAN ANY OF THE INSTANCES: every defect in this tool — the local-branch refspec (AUT-PD-029, found by another session), the unreachable `os.path.exists` guard, and this — was invisible to a suite driving a `FakeGit`, and every one surfaced the first time the tool met a real remote that had moved.
