⛔⛔ A REBASE-THEN-PUSH LANDS A TREE NO GATE EVER SAW, AND IT PUT A DUPLICATE ID ON `main` THAT CRASHED EVERY CYCLE'S STEP 3. Measured 2026-08-28. Two sessions filed AUT-PD-140 four minutes apart: CYC-0070-c84c64dd at e901ae619, then CYC-0070-225452b4 at 170314393 — and `git rev-parse 170314393^` IS e901ae619, so these were NOT divergent branches meeting at a merge. The second session allocated its id from state fetched before e901ae619, REBASED onto it, and pushed; the ledger's rows are separate array elements, so the rebase produced no conflict and no marker. ⛔ THE COST WAS TOTAL: `priority.py:merge` REFUSES a duplicated ledger (`ValueError: duplicate ledger ids: AUT-PD-140`), so `python3 research/autonomy/priority.py --write` — step 3 of the cycle contract, run before any item is taken — crashed on committed `main` for every session until it was renamed.
⭐ THE GUARD WAS CORRECT AND WAS SIMPLY NOT RUN AT THE MOMENT THAT MATTERED. Verified by stashing the fix and running the committed trunk: `research/autonomy/tests/test_ids_cannot_collide.py::test_the_committed_ledger_has_no_duplicate_ids` FAILS (1 failed, 10 passed), and it is inside preflight gate 13's scope — so a preflight run AFTER the rebase would have caught it before the push. ⛔ SO THIS IS NOT A MISSING GATE. IT IS A GAP IN WHAT 'THE TREE YOU COMMIT' MEANS. CLAUDE.md §6 requires that the run you report green is the run that saw the tree you commit; a rebase performed at push time creates a THIRD tree — neither session's gated one — and nothing re-gates it. Every id here derives from max+1 over committed state (AUT-PROP-013), so a rebase is precisely when a collision becomes possible and precisely when nothing looks.
⚠ AND THE DUPLICATED-EFFORT HALF REPEATED WHILE THIS WAS BEING WRITTEN, WHICH IS EVIDENCE THE FIX MUST BE MECHANICAL RATHER THAN A RULE. ⛔⛔ EVERY SPAWNED SEAT CREATES A ~586 MB GIT WORKTREE AND NOTHING HAS EVER REMOVED ONE. Measured 2026-09-02: 36 dead worktrees held ~21 GB, the session's writable allowance hit 100% with 33 MB free, and `./scripts/preflight.sh` exited 1 having written a ZERO-BYTE log.
★ THE FAILURE MODE IS THE POINT, NOT THE DISK. An out-of-space gate does not say it is out of space. It exits non-zero with no output, which reads exactly like a broken gate or a broken repository, and the correct first move -- read the whole log and batch the fixes (CLAUDE.md §6) -- returns NOTHING to work with. The discriminating observation was `df -h`, and nothing in the commit loop, the skills or the hooks points at it.
⚠ AND THE ENVIRONMENT'S OWN NOTE SAYS `df` MISLEADS HERE: 'Avail at 0 with low Used means the allowance is spent, not that the machine is broken' -- 38 G used of 252 G, reported as 100%. So even the right command needs the right reading.
★ THE ARITHMETIC IS UNFORGIVING AND IT IS NOT A ONE-OFF. A worktree is a full checkout of this repository. The session-shape rule in `research-loop` §3 prescribes parallel subagents as the NORMAL shape, and CLAUDE.md §1 sets `subagent_width` at 64. Sixty-four seats at 586 MB is 37 GB of working copies for a repository whose `.git` is 1.7 GB. **The governed width and the disk allowance have never been reconciled, and the width is the number the architecture already records as having failed catastrophically once.**
⛔ NOTHING WAS LOST THIS TIME AND THAT WAS LUCK. All 36 removed worktrees were clean with nothing unpushed -- checked before deleting, one at a time. A seat that had died holding uncommitted work would have had it deleted by the cleanup that freed the disk, and the session doing the cleanup is under pressure precisely because it cannot write.
entries.next_action: Make worktree lifetime someone's job. Options to argue rather than assume: have the seat prompt template end with `git worktree remove`, which fails the moment a seat dies; a reaper that removes worktrees whose branch is merged and whose tree is clean, modelled on `session_reaper.py` and sharing its refusal to clear anything holding uncommitted work; or stop giving read-only seats a worktree at all -- the five blind seats in this same round read the pinned commit with `git show` and used ZERO disk, which is the cheapest fix and covers the largest population. ⛔ Whatever is chosen must ALSO make an out-of-space gate say so: a preflight that exits 1 with an empty log is the actual cost here, and a two-line disk check at the top of `preflight.sh` is cheaper than any of the above. ⚠ Mind `scripts/tier-budgets.json` before adding a test; a disk precondition is not a test.

entries.what:
⛔⛔ THE TURN-END HOOK TELLS A SPAWNING SESSION TO CLAIM THE ITEM FOR ITS SUCCESSOR, AND DOING SO WOULD MAKE THE SUCCESSOR YIELD ITS OWN TOP ITEM. Measured 2026-08-29 (CYC-0083-381d0696) at the handoff itself. `ready-work-at-turn-end.sh` option 1 says to set `owner` and `claimed_utc` on the row the dispatched worker will run, at dispatch. `claim.py:decide()` answers `YIELDED` for any row whose `owner` is set and is not the caller's own `me`. A spawned successor calls `claim.py` with a cycle id built from ITS OWN harness session uuid, which does not exist when the parent spawns it — so no owner string the parent can write will ever match, and a pre-claimed top row is one the successor is guaranteed to hand back.

⭐ THE HOOK IS NOT WRONG, IT IS SCOPED TO A DIFFERENT WORKER. For a SUBAGENT the driver holds the lease and the subagent never calls `claim.py`, so claiming at dispatch is exactly right and the hook's own evidence (two dispatched agents unclaimed, 2026-08-27) is real. For a SPAWNED SESSION running the full twelve-step contract, step 3 re-scores and step 4 claims — the successor's prompt says in terms that the queue it was handed 'is a pointer, not a plan' — so a parent claim both breaks the mechanism and asserts something not yet true: the successor may legitimately take a different row.

⚠ THE COST TODAY IS NOISE, NOT LOST WORK, AND THAT IS PRECISELY THE DANGER THE HOOK'S OWN TEXT NAMES: 'a guard that cries wolf is a guard that gets tuned out — which is how this repository has already lost the value of several.' Every handoff ends with a correct spawn and a hook saying the work is not moving. No cycle has followed the instruction yet, which is the only reason it has cost nothing.

⛔ THE FIX IS A CHOICE. (a) Teach the hook the difference: a row is 'moving' if a session spawned in this turn was created to run it — but the hook cannot see session ids, so this needs the handoff to leave a mark it CAN see. (b) Give the row a `dispatched_to` field, distinct from `owner`, that the hook reads and `decide()` ignores — a claim is a lease held by a worker, and 'a successor has been spawned pointed at this' is a different fact that currently has no home. (c) Have `decide()` treat a `session_*` owner as claimable by any cycle whose session matches — ⛔ REJECTED ON READING: it widens the one predicate the whole mutual-exclusion argument rests on, for a convenience, and AUT-PROP-030's analysis is explicit that safety is enforced at the resource.
⭐ (b) IS THE SHAPE THAT ADDS A FACT RATHER THAN OVERLOADING ONE. Whoever takes this should check first whether `continuity.ready()` and `priority.release_stale_claims` also need to read it, because a `dispatched_to` that nothing ages out is the immortal-claim defect (CYC-0003) with a new field name.

⛔ `amendment_guard.py`'s `changed_paths()` runs `git diff --name-only <sha> --`, and `git diff` NEVER lists untracked files, staged or not -- so a brand-new file under a GOVERNED glob (a new `**/tests/**` file, a new file that happened to be named `CLAUDE.md`, etc.) is invisible to the anti-gaming guard until it has been `git add`-ed at least once. Measured 2026-08-29 (CYC-0074): three new files this session (research/autonomy/prepush_ledger_guard.py, .githooks/pre-push, research/autonomy/tests/test_prepush_ledger_guard_catches_duplicate_ids.py) were completely absent from `python3 research/autonomy/amendment_guard.py --receipt ... --diff-from 76702fbfa` even though one of them matches `**/tests/**` -- confirmed directly: `git diff --name-only 76702fbfa --` omits all three; `git add`-ing them first makes them appear. entries.what:
THREE ROUTES RECORDED `closed` STILL CARRY A REOPENING TRIGGER: RT-SYNPROMOTER and RT-RXR carry TECH-* revisit_triggers, RT-6MP a TR-* revival_trigger, while systems/CONVENTIONS.md §4.1 defines `closed` as conclusively unworkable and carrying no TECH-*. By the convention's own words these are `parked`, not `closed`. ⚠ The distinction is not cosmetic on a rising frontier (CLAUDE.md §5): `parked` means revisit when capability X lands and is re-graded on a schedule; `closed` means never look again. Recording a revivable route as closed is how a live option gets lost quietly.

★ RESOLVED 2026-09-02 by s38-closed-vs-parked. THE SWEEP WAS A CENSUS, NOT A SPOT-CHECK: all 77 routes tested in both directions. §4.1's literal test (`closed` carrying a `TECH-*`) has EXACTLY TWO hits -- RT-SYNPROMOTER and RT-RXR. The other direction (`parked` carrying no `TECH-*`) has ZERO. RT-6MP carries a `TR-*` and no `TECH-*`, so it passes §4.1's letter and fails its sense.
⭐ THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE IS NOT §4.1's PROSE -- IT IS THE ENFORCED CLOSURE MODEL. All three routes are `closure_kind: premise_false`, which `research/manuscripts/emc-systems-map.json._closure_model` declares `permanent: false, needs_trigger: true` ('a stated premise was measured and is not true. Revivable only if the measurement or the underlying fact changes'). The map and the graph therefore DISAGREED, and the map is the half with a checker. So the STATE field was wrong in all three; the triggers are not stale, they are required by the model that governs them.
⭐ INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION FROM A FIELD NOT TOUCHED: `state.work_state`. research-object.schema.json says '`dead` requires positive evidence of impossibility; a method that merely failed is `parked`'. The three routes that ARE correctly closed (RT-EWSR1-PROTEIN, RT-FET-LC-LIGAND, RT-DBD -- definitional / arithmetic_over_fixed_fact) are all `work_state: dead`. RT-SYNPROMOTER is `future`; RT-RXR and RT-6MP are `complete`. NONE of the three moved is `dead`. The graph already said they were not dead.
CHANGED: `state.status` closed -> parked on RT-SYNPROMOTER, RT-RXR, RT-6MP; and `timing.recommendation` closed -> monitor on RT-RXR and RT-6MP, because a `closed` timing recommendation asserts the route 'must appear on no watch list' (RT-EWSR1-PROTEIN's own words) which contradicts `parked`. RANKING-NEUTRAL: `priority.py` reads `recommendation` only as `== 'pursue_now'`, so `closed` and `monitor` score identically. VERIFIED BY FIELD-BY-FIELD DIFF over all 77 routes: 5 field changes, 0 touching `grade`/`readiness`/`blockers_inherited`, 3 routes touched.
★ WHAT THE CHANGE ACTUALLY BUYS: `priority.py::_kind` returns `regrade` for a route that is `parked` AND carries a `revival_trigger`, and returns it for no `closed` route -- so these three now enter the re-test schedule (emc-autonomy-architecture.md §8.2). It does NOT queue them as work: `parked` and `closed` are both in `NOT_TAKEABLE_STATUSES`, and `is_live` reads `work_state`+`closure_kind`, not `status`, so it is unchanged.
⛔ LIVE READINGS TAKEN 2026-09-02 (rung 0 WebSearch, per ci-escape-hatches §0) RATHER THAN REMEMBERED -- NO TRIGGER HAS FIRED, so no route is live that was not live before:
 (a) RT-RXR / TECH-RXR-HETERODIMER-REPORT: NOT LANDED. The 2026 eLife paper 'Towards a unified molecular mechanism for ligand-dependent activation of NR4A-RXR heterodimers' works on Nurr1-RXRalpha (NR4A2) and Nur77-RXRgamma (NR4A1); it does not report NR4A3/NOR-1 heterodimerising with RXR. The published negative -- NOR-1 unable to form RXR heterodimers, which is what distinguishes it from NGFI-B and Nurr1 -- stands. `current_state: absent` is now CONFIRMED rather than assumed. ⚠ But the field is actively working this axis and the paper's own stated aim is to test whether the mechanism is shared ACROSS NR4A-RXR heterodimers, which makes the trigger more watch-worthy, not less -- the argument for `parked` over `closed`. ⚠ The TECH carries 4 UNGRADED scan signals; none is a heterodimer report (checked).
 (b) RT-6MP / TR-NR4A3-DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: NOT LANDED. No report links 6-MP to the direction of effect on the EWSR1::NR4A3 fusion. The gain-of-function prior the closure rests on is corroborated (the fusion is a potent transcriptional activator), but that is the PRIOR, not the demonstration the trigger names.
 (c) RT-SYNPROMOTER / TECH-VECTOR-DELIVERY: NOT LANDED -- the vector-delivery literature is still hepatic and ex vivo; no solid-tumour platform at the coverage this route assumes. `current_state: absent` confirmed. TECH-EMC-EXPRESSION-DATA: still `early_signals`; a 2026 16-case EMC molecular study exists but whether it deposited data publicly is UNKNOWN and is left to the scan's human grader -- systems_check [X4] states the scan deliberately cannot change `current_state` itself.
★ GUARD ADDED so this cannot regress silently: `systems_check.check_closed_carries_no_reopening_trigger` emits ERROR `[T8]` when a `closed` route names ANY reopening condition, `TECH-*` or `TR-*`. It is STRICTER than §4.1 (which names only `TECH-*`, because it predates the `TR-*` registry minted 2026-08-06) and so cannot contradict it. MUTATION-TESTED 4/4: reverting each of the three routes to `closed` fires [T8] naming that route (RT-6MP on the `TR-*` alone, which is the half §4.1's wording would have missed); RT-DBD reverted to `closed` correctly does NOT fire. routes.json restored byte-identical (sha256 273fa9d3e450ae79aea219b11843f20a49dd50db1fdc6637583c7ceecd824393).
⚠ NO COMMITTED UNIT TEST FOR THE GUARD, AND THAT IS A BUDGET DECISION NOT AN OVERSIGHT: the guard lives in systems_check (cheapest tier, 0 test functions) but a pytest for it would land in `systems/tests`, which is in the `commit-loop` tier at 1393/1400 -- 7 functions of headroom. CLAUDE.md §6: raising a ceiling is the last of the three answers. A session with headroom should add one.
⛔ THREE FINDINGS RECORDED RATHER THAN ACTED ON (out of this row's scope):
 1. RT-DIAGNOSTIC-PATHWAY is `closed` with `closure_kind: premise_false` (non-permanent, needs_trigger) and NO trigger of any kind, and its `timing.recommendation` is still `pursue_now` -- stale, never updated when trimcrae closed it 2026-08-23 ('this is not a paper... drop it'). It carries no TECH-* so it does not violate §4.1 and was LEFT ALONE. Its closure is a scope decision, which no capability revives, so the likely defect is `closure_kind`, whose owner should rule. It is also the one graph-closed route ABSENT from emc-systems-map.json (40 routes vs the graph's 77), so its mismatch is unchecked from both directions.
 2. RT-6MP is now parked on a `TR-*` with NO `TECH-*` mirror, and TR-NR4A3-DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT has `on_watch_list: false` and no `scan_trigger` -- so NOTHING SCANS FOR IT. RT-RXR's equivalent published-measurement condition does have a TECH-* mirror with a scan trigger. A parked route whose trigger nothing watches is this row's own defect one layer down. Minting the technology needs a forecast, so it is a graph change for the registry's owner, not a check.
 3. CONVENTIONS.md §4.1 still names only `TECH-*`. The guard is stricter so nothing is misled, but the doc could be updated to name the `TR-*` register too. NOT done here deliberately: editing the convention in the same commit that enforces it is the shape `amendment_guard` refuses.

entries.what: ⛔⛔ REGENERATING THE ARCHIVE MANIFEST AT A LOCAL COMMIT PUBLISHES A `git_revision` THAT DIES IN THE REBASE THAT PUSHES IT. AUT-PD-168 established the ordering rule — commit the work first, then regenerate against a clean tree — and following it exactly is still not sufficient, because 'clean' and 'published' are different properties and only the first is checked. Measured 2026-08-29: a manifest generated at local HEAD, then rebased onto a moved origin/main, reached the trunk naming a commit no clone can resolve. ⭐ THE MISSING HALF OF THE RULE, IN ONE LINE: regenerate with HEAD at a PUSHED commit — fetch, rebase, THEN regenerate, commit and push — because origin's history is never rewritten and a recorded tip therefore survives as an ancestor of whatever comes next. ⚠ AND IF THE PUSH RACES, the rebase that resolves it must be followed by another regeneration, not just a retry. ⛔ THE HONEST COST HERE WAS SMALL — one preflight and one extra commit — but the artifact is the ASO deposit's provenance record and its whole purpose is that a reader can check out `git_revision` and verify the hashes. A manifest naming an unresolvable commit fails at precisely the moment it is supposed to work. ⭐ WHERE TO PUT IT: `aso_archive_manifest.py`'s own header, beside the ordering rule it already carries, and in the `--check-archive` refusal message that already teaches the ordering — a reader who hits one of these needs both halves.

entries.what:
⛔ TWO SESSIONS BOTH REGENERATE THE ASO ARCHIVE MANIFEST AND COLLIDE ON EVERY PUSH — THREE TIMES IN TEN MINUTES on 2026-08-27. Each merge brings in a manifest stamped against the OTHER session's tree; AUT-PD-016's guard then correctly REFUSES one whose `git_tree_is_clean_apart_from_this_manifest` is false; and the resolution is always identical — never hand-merge a generated file, regenerate it on the settled tree. ⭐ THAT RESOLUTION IS RIGHT AND IT DOES NOT CONVERGE WHILE TWO WRITERS KEEP PRODUCING IT: every regeneration is itself a commit, which is another push another session must merge, which restamps the flag. ⚠ THE GUARD IS NOT THE PROBLEM AND MUST NOT BE LOOSENED — it caught a real instance today, a manifest whose hash list was taken while tracked files were uncommitted and so may describe a file that is not what got committed. ⭐ THE CANDIDATE FIX IS ONE WRITER: have CI regenerate the manifest on the trunk after a push, the way the submission parts are already rebuilt on a runner, so no interactive session ever needs to. Check what `.github/workflows/aso-submission-parts.yml` already does before building anything — half of this may exist.

⚠ ATTEMPTED 2026-08-27 AND BACKED OUT. TWO CANDIDATE FIXES ARE NOW DEAD ENDS WITH EVIDENCE, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX I DID NOT GET. ⛔ (1) A GIT MERGE DRIVER MAKES IT WORSE, MEASURED NOT REASONED. I built it — `.gitattributes` mapping the manifest to `merge=derived-artifact`, a driver of `true` (keep ours; both sides are equally stale and the file's own `_derived_never_typed` key means no human value can be lost), registered by `dev-setup.sh` because git will not read driver definitions from a repository. It WORKED: a simulated two-sided conflict merged with zero markers. ⛔ THEN THE CONTROL KILLED IT — with `.gitattributes` present and the config absent, git says **`fatal: custom merge driver derived-artifact lacks command line`** and the merge FAILS HARD. A repository cannot ship local git config (a driver is an arbitrary command; that is a deliberate git security property), so any clone, any CI job and any worktree where dev-setup has not run gets a FATAL error instead of a recoverable conflict. Strictly worse than the problem. Reverted. ⛔ (2) 'STOP STAMPING git_revision ON EVERY REGENERATION' CUTS ALMOST NOTHING. Measured over the same 12 hours: of 22 manifest commits, only **6 changed just the repository-state lines** and **16 changed real inventory or hashes**. The churn is not stamping noise. ⭐⭐ SO THE MEASUREMENT REFRAMES THE ITEM: this is not a manifest problem, it is a CONCURRENCY problem wearing a manifest's clothes. Sixteen genuine content changes to the ASO archive in twelve hours came from several sessions writing the same subtree, and gate 11 correctly forces each of them to regenerate. The manifest is the place the collision becomes VISIBLE, not the place it is caused — which puts it in AUT-PD-021's family (a claim protects the claimant, not against a session that fetched before the claim landed), not in its own. ⚠ Whoever takes this next should read it as 'reduce concurrent writers on one subtree, or make the regeneration a step the trunk owns rather than each session', and should NOT re-try either dead end above. ⚠ AND ONE INCIDENTAL DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED WHILE FAILING AT THIS: the merge-driver registration was first written BELOW `dev-setup.sh`'s `--if-needed` early exit, so the hook that runs it would never have reached it — the file's own comment three lines above describes exactly that failure happening to the ghostscript step. I reproduced it verbatim while reading the warning about it. The probe-extension pattern is the lesson: any step added to dev-setup must extend the `--if-needed` probe IN THE SAME COMMIT, because a step the probe cannot see does not exist. That fix went out with the revert since the step it guarded is gone, and is recorded here instead.

entries._resolution:
FIXED, AND NOT BY THE ONE SENTENCE THE ROW PROPOSED. The row's remedy — a sentence in step 10 — would have been the FOURTH prose agreement of this exact shape (AUT-PD-013's fan-out key, AUT-PROP-013's ids, AUT-PD-037's serialization, this), and receipt_schema.py's own docstring already records that prose could not hold a convention this loop had got right twice. So the sentence landed AND the agreement is now measured.
MECHANISM: research/autonomy/contract_check.py, run by preflight as GATE 17. Direction A DERIVES what receipt_schema.py requires — it deletes each field in turn from receipts problems() accepts and re-runs the enforcer, so a deletion that produces a complaint proves that field is required; nothing is asserted about the enforcer's internals and no list is kept. Direction B additionally requires the contract to name every module-level `*_KEY`, as a backstop for a requirement conditioned on something no fixture exercises; that enumeration is complete only because no_literal_key_lookups() now refuses a receipt field name spelled as a string literal off a function's own argument. ⭐ THE FAIL-CLOSED HALF IS THE FIXTURES: a new requirement in receipt_schema.py makes them non-compliant, so the build reds on the commit that ADDS the requirement rather than on the cycle that later trips over it.
REPRODUCED BEFORE FIXING: contract_check --check on the unmodified trunk exited 1 naming `ccr_session_id` (s2-contract-check-before.log); after the step-10 edit it exits 0 (s2-contract-check-after.log).
VERIFIED, NOT INHERITED: the dispatch note's claim that `get_session` with NO arguments returns the CCR id was re-checked live on 2026-08-29 — it returns `.ccr.id` = a `session_01…` value, while CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in the same container is a bare UUID. Two id spaces, confirmed, so collapsing them stays the wrong fix.
SECOND GAP FOUND AND CLOSED IN PASSING: `cycle_id` was read as a string literal in two places in receipt_schema.py and named nowhere in step 10. It is now CYCLE_ID_KEY (behaviour-preserving — problems() still falls back to the filename, so it is NOT in the derived required set) and step 10 names it. It is the one field where directions A and B diverge, and a test pins that.
MUTATION-TESTED ON A COPY of research/autonomy plus the skill (never the live tree): 16 single-site mutations, 15 caught. ⛔ SURVIVOR REPORTED RATHER THAN FOOTNOTED: M5a — dropping ONE of the two CCR-governed fixtures — survives, and on inspection it is an equivalent mutant: the other CCR fixture still exercises that branch, every derived requirement is unchanged and the coverage invariant still holds, so no verdict moves. Two mutants that DID survive the first pass were real and are now caught: dropping every CCR-governed fixture, and dropping the only fixture with a non-zero fan-out, both left all 22 tests green because no requirement hangs off those branches TODAY while silently removing the coverage that would catch the NEXT one; test_the_fixtures_span_every_condition_the_enforcer_branches_on now asserts both sides of both branches.
⛔ ORDINAL COLLISION CAUGHT BEFORE THE COMMIT, NOT AFTER: the gate was first placed beside gate 12, where it belongs by subject. preflight.sh's gate headings are numbered BY POSITION, and ids.py and priority.py both say 'preflight gate 15' in prose about research/autonomy/tests, so that placement would have silently renumbered four gates and falsified those references — the same doc/code drift this item is about. It is APPENDED LAST instead, for the reason gate 16's own note already gives, and .claude/skills/repo-gates/SKILL.md now lists it as (17).
⛔ WHAT IS NOT COVERED, AND IT IS NOT SMALL: this checks the ONE enforcer that fails the commit. health.py (`handoff.child_session_id`, `session_id`, `route_advanced`), session_cap.py and holder_liveness.py (`ccr_session_id`) all read receipt fields too; all are named in the contract today and none is checked here, because a reader that only GRADES a receipt produces a wrong number rather than a red build. Extending contract_check to them is a separate item, not something to absorb silently into this one. And the checker can prove the contract NAMES a field; it cannot prove what the contract SAYS about it is true — only the two identifying tokens of the get_session instruction are pinned.
⚠ CORRECTION APPENDIX (rule 1.2 — recorded, not silently rewritten). The first draft of this fix said in four places that a cycle following the contract 'wrote a receipt the gate refused and learned the requirement from a red build', and that a single cycle complied. MEASURED and false: all SEVEN receipts at or after CYC-0070 carry `ccr_session_id`, so no build has gone red over this gap and more than one cycle complied. The true and weaker statement — the one now in contract_check.py, receipt_schema.py, the new suite and step 10 — is that the gap removed the GUARANTEE rather than any build: CYC-0073-d4ccfde4 recorded that it wrote the field only because it had opened receipt_schema.py for an unrelated reason. ⛔ The two amendments.jsonl records committed in f177cc092 still carry the overstated clause in their `why`. That log is APPEND-ONLY by design — amendment_guard's check_log treats a rewritten history as the tell that the guard was worked around — so the record stands and the correction lives here instead.

entries.evidence:
✅ SWEPT 2026-09-02 (seat s39-transcript-vs-protein). ⭐ THE ANSWER IS ZERO FURTHER INSTANCES, AND THE DENOMINATOR IS THE RESULT. Population: all 77 routes, 720 records across the 18 files of systems/graph, 16,481 sentences. ⛔ THE ARTIFACT SET WAS THE PART THAT WAS NEARLY WRONG: the graph registers only SIX expression series as ART-* ids, and a `git ls-tree` pass over research/modalities found EIGHTEEN — the twelve unregistered ones include emc-kinase-lane-panel-read.json (PRKDC and SGK1, i.e. this very defect's own lane), emc-fourth-cohort-quant.json (raw reads per gene), the three GTEx normal-tissue reads, and the hypoxia confound audit. A sweep scoped to the registered ids reaches 27 routes; the full set reaches 37, so scoping to the graph's own registry would have left 10 routes unexamined.
★ THREE INDEPENDENT DISCRIMINATORS, RUN OVER THE SAME POPULATION. (1) CITATION-SCOPED: 45 graph records cite one of the 18 artifacts (37 routes, 7 artifact records, 1 modality); 289 sentences in them name a property an expression series cannot measure (activity, phosphorylation, signalling, protein, IHC, copy number, deletion, dependency, hypoxic state, isoform, surface density). All 289 read and cleared. (2) BARE-ASSERTION filter over those 289 — drop every sentence carrying a negation, hedge or attribution — leaves 102, all of them route titles, strategy ids, questions, required_validation items naming what is MISSING, or DepMap CRISPR dependency figures whose instrument genuinely does measure dependency. (3) NUMERIC FINGERPRINT, independent of the citation graph: sentences carrying BOTH an expression figure (percentile, SD units, t=, GSE/GPL accession) AND a non-expression property — 5 of 16,481, and all five are the DISCLAIMERS themselves.
⛔ THE ONE KNOWN INSTANCE WAS ALREADY FIXED AND IS NOT REOPENED — by AUT-PD-099, commit 61231a22c, 2026-08-29 ('retract RT-SGK1's activity-shaped clause; correct the census reason'), verified here with `git log -S` rather than recalled. RT-SGK1's grade carries '⚠ Superseded, retained (corrected 2026-08-29)' over the original 'which is an activity-shaped reading rather than an abundance one', now reading 'that number is NDRG1 TRANSCRIPT ABUNDANCE, which is not a readout of SGK1 activity'. NO route grade, state, readiness or blockers_inherited was touched by this seat; no file under systems/ was modified at all.
★ WHY THE NEGATIVE IS CREDIBLE RATHER THAN MERELY UNPRODUCTIVE — THE SWEEP WAS MUTATION-TESTED. Five synthetic defects of this exact class were injected into a SCRATCH COPY of systems/graph (never the live tree, CLAUDE.md §6): M1 restored RT-SGK1's pre-correction sentence verbatim; M2 'ASS1 protein is present in EMC at the 92nd percentile'; M3 'the CDK7 module is higher on both platforms, so EMC is CDK7-dependent'; M4 'SSTR2 receptor density on the EMC cell surface is sufficient for a theranostic'; M5 'HSP90 chaperone activity is elevated and the fusion is its client'. Discriminator (1) caught 5/5; (3) caught 4/5, its miss being M3, which carries no figure and is by construction (1)'s job. ⚠ THE FIRST RUN CAUGHT ONLY 4/5 AND 3/5 — M2 escaped both because the vocabulary had 'protein level' and 'at the protein' but not bare 'protein'. The vocabulary was widened and both were re-run against the clean tree; the verdict did not move.
⭐ AND THE MECHANISM THAT KEPT THE GRAPH CLEAN IS WORTH RECORDING, BECAUSE IT IS WHAT A FUTURE SWEEP SHOULD CHECK FIRST: every one of the 18 expression artifacts carries an explicit limits statement — 18/18, measured, no exceptions — but there is NO CONVENTION FOR WHERE IT LIVES: the statement surfaces under 57 distinct top-level keys across the 18 files (`_what_this_cannot_conclude` + `_limits`, per-read `what_it_cannot_settle`, per-route `what_this_does_not_settle`, `_ceilings`, `_language_discipline`, `_framing`, `_what_this_is_not`, `platform_gate` + `value_kind`, `_absent_reading_warning` and `_discipline` among them, and several are ordinary data keys like `verdict`, `method`, `panels` and `ratio_calibration` that happen to carry the caveat inline). census-route-expression-grading.json gives all 16 of its route verdicts one, and the consuming route records restate the limit in the same breath as the number: RT-SSTR2 'says nothing about receptor density, protein or imaging avidity'; RT-B7H3 'SELECTIVITY is a protein and tumour-versus-normal axis'; RT-FAP-RLT 'reaches no protein, IHC or imaging value'; RT-MTAP-PRMT5 'A TRANSCRIPT IS NOT A COPY NUMBER'; RT-APOPTOSIS-DEP 'the axis abundance cannot measure'; RT-HYPOXIA-PRODRUG withdrew a SUPPORTED grade for precisely this error. RT-RET catches the defect in the PUBLISHED literature (PMID 28423517 rendering transcript abundance as 'expression and activation').
⛔ A LEXICAL GUARD FOR THIS CLASS IS NOT FEASIBLE, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO RATHER THAN AN OPINION. Discriminator (1) has 100% power on the mutants and a 100% FALSE-POSITIVE RATE on the trunk — 289 fires, 0 defects. Discriminator (3) is far sharper (5 fires) and is WORSE as a gate, because all five fires are the correct disclaimers: the only way to make it green is to DELETE the caveat. ★ THE ROOT CAUSE IS THAT THE DISCRIMINATING FEATURE IS NOT LEXICAL. RT-SGK1 before and after its correction share every token class — instrument noun, figure, activity noun — and differ only in the POLARITY of the relation asserted between them ('is not a readout of' vs 'is an activity-shaped reading'). That is the strength-vs-DIRECTION orthogonality CLAUDE.md §6 already records from the `git add -A` incident ('an inverted sentence is still a sentence'); a pattern cannot read polarity across a clause boundary, and 'names activity' is a judgement.
★ WHAT IS FEASIBLE IS STRUCTURAL AND IT IS NOT FILED AS FREE: assert that every expression-series artifact carries a non-empty limits field and that each of its reads does too — deterministic, no judgement, no false positives. ⚠ BUT IT WOULD BE GREEN ON DAY ONE (18/18 already comply), which is CLAUDE.md §6's own definition of a guard whose incident cannot currently recur, and the 57 distinct key names mean the check must either accept an alias list or force a rename across 18 committed artifacts. Cost if taken: ~3 test functions. ⛔ AND THE BUDGET IS TIGHTER THAN THE BUDGET FILE'S OWN PROSE SAYS — `scripts/tier-budgets.json` reads 'At 1,277 functions on 2026-09-02' for commit-loop and 7,134 for modalities, while `tier_budget.py --check` measured 1,393/1,400 and 7,189/7,500 on that same day, i.e. SEVEN functions of headroom in commit-loop rather than 123. ⚠ THAT IS A TYPED TOTAL DRIFTING FROM ITS DERIVED ONE (CLAUDE.md §1: a total is DERIVED, never typed) — recorded here rather than fixed, because the count moves with every seat that lands a test and the right repair is to stop typing it in the `why` prose, which is a change to that file's contract and not this row's business. A 3-function guard would fit commit-loop at 1,396/1,400; modalities and paper-guards (887/1,000) have real room. NOT BUILT BY THIS SEAT — filed as a decision with its cost, per §6's rule that the question is where a guard belongs and whether it earns its place, not whether it is good.

A field name agreed in PROSE between a writer and a reader is not agreed at all: it is a hope, checked by nothing, and `subagents.max_concurrent` proves prose cannot even HOLD a convention the loop had already got right twice (three schemas in seventeen receipts). ⭐ THE SWEEP: enumerate every key one file writes and another reads — `handoff.child_session_id` (read by `cycles_are_sized`, spelled verbatim in the handoff prompt precisely because somebody already noticed this exposure), `route_advanced`, `blocked_by[].path`, the five `RECEIPT_TIME_KEYS`, the ledger's `closes_clause`/`requires_trimcrae`/`owner`, and `autonomy-state.json`'s dials — and for each ask the ONE question: what happens if the writer spells it differently? ⛔ THE ANSWER THAT MATTERS IS NOT 'the check fails' but 'the check goes UNMEASURED or, worse, GREEN', because a reader that cannot find a key reports absence, and this repository grades absence as restraint in at least one place already. ⭐ THE FIX SHAPE IS SETTLED by AUT-PD-013 and should be copied rather than re-derived: one module owns the name, both sides import it, a preflight gate checks the writer at the commit, and history is grandfathered by a number so the gate cannot latch. ⚠ CHEAP AND FREE — it is a grep, a reading and a test file; no compute, no network, nobody's permission.

DONE 2026-08-27: Surveyed every candidate the item named. FIXED (2, both landed, both mutation-tested against real receipts): (1) `route_advanced` -- no shared constant existed anywhere; health.py hardcoded the literal string in `c_advancing_live_work`, and receipts are hand-authored per receipt_schema.py's own docstring, so the only agreement was prose in the research-loop skill. Added `receipt_schema.ROUTE_ADVANCED_KEY` + `route_advanced_of()`, wired the same `--check` gate (already in preflight's default fast tier) to fail a governed receipt missing it, and made health.py import the constant instead of spelling it. (2) `handoff.child_session_id` -- handoff.py already named `CHILD_ID_FIELD` for the human-facing prompt, but health.py's `c_cycles_are_sized` re-derived the same two-level dict lookup inline rather than importing anything, so the NAME and the TRAVERSAL were both duplicated. Added `handoff.child_session_id_of()` as the one reader; health.py now calls it. Both fixes proven live: copied the real receipts dir to scratch, renamed the field in a real committed receipt, watched `receipt_schema.py --check` and `health.py`'s reader both flip from green/SIZED to red/unmeasured on the mutation, confirmed the un-mutated copy stays green, discarded the copy. New tests: research/autonomy/tests/test_handoff_child_id_shared_reader.py (6 tests) + 6 new tests appended to test_receipt_schema.py, all passing (89 + 6 = ok, full research/autonomy/tests + systems/tests/test_autonomy_health.py suite: 180 passed, 0 regressions). ALREADY SAFE, NO ACTION: `blocked_by[].path` (amendment_guard.py's `blocked_by_paths()` already raises RuntimeError on a blockage entry with no readable `path` -- fails loud, category (a), not (b)/(c)); the five `RECEIPT_TIME_KEYS` (health.py already accepts multiple synonyms in one file with no independent writer module, and a receipt matching none of them reads as RECEIPT-TIME-UNREADABLE, never green); `closes_clause` (continuity.py's mismatch always reports a clause as still-uncovered rather than closed -- the conservative direction, never a false green). SURVEYED, LOWER RISK, NOT FIXED THIS CYCLE (scope bigger than one focused cycle -- filed as AUT-PD-030): the ledger's own `owner`/`requires_trimcrae` fields are hand-typed directly into an 80+-entry JSON store with no writer module to attach a shared constant to; a typo on `requires_trimcrae` specifically would silently let an outward-facing item read as ready in continuity.py with no warning (unless its text also matches the outward-facing regex) -- real risk, but the fix is a whole-ledger schema/typo linter, not a two-file constant-sharing pattern, so it is filed separately rather than forced into this shape. `autonomy-state.json`'s dial names were checked for a second writer that could independently drift and none exists today -- it is hand-edited directly, every reader (health.py, continuity.py, handoff.py) spells its keys identically, and each key carries its own inline `_<key>_means` documentation reducing typo risk -- so this is not a live two-file drift risk unless a governor script starts writing it programmatically, and no such script exists. Not filed as a follow-up; re-open if that changes.

entries.what:
⛔⛔ THE MAP-EDIT STATE MACHINE CANNOT SEE AN EDIT APPLIED THE WAY THIS REPOSITORY REQUIRES, SO IT REPORTED FOUR FALSE 'PENDING' ROWS — one of them for three weeks. `map_edits_required` decides PENDING by asking whether the text an edit meant to REPLACE is still in the file. CLAUDE.md rule 1.2 requires a corrected passage to CARRY its superseded wording ("Superseded, retained: '<old sentence>'"), so applying an edit correctly leaves that text findable and the row never clears. The convention and the checker were in direct conflict.
TWO MORE SHAPES FAIL IDENTICALLY, each found only by fixing the one before it: (a) an ADDITIVE edit's anchor survives its own application — RT-TCIP.artifacts proposes '"ART-TCIP-REACH"' -> '"ART-TCIP-REACH", "ART-TCIP-EFFECTOR-ARMS"', so the old string is a SUBSTRING of the new one and the row could never reach APPLIED by any action; (b) the proposal for that same row spans TWO LINES, and the search is line-at-a-time, so the applied check could only ever answer no.
FIXED: the PENDING question is asked only of each line's LIVE part (up to any supersession marker); an uninformative additive anchor is overridden only by a POSITIVE applied reading; multi-line needles are matched across lines with whitespace collapsed.
⚠ AND THE FIRST TWO ATTEMPTS AT THIS WERE EACH WRONG IN A WAY THE TESTS CAUGHT: ignoring an additive anchor outright dropped the 'closure_kind — NO EDIT REQUIRED' row to STALE_ANCHOR, the one state that FAILS THE BUILD, for a row whose point is that nothing is owed; and the multi-line branch was written correctly but tested AFTER `_strip_emphasis`, which collapses newlines — so the branch read correctly and never ran.
⛔ MUTATION-TESTED, AND THE FIRST PASS WAS A FALSE PASS. Three reverts were run against a COPY: two 'were not caught', and re-running with an assertion that the mutation had actually applied showed one of those had silently not applied at all. Of the genuine two, one was a real gap — nothing asserted that the STATE MACHINE passes the live-only flag, only that the helper honours it when handed it, so the helper could be correct and unused. A test was added and all three reverts now fail.
entries._what_is_left: Nothing. 12 tests in research/modalities/tests/test_a_described_map_edit_resolves_through_the_correction_convention.py, including the negative control that a genuinely owed edit still reads PENDING and a genuinely stale anchor still reads STALE_ANCHOR — three narrowings must not buy a green board by deleting the alarm.

entries.what: ⛔⛔ WIRE `holder_liveness.py` INTO `continuity.py`'s CAPACITY COUNT — AND IT IS FILED RATHER THAN DONE BECAUSE OF research-loop §6. AUT-PD-150 built the detector: given a driver-supplied verdict it classifies every open lease ALIVE / DEAD / UNMEASURED / UNRESOLVED / UNKNOWN_STATUS, fails closed in every direction, reports and never acts, and is pinned by 14 assertions with 8/8 mutations caught. What is still missing is the CONSUMER: `continuity.py` counts a dead seat as a live worker, so the capacity reading that parked 109 rows would still be printed today. The shape is a `--holder-verdict PATH` argument, `dead_owners()` discounted from `by_owner` in the capacity block, and the discounted holders NAMED in the output so the discount is falsifiable rather than silent. ⛔ WHY CYC-0072-2e57571a DID NOT MAKE THIS EDIT ITSELF. research-loop §6: *a bar may not be changed by the cycle that the bar just blocked.* The capacity check is exactly the bar that blocked this cycle — `continuity.py --check` printed AT CAPACITY at 23:30Z and every row in the queue was unstartable. An edit that makes that check stop blocking me, written by me, in the cycle it blocked, is the precise shape §6 forbids, and the honest test it gives — *does this change make it easier for me to report success?* — answers yes. So the detector (new module, reports only, changes no bar, blocks nothing) landed, and the consumer (which moves a bar) is filed for a LATER cycle, which §6 explicitly permits: 'a later cycle may make the identical change'. ⭐ THE RELEASE THIS CYCLE PERFORMED IS NOT THAT EDIT AND SHOULD NOT BE READ AS ONE. `continuity.py`'s own message instructs it in as many words — 'if a lease above names a worker that is not actually running, that is litter — release it (owner: null)'. Releasing litter is the sanctioned response to the check; rewriting the check is not. ⚠ AND THE TAKER SHOULD DECIDE ONE THING THIS ROW DELIBERATELY DOES NOT: whether an UNMEASURED holder should ever be discounted. It must not — 'not observed is not alive' is the whole safety property — but a future author under capacity pressure will be tempted, so the argument is written here where they will read it, not left to be re-derived.

entries.what:
⛔ A REVIEW-SEAT SUBAGENT EDITED THE LIVE TRACKED TREE DURING A READ-ONLY HARDENING ROUND, AND ONLY THE 'STAGE BY PATH, NEVER -A' RULE CAUGHT IT (CLAUDE.md §6). Round 12 of PUB-ASO hardening (AUT-PROP-040) dispatched five parallel blind-review subagents, each explicitly told 'do NOT edit any tracked file in the working tree — this is a read-only review seat' and, if it wanted to mutation-test a guard, to 'make a scratch copy first ... and mutate the COPY, never the live tree.' Mid-round, `git status` showed an UNSTAGED, UNEXPECTED edit to research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md: 'with *TAF15* a substantial minority ⭐ and your *TCF12* and *TFG*' — a nonsensical two-token insertion the driver did not make. Caught only because the driver staged research/manuscripts/submission-metrics.json BY PATH rather than `git add -A`; had -A been used, this would have committed and pushed to `main` inside an otherwise-legitimate commit, matching the shape of the 13-inverted-claims incident this rule already exists to prevent. Reverted immediately with `git checkout --`; no commit ever contained it.

ROOT-CAUSED, NOT GUESSED (CLAUDE.md §4): seat 1 (the regression lens) later reported it had verified this exact mutation 'on a scratch clone (/tmp/.../seat1-clone-real, checked out at the pinned commit, git checkout -- ... used to revert each time)'. The obvious hypothesis — a `cp -al` hardlink clone whose in-place edits leak back to the source inode, the failure mode paper-hardening §8b.1 already documents — was checked directly and REFUTED: `stat -c %i` on the live file (inode 483841) and on the same path inside scratchpad/seat1-clone-real (inode 1886303) are DIFFERENT inodes; seat1-clone-real also carries its own .git directory, confirming it is a real separate checkout, not a hardlinked copy. So the clone itself was not the leak. The mutation must have reached the live path some other way — most plausibly the seat's editing tool was pointed at the live repo path for at least one test before (or instead of) the clone for that specific mutation, and its own revert step ran after the driver's `git status` check happened to land in the open window. The seat's own report and the driver's direct observation cannot both be fully accurate; this entry records the observation (the live-tree diff, with inode evidence) rather than the seat's self-report, per CLAUDE.md §4's own priority of a real diagnostic over an agent's account of its own actions.

⚠ NOT A CATASTROPHE THIS TIME, BUT THE MARGIN WAS ONE HABIT: if the driver had used `git add -A` (a natural shortcut when only one file was actually intended to change), this lands on `main`. The instruction given to seats ('use a scratch copy, never the live tree') is a PLAIN SUGGESTION, not a structural boundary — nothing prevents a general-purpose subagent's editing tool from targeting any path it likes, including the shared live tree, when its cwd is the same repo the driver is sitting in.

PROPOSED FIX (not applied here — scoping only): any future review-seat prompt that even mentions the possibility of mutation-testing should either (a) launch the seat inside an isolated worktree (EnterWorktree / a dedicated git worktree per seat, per research-loop §3's existing worktree guidance for MUTATING subagents) rather than relying on a self-reported scratch copy, or (b) if a true read-only seat only occasionally wants to check mutation robustness, make the instruction a hard constraint naming the exact clone path and explicitly forbidding any tool call from touching a path under the live repo, not a soft 'if you want to test something, use a copy' suggestion. Either way: CLAUDE.md §6's 'stage by path, never -A, while a subagent that mutates the working tree is running' is the backstop that actually worked here and must stay in force even for seats explicitly told they are read-only, since this incident shows that instruction alone is not reliable.

⛔⛔ UPDATE, SAME CYCLE, MORE SEVERE THAN THE NEAR-MISS ABOVE: it did NOT stay a near-miss. While fixing the 'stale submission-metrics.json' preflight failure, the driver ran `python3 research/manuscripts/submission_metrics.py` (the real regeneration, not `--check`) directly against the LIVE WORKING TREE while seat 1 was still active in the same window — and the live article file was contaminated at that exact moment. The regeneration silently captured the contaminated word count (main_words 3721, i.e. the clean 3719 plus the two inserted tokens '⭐'+'your', which this counter's regex apparently both count) and the driver COMMITTED it (6e7d44e06), reading the discrepancy as genuine pre-existing drift rather than live contamination. This is a corrupted-artifact commit that landed on `main`, not merely a caught-in-time diff. It was caught two commits later by round 12's own seat 4 (citations/build/gates lens), which independently regenerated the metric inside an isolated worktree of the PINNED commit and got 3719, flagged the direction of the 'fix' as backwards, and named the exact mechanism. Corrected in 3a53478a8.

★★ THE GENERALISABLE LESSON THIS ADDS, BEYOND THE git add -A RULE ALREADY STATED ABOVE: 'stage by path, never -A' protects the COMMIT boundary, but it does NOT protect a DERIVATION step that reads the live working tree WHILE a mutation-risk subagent is running. `submission_metrics.py` (like `aso_archive_manifest.py` and any other generator that reads files off disk rather than off `git show`) has no way to know the tree it just read was transiently contaminated -- it can only report what the bytes said at read time. The fix that actually worked here was VERIFICATION AFTER THE FACT (a second seat re-deriving the same number against an isolated pinned-commit worktree), not prevention -- which argues for either (a) not running any live-tree-reading regeneration script while review/mutation-risk subagents are still active, deferring such fixes until they have all reported, or (b) always regenerating from a `git stash`-clean or freshly-cloned tree rather than the shared working directory when subagents are concurrently active in it.

Measured 2026-08-28 by CYC-0053-3217966b, on itself: the driver held (a) an unpushed merge commit of seat s55's branch and (b) uncommitted edits to research-ledger.json (a closure plus three new rows), with `./scripts/preflight.sh` STILL RUNNING on that tree. Net: 467 lines of new code and 64 lines of ledger reached origin/main with the gate that was supposed to clear them still in flight. ⚠ THE GATE DID NOT FAIL — IT WAS BYPASSED, which is the same shape as AUT-PD-0xx's `git add -A` mutation window: a narrow tool that stages by FILE and pushes by BRANCH cannot distinguish the one row it was asked to lease from whatever else the working tree happens to be holding. A green outcome is not the finding; the absent refusal is.) ★ FIX, and the choice matters: `claim.py` should REFUSE to run when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty outside the ledger row it is about to write, or when HEAD is ahead of origin/main by commits it did not author — printing what it found, so the caller commits and gates deliberately. ⛔ DO NOT 'fix' this by having claim.py stage a partial hunk or push a detached ref: the claim's whole safety argument is that the push is an atomic compare-and-swap on the trunk (AUT-PROP-030), and anything that makes the push narrower than HEAD weakens the arbiter. The honest fix is a refusal, not a cleverer push. ⚠ AND WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the refusal must not deadlock the ordinary loop, where a cycle legitimately holds a ledger edit and a claim at once — decide explicitly whether 'dirty' means the ledger file itself (usually legitimate) or anything else (never legitimate), and mutation-test both directions.

entries.what: ⛔⛔ `session_cap.verdict()` IS INVERTED ON THE SUCCESS CASE: A SESSION THAT HANDS OFF CORRECTLY IS TOLD **MUST NOT STOP**, AND ONE WHOSE HANDOFF FAILED IS TOLD **MAY STOP**. Measured 2026-08-29T00:35Z (CYC-0073-2e57571a) against the module's own functions, not by reading: `blocked_handoff({'handoff':{'child_session_id':'session_CHILD','attempted':True}})` -> `None`; `blocked_handoff({'handoff':{'attempted':True,'refused_by':'platform said no'}})` -> the reason; `blocked_handoff({'handoff':{'attempted':False}})` -> `None`. `verdict()` then does `why = blocked_handoff(ours[-1]); if not why: return False, '…records no handoff attempt — an absent record is a session that did not try'`. So A SUCCESSFUL HANDOFF AND A HANDOFF NEVER ATTEMPTED ARE THE SAME VALUE AT THE ONE PLACE THAT DECIDES, and only the FAILED handoff earns the right to stop. ⭐ THE INTENT IS NOT IN DOUBT AND THE COMMENT SAYS IT OUT LOUD, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A WIRING SLIP AND NOT A DESIGN DISAGREEMENT. `blocked_handoff`'s docstring: *'A receipt that HANDED OFF is not blocked — `child_session_id` present means the ordinary path applies and this module has nothing to say.'* It correctly returns None to mean 'not my case'. The CALLER never implemented that ordinary path, so 'not my case' silently became 'did not try'. `verdict()` needs the handed-off case checked FIRST, before the blocked case, and it is missing entirely. ⛔ THE HARM IS THE CAP DOING THE OPPOSITE OF ITS JOB. `max_cycles_per_session` exists so a session stops and a FRESH context takes over — research-loop §3, and autonomy-state.json calls the third cycle 'the signal that the driver should have spawned'. As wired, every session that obeys the rule is told to keep going, and the only sessions permitted to stop are the ones that failed to produce a successor. Observed live: this session wrote 2 receipts against a cap of 2 and created session_01G6maQEKfLfVi8TqsraQVse, and `session_cap.py` still returned `may_stop: false`. ⛔⛔ AND `research/autonomy/session_cap.py` IS ABSENT FROM `amendment_guard.GOVERNED`, WHICH IS A SECOND DEFECT AND THE MORE DANGEROUS ONE. That tuple governs priority-weights.json, publish_bar.py, health.py, CLAUDE.md, the architecture, the skills and the tests — every file that decides whether a cycle may claim success. `session_cap.py` decides whether a session has earned the right to STOP, which is exactly that kind of file, and the guard's own header says an unsure case is treated as GOVERNED because 'a misfiled governed edit is an annoyance; a misfiled free edit' is not. ⚠ WHY CYC-0073 DID NOT FIX EITHER HALF, AND THIS IS THE POINT OF THE ROW. research-loop §6: *a bar may not be changed by the cycle that the bar just blocked.* This bar was blocking THIS cycle at the moment it was found, and §6's honest test — *does this change make it easier for me to report success?* — answers yes without qualification: the edit flips this session's own verdict from MUST NOT STOP to MAY STOP. `amendment_guard --diff-from` would have returned PERMITTED, because the path is not in the list — and taking that as permission would be using the second defect to excuse editing under the first. A LATER CYCLE MAY MAKE THE IDENTICAL CHANGE (§6 says so in as many words); this one may not, and a fresh session is already running. ★ THE FIX, WRITTEN OUT SO THE TAKER NEED NOT RE-DERIVE IT: in `verdict()`, after the receipt-count check, `if handoff.child_session_id_of(ours[-1]): return True, '<n> receipt(s) at a cap of <c>, and the handoff produced <child>'` — then fall through to the existing blocked/absent logic unchanged. Add `research/autonomy/session_cap.py` to `amendment_guard.GOVERNED` in the same commit, and pin BOTH with tests: `test_a_capped_session_may_stop.py` exists and did not catch this, so read why before adding to it.

entries.what: ⛔⛔ `session_cap.py` CANNOT TELL A SUCCESSFUL HANDOFF FROM NO HANDOFF AT ALL, AND SAYS THE WRONG ONE. Measured 2026-08-28 by CYC-0061-3217966b on its own committed receipt: `handoff.child_session_id_of(r)` → 'session_01AiEBt1BhjfPMi9rCZ4rZ53' (the successor really was created), `session_cap.blocked_handoff(r)` → None, `session_cap.verdict()` → (False, '… the latest receipt records no handoff attempt — an absent record is a session that did not try'). ⭐ THE MODULE IS RIGHT AND ITS CALLER IS WRONG: `blocked_handoff` is documented to return None when a receipt carries a child_session_id, precisely because 'a session that DID hand off is not BLOCKED'. `verdict()` then reads that None as 'no handoff attempt', CONFLATING THE SUCCESS PATH WITH THE ABSENT ONE. ⛔ THE CONSEQUENCE RUNS THE WRONG WAY: a session whose handoff FAILED may stop, while a session that created its successor as prescribed is told MUST NOT STOP — permanently, by a message that misstates its own receipt. The only remaining exits are 'my handoff was refused' and 'keep working past the cap', and the second is the context-exhaustion failure the cap exists to prevent, so the instrument pushes sessions toward the harm it guards. ★ THE FIX IS IN `verdict()`, NOT IN `blocked_handoff` AND NOT IN THE RECEIPT SCHEMA: at or over the cap, MAY STOP should hold when the latest receipt carries a child_session_id (handed off) OR when blocked_handoff names a refusal (attempted and blocked); only an ABSENT record stays red. Keep the absent-record rule exactly as it is — it is the half that works, and it is why this session created a successor at all. ⛔⛔ DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED BY THE CYCLE IT BLOCKED (CLAUDE.md §6, amendment_guard): this is the bar refusing that session's stopping point, so its own fix would be self-serving even though the diagnosis is independently checkable by the three-line reproduction above. A LATER CYCLE MAY MAKE THE IDENTICAL CHANGE. ⚠ Until it lands, a correct handoff still reads MUST NOT STOP — do not take that message as evidence a handoff is missing; read `handoff.child_session_id` in the receipt instead.

⛔⛔ A RETIRED PERMISSION IS STILL ASSERTED IN autonomy-state.json, AND A CYCLE BELIEVED IT OVER THE AUTHORITY RECORD — COSTING AN ESCALATION trimcrae SHOULD NEVER HAVE SEEN. Measured 2026-08-31 by CYC-0090-d7df5340, caught by trimcrae in one sentence: 'Aren't you supposed to post to zenodo on your own when needed'.
★ THE TWO HOMES. research/autonomy/publication-authority.json `zenodo_archive_publication` is the fact: standing_grant true since 2026-08-30, per-publication approval retired the same day, exercised twice with read-backs. research/autonomy/autonomy-state.json `budget_hold.authorised_exceptions[0]` says, in its scope note, 'the Zenodo publish is still his by hand'. That sentence was true when written and was never retired when the grant landed.
⛔ THE COST WAS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Round 27's third blocker (R27-B3, the paper citing an unpublished Zenodo DOI) was filed as AUT-PROP-054 with requires_trimcrae true, round 28 was BLOCKED behind it, a PushNotification was sent and an AskUserQuestion put four options to him — all on a permission that had not existed for a day. The correct behaviour was to refresh the draft and publish, which is work the loop is already authorised to do and had already done twice.

But it is stated as prose IN the authority file, so it only binds a reader who already opened the authority file; a cycle that reads the state file first and finds a confident sentence there never gets to it. That is CLAUDE.md §1's one-fact-one-place rule failing in the direction it always fails: the stale copy is the one that gets read.
★ CANDIDATE FIXES, none taken here: (1) delete the claim from autonomy-state.json and leave a pointer — cheapest, and the one rule 1.1 actually prescribes; (2) a health row or lint rule that greps the governance artifacts for permission language and fails when a file other than publication-authority.json asserts what the loop may or may not publish; (3) have `authority_permits` be the only readable source, with the state file carrying no permission prose at all. ⛔ (1) and (3) touch a GOVERNED path and this cycle is the one that was misled by it, so amendment_guard applies and a later cycle should make the edit.

entries.what: ⛔ `TaskStop` ON A BACKGROUNDED PREFLIGHT KILLS THE HARNESS'S WRAPPER AND LEAVES `preflight.sh` RUNNING. Measured 2026-08-27 (CYC-0020): §6 says to kill a gate run the tree moved under rather than sit through it, and this cycle did that three times. Each TaskStop reported success. `ps` then showed pid 8682 STILL running the stopped run's preflight.sh at 3:05 elapsed, with its own `pytest -n 4` child, alongside the live run's pid 9789 — TWO gates, eight workers, on a box sized for four. ⚠ THE SYMPTOM IS NOT A CRASH, IT IS SLOWNESS, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVES: the live gate simply takes much longer than its measured ~255 s, and the honest reading of that ('unexpected slowness is a signal', CLAUDE.md §4) is indistinguishable from 'the suite is just slow today' unless somebody runs `ps`. It was found only because the manuscripts suite overran and this cycle went looking for a mechanism instead of reassuring itself. ⛔ AND THE HARNESS THEN REPORTS THE KILLED JOB AS `failed with exit code 1`, which reads exactly like a RED GATE — a second way to draw a wrong conclusion from a stop. The killed run wrote no `EXIT=` marker, which is what distinguishes the two and is why the marker rule exists. ⭐ THE FIX IS A STOP THAT REACHES THE CHILD: have preflight.sh write its own pid to a file and give the repo a `scripts/stop-preflight.sh` that kills that pid's process GROUP, or run it with `setsid`/`exec` so the tracked process IS the gate. ⛔ NOT `pkill -f preflight` — CLAUDE.md §6 records that pattern matching the killer's own command line, three times in one session. Kill by recorded pid, never by pattern.

entries.what: ⛔⛔ ENTRY IDS COLLIDE THE SAME WAY RECEIPT IDS DID, AND THE FIX APPLIED TO ONE WAS NEVER APPLIED TO THE OTHER. `ids.next_entry_id` derives max+1 over committed state, so two sessions reading the same trunk allocate the SAME id — concurrency is outside the derivation BY CONSTRUCTION. That is verbatim the finding AUT-PROP-013 recorded for RECEIPT ids on 2026-08-27, and receipt ids were fixed by appending a session discriminator (`CYC-0064-f5c9b5f2`). Entry ids were not. ⚠ MEASURED 2026-08-28, live: CYC-0064-f5c9b5f2 filed AUT-PD-117 and AUT-PD-118; CYC-0064-1f1a2449 filed a DIFFERENT AUT-PD-117 and a DIFFERENT AUT-PD-118 from the same committed state, minutes apart, and pushed first. Both pairs are real, distinct, wanted items. The loser renumbered by hand to AUT-PD-119/120/121. ⭐ IT IS CAUGHT RATHER THAN SILENT — `priority.py` refuses a ledger with a duplicated id, and the push is a compare-and-swap, so the collision surfaces as a conflict instead of an overwrite. That is the good half. The bad half is that it surfaces AFTER both sessions have written their rows, the merge is manual, and the handoff prompt has to warn every successor to check for duplicates by hand after every rebase — a warning that exists precisely because the id does not carry what would make the warning unnecessary. ★ THE FIX IS THE ONE ALREADY IN THE REPOSITORY, one function over: give `next_entry_id` the same discriminator `next_receipt` has. Two sessions can then both file the Nth process defect of the day and never share a filename. ⛔ NOT DONE HERE, and deliberately: this cycle IS the losing side of the collision, and `research-loop` §6's invariant is that a bar may not be changed by the cycle it just blocked. The identical argument applies to a mechanism that just cost this cycle a renumber. A later cycle may make this change; this one records it.

entries.what: ⛔ `continuity.py --check` IS STEP 12 OF THE CYCLE CONTRACT AND A CORRECTLY-HANDED-OFF CYCLE CANNOT PASS IT. Its own message names three acceptable ways to end a turn — 'something actually running (a subagent, a dispatched workflow, a spawned session), an item genuinely blocked, or an empty list' — but the CODE has exactly one exit-0 path: `at_capacity`, which is true only when the number of LEDGER LEASES (rows carrying an `owner`) is >= autonomy-state.json `subagent_width`. A spawned successor session holds no lease; neither does a dispatched workflow. So the two things the text invites a cycle to do are both invisible to the check that grades it. ⚠ THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE TWO DEFECTS research-loop §1 ALREADY RECORDS (`cycles_are_sized`, `fanout_is_governed`): an instrument whose green state is unreachable by correct behaviour, which trains cycles to ignore it. ⭐ WHAT THE FIX IS NOT: raising the exit-0 surface to 'a receipt mentions a handoff' would make the check pass on a SENTENCE, which is the v1 defect its own header records ('it asked whether the work was WRITTEN DOWN rather than whether it was MOVING'). The honest options are to count a committed `handoff.child_session_id` from THIS cycle as a running worker, or to accept a caller-supplied declaration of what was dispatched — the header considers and rejects a `--what-is-running` flag, so that rejection is the thing to re-argue, not to route around. Decide which, and mutation-test that a cycle which spawned NOTHING still fails.

entries.what:
⛔⛔ A REBASE BEFORE PUSH SILENTLY ORPHANS EVERY ARTIFACT THAT RECORDS `HEAD`, AND THE REBASE IS THE ROUTINE MOVE WHEN A CONCURRENT SESSION HAS MOVED THE TRUNK. Measured 2026-08-31 by CYC-0090-d7df5340, on itself, and then recognised as the cause of a CI red this cycle had already mis-diagnosed once.
★ THE MECHANISM, REPRODUCED RATHER THAN ARGUED. `aso_archive_manifest.py` stamps `git_revision` = HEAD at generation time. The prescribed ordering is: commit everything, regenerate the manifest against the committed tree, commit it. That records the PARENT commit's sha, which is correct — until `git rebase origin/main` before the push rewrites that parent. This cycle recorded 6820db2add67, rebased onto a trunk two commits ahead, and pushed; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6820db2add67 HEAD` then exits non-zero. The sha still resolves in the LOCAL clone (it is in the reflog), so nothing looks wrong here, and it does not exist on the remote at all.
⭐ AND THAT IS WHY CI WAS RED, WHICH THIS CYCLE FIRST EXPLAINED WRONG. tests.yml on f9e50599 failed `test_the_deposit_the_papers_cite_is_current` twice — `b93499e944013bbf199afe98ad402a516e63b798` and `fbb473bce3ac2ec214ee86b95db68b162160f0ea` reported as 'Not a valid object name'. Both resolve locally, so this cycle hypothesised a shallow `actions/checkout` clone. ⛔ THAT WAS A 'probably X' AND IT WAS WRONG. The runner clones from the REMOTE, where those commits were never pushed under those shas — an earlier session rebased before pushing, exactly as this one did. Same defect, three commits apart, in two different artifacts.
★ THE GUARDS EXIST AND FIRE, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON THIS IS VISIBLE: test_the_manifest_revision_is_a_commit_a_reader_can_resolve.py and the two deposit-state guards beside it. They catch it AFTER the push, in CI, which costs a commit each time.
★ CANDIDATE FIXES, none taken here. (1) A pre-push hook that re-derives any artifact whose recorded revision is no longer an ancestor of HEAD — .githooks/pre-push already exists and is already pointed at by core.hooksPath. (2) Push first and rebase only on rejection, so the recorded sha is the one that lands — weaker, since the rejection path still rebases. (3) Record the TREE hash rather than the commit sha, which a rebase does not change; that is the only option immune to the mechanism rather than defending against it, and it is a change to what the artifact means, so it is a proposal and not a repair. ⚠ deposit-state.json's two orphaned revisions are still orphaned on the trunk and are NOT fixed by this row — they name uploads that really happened, so re-stamping them to a live sha would be inventing provenance, not repairing it. What they need is the observation of which commit each upload actually corresponds to, which only a re-dispatch can settle.

entries.evidence: BUILT AND TESTED. Added `lease_arbitration()` to research/autonomy/continuity.py, plus a `--leases` CLI flag. For every OPEN row an OTHER worker's lease is holding back, it computes the same claim_lease arithmetic `priority.release_stale_claims` uses (periods x the cycle interval, read live from priority-weights.json / autonomy-state.json, never restated) and reports the lease's age against that threshold, whether it is already past expiry (would be released on the next `priority.py --write` but has not been yet), and whether the row would read as ready right now if that lease were gone (`would_be_ready_if_released`, checked against a copy so the view mutates nothing). This is the arbitration the item asked for: between a lease that LOOKS alive because nobody has re-scored yet, and a ready row sitting behind it. 11 new tests in test_continuity_has_no_green_state_recording_can_buy.py (54 total, all green): self-exclusion of the caller's own lease, within/past the lease window, an unstamped claim treated as stale immediately (mirrors release_stale_claims' fail-toward-releasing direction), would_be_ready_if_released against a second real block vs. the lease being the only block, finished rows excluded, sort order (unstamped first), and the CLI's own output. Mutation-tested by hand against the live tree (no subagent, no concurrent mutation window): reverting the self-exclusion check and reverting the unstamped-is-stale branch each made the corresponding new test fail, then both were restored and the full suite reconfirmed green (54 passed). entries.what: THE COMMIT LOOP IS ~4x SLOWER THAN THE TRUNK'S MEDIAN PUSH INTERVAL, SO A DRIVER THAT OBEYS THE GATING RULE IS STRUCTURALLY LIKELY TO BE OVERTAKEN -- AND THE COMMITS OVERTAKING IT MOSTLY DO NOT PAY THE GATE. GATE COST: preflight on the merged tree ran 02:38:2x -> 02:50:01Z, ~11.6 min, dominated by gate 13 (`pytest -n 4 --dist loadfile scripts/tests research/autonomy/tests`), consistent with AUT-PD-155's independent 369.68 s / 373.95 s for that gate against the 39.3 s pinned in CLAUDE.md section 6. TRUNK RATE: over the last 25 origin/main commits the median inter-push gap is 2.7 min and the mean 4.6 min; 22 of 24 gaps are under 13 min. So a single gated push has a low chance of surviving its own gate window, and this cycle was in fact rejected non-fast-forward at 02:50 and overtaken AGAIN (0c8d307b5) while resolving the resulting conflicts. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MOVING THE TRUNK, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MAKES THIS A DEFECT RATHER THAN TRAFFIC: 10 of the last 40 origin/main commits are `claim <ID> for <seat>` lease-writes from claim.py, and others are automated CI ticks (`autonomy tick: loop health board`, `vast watch`, `ternary watch`). NONE of these pays an 11.6 min preflight. The trunk's push rate is therefore set by cheap automated writes while correctness-bearing commits are gated at ~4x that interval -- the starvation is between two different classes of writer, not between competing researchers. ⭐ THE REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY CONCEDED THE PRINCIPLE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FIXABLE RATHER THAN A LAW OF NATURE: push_guard.py's docstring states it is deliberately 'NOT A RE-GATE' because 'nothing that expensive can sit in front of every push and survive', and that an integration performed AT PUSH TIME creates a third tree neither session gated. entries.what:
⛔⛔ A HALF-FINISHED ZENODO CORRECTION WAS UNRECOVERABLE, BECAUSE THE SCRIPT COULD ONLY ASK FOR A NEW VERSION AND NEVER FOR THE ONE IT HAD ALREADY OPENED. Measured 2026-09-01 by CYC-0090-d7df5340, in two real run logs rather than reasoned from the API docs.
★ THE TWO OBSERVATIONS THAT TOGETHER MAKE IT A TRAP, EACH READ FROM ITS LOG:
  · run 33498033370 (job 99824631459) — `POST /deposit/depositions/22182180/actions/newversion` SUCCEEDED and the immediately following `GET https://zenodo.org/api/deposit/depositions/22229096` returned `504 Gateway Time-out`. ⭐ THAT LOG LINE IS ALSO WHERE THE DRAFT ID COMES FROM: 22229096 is READ, not inferred from a numbering pattern (CLAUDE.md §7).
  · run 33498227279 (job 99825249726) — the retry POSTed newversion again and Zenodo answered `400 {"field": "files.enabled", "messages": ["Please remove all files first."]}`. That is Zenodo declining to open a second version while one is open, and NOTHING in that wording says so — it reads as a defect in the archive rather than a run that needs resuming, which is how this cycle spent an hour on a probe branch built on the wrong premise.
⛔ WHY A RETRY CANNOT FIX THIS AND MUST NOT BE ASKED TO. AUT-PD-199 deliberately retries reads only; the failure here is a mutation that ALREADY SUCCEEDED, so repeating it is exactly the second-orphan case that scope exists to prevent. The recovery had to be a READ of state Zenodo already holds.
★ THE FIX: the published record's own `links.latest_draft` names the open draft, so the new-version path now reads it FIRST and adopts that draft, POSTing `actions/newversion` only when no draft is open. The correction becomes resumable — a transient failure anywhere after the POST costs a re-run, not a record.
⛔ AND IT IS CHECKED, NOT TRUSTED, BECAUSE THE FAILURE MODE IS THE WORST ONE AVAILABLE: adopting whatever a link points at is how a corrected archive gets uploaded over a version a reader may already cite. An adopted deposition that comes back `submitted`, or that is the published record itself, refuses BEFORE any PUT or DELETE.
★ GUARDED AND MUTATION-TESTED: `scripts/tests/test_a_new_version_run_adopts_the_draft_it_already_opened.py`, 6 tests, 4/4 mutations caught (adopt branch removed · inherited files never cleared · submitted-target refusal dropped · self-link refusal dropped).
⚠ THE SELF-LINK MUTATION SURVIVED THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT SUITE, and the reason is worth keeping: the fake API keyed on the deposition id appearing in the path, and the adopted deposition's path CONTAINS the published id in that case — so the fake returned a `submitted` record, the earlier refusal fired, and the test passed with the guard deleted. A test whose double is shaped like its own assumption measures the double.

entries._CORRECTION_2026_09_01_live_run:
⛔⛔ THE FIX'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE LIVE RUN IS WHAT SAID SO — `links.latest_draft` IS NOT A DRAFT POINTER. Run 33519701596 on f37ef3c02, the first real exercise of this code: `a new-version draft is ALREADY OPEN on record 22182180 — adopting it`, immediately followed by `the draft link on record 22182180 resolved to deposition 22182180, which Zenodo reports as PUBLISHED`. That link tracks the latest VERSION, normally the published one.
★★ THE GUARD DID ITS JOB ON ITS FIRST LIVE RUN, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. The `submitted` refusal was written as belt-and-braces against a case reasoned about rather than seen; the case was real, it arrived within the hour, and what it stopped was uploading the corrected archive over the version both papers cite. ⭐ A helper's guarantee is not a guard — the refusal is at the CALL SITE, so it holds for a draft this run opened and for one it adopted alike.
★ ALSO PROVEN LIVE IN THE SAME LOG, AUT-PD-199's retry: `Zenodo GET /deposit/depositions/22182180 -> 502; retrying in 2s (1/3)`, then success. Before that fix this run would have died on the 502 and been reported as another outage.
★ THE CORRECTED FIX: the open draft is found by LISTING the account's depositions (`/deposit/depositions?status=draft&size=100&all_versions=1`, falling back to the unfiltered listing) and matching on `conceptrecid`, which every version of a record shares. An entry that is not `submitted`, carries that concept id, and is not the published record itself IS the open draft. Reads only; returning nothing means 'found nothing', never 'there is nothing', which is why the call site re-checks rather than trusting the helper.
⛔ AND ONE MUTATION SURVIVED THE REWRITE'S FIRST TEST PASS, WHICH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE HERE: removing the `submitted` filter from the listing search left all 8 tests green. Because every version shares the concept id, that mutation makes the run adopt an OLDER PUBLISHED VERSION — id different from the current one, so the self-check does not fire — and upload over it. The fixtures were all shaped like the happy path. A ninth test now drives exactly that listing; 5/5 mutations caught.

entries.what: ⚠ `lint_readability.sentences()` DOES NOT BREAK BEFORE A CALLOUT GLYPH, SO IT REPORTS TWO SENTENCES AS ONE AND OVERSTATES THE LENGTH. The split regex is `(?<=[.!?])\s+(?=[A-Z(“\"])`, so a sentence opening with ⛔, ⭐, ⚠, ★ or ✅ — the house callout style, used on nearly every emphatic sentence in these manuscripts — is glued to the sentence before it. Two other openers fail the same way and both were hit in this document: a section reference (`§4.3's conservative-floor reading …`) and a sentence following a quotation whose period sits INSIDE the closing quote (`… EMCs.” So the honest reading …`). ⭐ THE DIRECTION MATTERS AND IT IS THE SAFE ONE: the defect makes the screen STRICTER, never laxer, so nothing has been let through by it and no published claim rests on it. That is why it is filed rather than fixed. ⛔⛔ AND IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED FOR A SECOND, BINDING REASON: `lint_readability` IS the instrument behind publish_bar clause 7, clause 7 had just BLOCKED PUB-FUSION-PARTNER, and research-loop §6's invariant is that a bar may not be changed by the cycle the bar just blocked. Fixing the splitter would have retired 2 of the 17 findings without touching the prose — the textbook self-serving edit `amendment_guard` exists to catch. CYC-0070-ba841eee therefore split all 17 in the prose instead, including the 2 whose real sentences were already inside the ceiling. ★ A LATER CYCLE MAY MAKE THE IDENTICAL CHANGE, and should: extend the lookahead to the callout glyphs and to `§`, and treat a closing quote or bracket after terminal punctuation as still terminal. ⛔ MUTATION-TEST IT — a splitter change moves every count in `readability-baseline.json`, so re-pin the baseline in the same commit and state that the counts moved because the instrument did, not because the prose did.

entries.what: ⛔ A COMMIT THAT EDITS AN ARCHIVED MANUSCRIPT CANNOT HAVE A GREEN PREFLIGHT, AND THE GENERATOR'S OWN DOCUMENTED FIX REQUIRES MAKING THAT COMMIT ANYWAY — MEASURED 2026-08-28 (CYC-0069), on a one-sentence split in the ASO journal article. ⭐ THE TRAP IS THAT BOTH REACHABLE STATES ARE RED, so there is no ordering inside ONE commit that clears it. (a) Leave the manifest at HEAD: the inventory no longer matches the edited article, and --check-archive reports STALE. (b) Regenerate it: the tree is necessarily dirty (the article, and whatever else the commit carries), so the manifest records `git_tree_is_clean_apart_from_this_manifest: false` and --check-archive REFUSES it as a provenance failure — correctly, and that refusal is AUT-PD-016's guard doing its job. ⭐ THE GENERATOR PRINTS THE RIGHT ANSWER AND IT IS A TWO-COMMIT ANSWER: 'commit (or stash) every other change FIRST, then regenerate the manifest against the clean tree as the session's LAST commit.' ⛔ THAT MAKES THE FIRST COMMIT'S PREFLIGHT RED BY CONSTRUCTION — CLAUDE.md §6 says preflight must pass before committing, and here the documented procedure says it cannot. ⚠ STASH IS NOT AN ESCAPE, THOUGH THE GENERATOR OFFERS IT: stashing the article edit makes the tree clean, but then the manifest regenerates against the UNEDITED article and is stale again the moment the stash comes back. Only committing works. ⚠ AND THE PRECEDENT ON `main` SHOWS THE COST IS ALREADY BEING PAID SILENTLY: 86c68df edited this same article and did not touch the manifest at all; the manifest was reconciled two commits later by an unrelated CI lane tick (0d009f1, 'selcal reap: lane tick (CI)'). So the trunk's manifest is routinely stale for a window nobody declares, and the repair is incidental to a job that exists for another purpose. WHAT TO DO — the options, none of them free, and the choice is a real one rather than obvious. (1) Let --check-archive distinguish 'stale because THIS working tree edited an archived file' (expected, and clears on the follow-up commit) from 'stale on a clean tree' (a real red), and report the first as a WARN naming the required follow-up commit. (2) Have preflight accept a declared two-commit sequence — a marker the first commit carries and the second clears — so the window is explicit and a forgotten follow-up is itself a red. (3) Move the manifest out of the commit loop entirely and make the CI lane that already fixes it the declared owner, which is the de-facto state today and should be written down or abandoned rather than left implicit. ⛔ DO NOT weaken the `false`-flag refusal to get a green: that flag is the whole content of AUT-PD-016, where a manifest on `main` asserted a sha256 for content that was in no commit.
