entries.what:
⛔⛔ THREE PROTECTIONS IN THIS REPOSITORY WERE RECORDED AND ENFORCED BY NOTHING, AND THE THIRD WAS BEING VIOLATED WHILE IT WAS BEING WRITTEN DOWN. PROPOSE: no bar, cap or prohibition may be declared without, in the SAME COMMIT, either the code that reads it or an explicit UNENFORCED marker naming what is holding the line instead.
★ THE THREE, EACH MEASURED RATHER THAN RECALLED:
(1) `subagent_width` — a governed number `grep -rn` proved no code read: two hits, the JSON defining it and one test asserting it equals 5. Compliance was luck. Recorded in CLAUDE.md §1.
(2) `max_versions_per_paper: 3` — measured 2026-09-02: three hits, none of them a reader, and `authority_permits('PUB-VACCINE-PATH','aixiv','new_version')` returns ok=True for a paper already carrying ELEVEN posted versions. The cap exists because eleven versions of one paper never moved its rating above 6 and trended DOWN; an uncapped loop would have put ten near-identical versions under trimcrae's ORCID.
(3) `gpu_spend_prohibited` — trimcrae, 2026-09-02: 'You shouldn't be doing any GPU runs as part of this automation.' It was written into `autonomy-state.json` at 16:20Z. Between 15:55Z and 16:15Z the ternary Vast lane had already made FOUR launch attempts, and it kept dispatching afterwards from a supervisor loop that a cron removal does not stop.
⭐ THE COMMON SHAPE, AND IT IS NOT FORGETFULNESS: in all three the rule was CORRECT, VISIBLE and WELL-ARGUED, and something else was the only thing actually holding the line — in (3) a price gate, which refused two attempts and let an unrelated fault kill the other two. ⛔ A ROUTINE THAT HAPPENS TO REFUSE IS NOT A CONTROL. Nothing billed, and $0 was the outcome of a gate doing an adjacent job, not of the ban working.
★ WHY A NEW RULE RATHER THAN MORE CARE: CLAUDE.md ALREADY says 'RECORDED IS NOT ENFORCED' and cites (1) by name. That sentence was in front of every session that then shipped (2) and (3). A rule this repository has already written, and violated twice more since, is not a rule that needs restating — it needs a gate, which is the proposal's own argument turned on itself.

entries.what:
✅ DONE 2026-08-27, same session it was found. ⛔ `priority.py` CRASHED ON THE COMMITTED LEDGER AND HAS FOR SOME TIME — the loop's RANKER, dead, and nothing noticed because no gate runs it. Measured 2026-08-27 on a CLEAN tree at `origin/main` (`git stash`, re-run, reproduced — so it is not the working change): `KeyError: 'score_inputs'` at priority.py:423 in `apply_session_penalties`, `entry['score_inputs']['blocked_with_evidence'] = True`. ⭐ THE CAUSE IS THE SAME CLASS AS AUT-PD-013, WHICH IS WHY IT IS FILED HERE: a field one writer emits and another reader assumes. **47 of 124 ledger entries carry no `score_inputs` key at all** — every `AUT-PROP-*`, every `AUT-PD-*`, `AUT-COV-*`, `AUT-BIX-*`, `AUT-INC-001`, `AUT-078` — because they were appended by hand or by a seat rather than by whatever wrote the originals. ⚠ THE FIX IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A `setdefault`: writing an empty `score_inputs` makes the ranker RUN and rank 47 items on absent inputs, which is a populated field that is not a measured one (CLAUDE.md §4). Decide whether an entry with no score inputs is unrankable (and say so in the output) or whether the missing inputs have honest defaults, then make the ledger's own schema enforce it. ⛔ AND WIRE IT TO SOMETHING: an unrun ranker is AUT-PD-018 again. ⭐ FIXED: `entry.setdefault("score_inputs", {})` at the penalty line and `(parent.get("score_inputs") or {})` at its sibling — the inheritance line, which would have been the next crash and is the shape `paper-hardening` §8b.2 measured six of eleven list-scoped fixes missing. ⛔ THE JUDGEMENT WENT THE HONEST WAY: the dict is created EMPTY, carrying only the flag this function actually observed, rather than filled with zeroed defaults. A hand-filed entry is HAND-SCORED, not unscorable — it carries a `score` its filer typed and a `_score_basis` in prose; what it does not carry is the DERIVED scorer's audit trail, and fabricating one would make it look computed. ✅ `priority.py` now exits 0 and ranks all 126 entries. ⭐ AND IT IS WIRED: `research/autonomy/tests/test_priority_ranks_the_hand_filed_entries_too.py` runs the ranker against the REAL committed ledger (a synthetic two-row fixture would have passed on the broken code, because both rows would have been derived), plus the two unit cases and a precondition test that fails if every entry ever starts carrying `score_inputs` — otherwise this suite would go green for the wrong reason, which is how `in_progress` was dropped from the continuity suite's OPEN_STATES with all twelve tests passing.

⚠ CORRECTION 2026-08-27, appended not edited (CLAUDE.md §1.2), and it goes against my own framing: I wrote that nothing caught this because no gate ran the ranker. **CI caught it and had been red on it.** `systems/tests/test_autonomy_priority.py` runs in tests.yml on every push, and run 33109624214 at 8226753f9 reports FOUR failures reading `KeyError: 'score_inputs'` — the exact traceback — inside `5 failed, 9808 passed`. What is true is narrower and still worth the fix: no PREFLIGHT gate ran the ranker, so the crash was invisible in the COMMIT LOOP and was only ever reported minutes later by a workflow nobody had read that day. ⛔ THE HONEST FINDING IS WORSE THAN THE ONE I CLAIMED: this was not an unseen defect, it was a SEEN one — red on main, in a suite that names it plainly, and it survived anyway. A guard that fires where nobody looks is closer to AUT-PD-018 than I allowed.

entries.what:
⛔⛔ THE STALL HOOK EXITED 0 WITHOUT READING ANYTHING, ANYWHERE ITS HARDCODED PATH DID NOT EXIST — AND ITS OWN TESTS ARE WHAT CAUGHT IT. Measured 2026-09-01 by CYC-0090-d7df5340, in CI run 33513565956, hours after the hook landed in 7335bb83a.
★ THE EVIDENCE, FROM THE RUN LOG RATHER THAN FROM READING THE SCRIPT: three of `test_a_promise_with_no_commit_stops_the_turn.py`'s cases failed on a GitHub runner with `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=0, stdout='', stderr='')` on the three real stalls it catches locally. ⭐ A SILENT EXIT, NOT A WRONG VERDICT — no stderr at all, which is the tell that the script returned before it reached its own logic.
★ THE CAUSE: `REPO="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-/home/user/Rare-cancers}"` followed by `cd "$REPO" 2>/dev/null || exit 0`. A runner has neither the variable nor that path, so the hook exited at line two of its own body. Every assertion in the test file was CORRECT and the hook was never reached.
⛔⛔ AND THE SHAPE IS THIS REPOSITORY'S OLDEST ONE, ARRIVING INSIDE THE FIX FOR ANOTHER INSTANCE OF IT: 'a guard that cannot run is not a guard that passed' — the same finding as `subagent_width` (a governed number no code read for a fortnight) and the census lane wired to a name nothing passed. This hook was written that same hour precisely because CLAUDE.md §2's phrasing test was measured by nothing, and it shipped measured by nothing outside one machine.
★ THE FIX: the repository is DERIVED from the hook's own location (`${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` → strip `/.claude/hooks`), with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` still preferred when it names a real git tree, because the harness knows which project it launched. Each candidate is checked with `git rev-parse --git-dir` rather than assumed.
★ GUARDED: one test added that removes `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` from the environment entirely and requires a stall to still be refused — the anti-vacuity test the file lacked. Verified three ways: in place, with the variable unset, and from a COPY OF THE REPOSITORY AT A DIFFERENT PATH (11/11 in each), which is the CI condition reproduced rather than argued about.

entries.what: ⭐ MEASURE THE BLIND SEATS' MISS RATE, WHICH IS THE ONE NUMBER THAT WOULD LET CLAUSE 1 CARRY A REAL STOPPING BOUNDARY. AUT-PROP-038 established that hardening convergence is an optional-stopping verdict and added the two constraints that need no unknown parameter (the round count must be stated; the declaring round may not be narrower than the widest before it). The constraint it could NOT add is an alpha-spending boundary, because that needs q — the probability a round of k blind seats returns clean while a real defect is present. ★ q IS MEASURABLE FROM WHAT IS ALREADY COMMITTED, and the estimator is the obvious one: a finding raised at round R against text that round R-1 also reviewed is a MISS by round R-1's seats. research/autonomy/review-seats/ holds per-commit blind-seat records with their findings, and git holds the text each commit carried, so for every consecutive pair of rounds on the same paper the denominator (findings raised at R) and the numerator (those whose text predates R's commit) are both derivable. Three papers have such series; PUB-FUSION-PARTNER has four rounds. ⛔ DO NOT ESTIMATE q FROM ROUND-OVER-ROUND FINDING COUNTS ALONE — the counts move because the TEXT moves. The pairing has to be per-finding and text-anchored, or it measures editing rather than missing. ⛔ AND DO NOT LOWER ANY CLAUSE WITH THE RESULT. A measured q can only ever be used to make the stopping rule stricter than the two ordering constraints already are; if it comes out low enough to argue for relaxing them, that argument is `amendment_guard`'s to refuse. ⚠ RENUMBERED ON PUSH (2026-08-28): filed as AUT-PD-123 and a concurrent session filed a different AUT-PD-123 from the same committed state. Second such collision in one session — AUT-PD-122 records the mechanism and the fix that already exists for receipt ids.

⭐ GIVE THE LOOP AN EXTERNALLY-ANCHORED FAILURE VOCABULARY — adopt BixBench3's closed ten-tag failure-mode set as an optional `failure_modes` block on the cycle receipt, and measure it in health.py.
WHY IT IS NOT BUSYWORK: method-watch-autonomy-prior-art.md §2 item 3 states the gap plainly — 'this loop has no external calibration of any kind: health.py grades the loop against rules we wrote.' BixBench3 measured that a run's total failure-tag count predicts its score at Spearman rho = -0.92 (p = 9.9e-6), with premature termination (~2.0x) and repetitive retry loop (~2.2x) the most enriched in the worst quantile. Mapping that vocabulary onto CLAUDE.md's own dated incidents lands SEVEN of the ten (repetitive retry loop = the pgrep self-match loops, 2026-08-26; premature termination = the bare `&` orphaned jobs, 2026-08-27; synthetic/placeholder output = the env-echoed fabricated verdict; output format violation = the generated-artifact regime; environment setup failure = the fresh-sandbox import reds, 2026-08-23; incomplete data = 'an absent reading is not a reading of absence'; inefficient analysis = the serialized-preflight complaint, 2026-08-25).
⛔ THE THREE MISSES ARE THE POINT, AND THE ITEM IS NOT DONE WITHOUT THEM: input misinterpretation, wrong method substitution and method misconfiguration have NO dated incident here. They are the SCIENTIFIC execution errors, and the benign reading (we do not make them) is not the only one — an operational failure is loud and a misconfigured method is silent, and nothing in this loop is instrumented to catch the second. State which of the three this loop could actually detect, and say UNMEASURED for the rest rather than shipping a green row. ⚠ A receipt that records no `failure_modes` block must leave the health row UNMEASURED, never green — the exact defect AUT-PD-013 records for `fanout_is_governed`. entries.what:
⛔ TABLE 1'S LAST COLUMN IS CLIPPED IN THE CANONICAL SUBMISSION PDF, AND THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE ONE THAT CORRUPTED A SEQUENCE LAST TIME.
★ MECHANISM, DIAGNOSED: `wide_body` in build_submission_pdf.py is `len(head) >= LANDSCAPE_MIN_COLS (8) and not _IN_FLOAT`. Table 1 has SIX columns, so it is not wide_body and never receives `.wide-body-table`'s `table-layout: fixed`. The journal and anonymized builds set `tables_in_column: True`, so it renders inside the narrow (~88 mm) column under `.col-float table { font-size: 6.6pt; width: 100% }`. The generic `th, td` rule ALREADY carries `overflow-wrap: break-word`, so this is NOT a wrapping failure: under auto table layout the table's min-content width exceeds its container, the table overflows the column, and the overflow is clipped at the edge. The preprint and manuscript builds do not opt into tables_in_column, which is why 'engineered construct' appears 4x there and 2x here.
⛔⛔ DO NOT REACH STRAIGHT FOR `table-layout: fixed`. The emitter's own comment records that scoping it on column count alone 'broke the deposit': Tables 2-6 picked it up on top of the landscape stylesheet, their sequence cells overflowed and were overprinted, and the journal PDF printed 5'-GGGCATATCCATCAGA3-3' — a CORRUPTED 16-MER with a neighbouring cell's digit fused in, 0 of 93 sequence cells well formed against 93 of 93 in the submission format. A wrong reagent sequence in a published paper is far worse than a clipped word.
★ SO THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS THREE-PART AND MUST BE RUN ON THE REBUILT PDFs, not reasoned about: (1) 'engineered construct' returns to 4 and 'test article' to 8 in the journal build, matching the preprint build; (2) EVERY oligonucleotide cell is byte-identical to fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv — extract them all and compare, do not spot-check; (3) the journal build is still 6 typeset pages (test_the_journal_pdf_fits_its_page_budget). Check the anonymized build too: it is what a double-blind reviewer reads and it shares the defect.
⚠ NOT ATTEMPTED IN THE SESSION THAT DIAGNOSED IT, deliberately. The fix is small; its verification is not, and the failure mode on the other side of it is a corrupted reagent sequence. It wanted a fresh context, not the tail of a long one.

entries.what: ⛔ A REBASE SILENTLY INVALIDATES THE ARCHIVE MANIFEST'S PROVENANCE, AND EVERY GUARD IT HAS STAYS GREEN — MEASURED 2026-08-28 (CYC-0070). AUT-PD-138's ordering says regenerate the manifest against a clean tree as the session's LAST commit, so `git_revision` names the content commit it describes. That is what happened: the manifest named 6a4c833fd, `git_tree_is_clean_apart_from_this_manifest: true`, --check-archive exit 0, and both manifest guard modules 11/11. ⛔ THEN TWELVE COMMITS LANDED FROM A CONCURRENT SESSION AND THE REBASE REWROTE 6a4c833fd TO 656ff2a29992. The manifest was now naming a sha that exists ONLY in this container's reflog — unreachable for anybody who clones — while its clean flag still read true and its inventory was still current. ⭐ THE THREE THINGS THAT WOULD CATCH IT ALL LOOK RIGHT: the cleanliness flag is about the TREE, not the ref; --check-archive explicitly does not compare repository-state fields; and `test_the_manifest_revision_is_a_commit_a_reader_can_resolve` passes locally because the orphaned sha still resolves through the local reflog. It was caught by hand, by comparing git_revision against `git rev-parse HEAD~1` after the rebase, and nothing required that. ⚠ AND THIS IS THE NORMAL CASE, NOT AN EDGE ONE. A concurrent loop session pushed 12 commits during the ~20 minutes this cycle spent rebuilding a deposit family, and the trunk moved under it three separate times. Any manifest commit that has to be rebased has this defect. WHAT TO DO: the candidate is to make the revision check ask git whether the named sha is an ANCESTOR OF THE COMMITTED BRANCH rather than merely resolvable — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <git_revision> HEAD` — which is false for an orphan and true for a real parent, and which the reflog cannot fake. ⚠ Note it must run against the committed history, not the working tree, or it reintroduces AUT-PD-138's ordering trap. ⛔ DO NOT 'fix' this by regenerating the manifest after every rebase as a convention: that is the remembered pairing AUT-PD-130 is about, and it failed there for the same reason it would fail here.

⛔ A ROUND'S ROLL-UP RECORD IS COUNTED AS A SIXTH SEAT BY THE CLAUSE IT FEEDS, SO A ROLL-UP THAT CARRIES THE UNION OF ITS SEATS' FINDINGS DOUBLE-COUNTS THEM. Measured 2026-08-31 by CYC-0090-d7df5340 while writing round 27's record. `publish_bar._seat_records` globs `{pub_id}-{sha}*.json`, and the roll-up's own filename is `PUB-ASO-<sha>.json`, which that glob matches with `*` empty. The clause then computes `seat_blockers`/`seat_p1s` by summing `blockers`/`p1s` over every returned record, roll-up included.
★ TWO CONVENTIONS ARE ON DISK AND THEY ARE OPPOSITE. PUB-ASO-b53290b37…json (round 20) carries EMPTY tallies and says so in a `_tallies_live_on_the_seat_records` field citing the round-7 PUB-FUSION-PARTNER precedent — that one is correct against the code. PUB-ASO-7a7f40825…json (round 26) carries a POPULATED union of 1 blocker and 5 P1s and its `_role` states the opposite rationale in words: 'carries the union of their tallies, so a derivation over the seat glob counts each finding exactly once.' Round 27's roll-up follows the round-20 convention and records why.
⚠ IT HAS COST NOTHING YET, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY IT IS FILED NOW. Clause 1 refuses on any blocker, so an over-count of a non-zero count changes no verdict, and neither round has ever cleared. The reachable failure is the OTHER direction: the clause also refuses when the hardening-state record 'under-reports its own seats' (`len(blockers) < len(seat_blockers)`), and a doubled seat total is what that comparison is made against — so a correct record-keeping round can be refused for under-reporting findings that exist once.
★ THE FIX IS THE INPUT, NOT THE METER (paper-hardening §8.0a's rule, one level over): either the glob excludes the roll-up (`{pub_id}-{sha}-seat-*.json`) or the roll-up is required to carry empty tallies and a guard asserts it. ⛔ Whichever is chosen, `publish_bar.py` is a GOVERNED path — run amendment_guard, and note that the cycle blocked by clause 1 may not be the cycle that changes it.

entries.what:
⛔⛔ `zenodo_deposit.api` HAD NO RETRY, SO ONE TRANSIENT 504 KILLED A WHOLE DEPOSIT RUN — AND THE CYCLE DIAGNOSED IT AS A ZENODO OUTAGE. Measured 2026-09-01 by CYC-0090-d7df5340, which made both errors.
★ THE CODE: `except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc: raise SystemExit(...)`. No retry, no backoff, and no distinction between 4xx (our request is wrong — repeating it is noise) and 5xx (their gateway blinked — repeating a READ is correct). The timeout was already a generous 600 s, so this was never slowness.
⛔ THE WRONG DIAGNOSIS IS THE MORE INSTRUCTIVE HALF. Three runs died and the cycle wrote 'Zenodo's deposit API is down' into a ledger row, a checklist section and a commit message. trimcrae asked whether there was actually an outage; a `record=verify` dispatch then read the published record in THREE SECONDS (run 33508963185). Three responses on one endpoint were generalised into a claim about a service's health, which is the 'probably X' CLAUDE.md §4 forbids — and the discriminating observation cost one dispatch.
★ THE FIX, AND ITS SCOPE IS THE POINT: retry is bounded (4 attempts, 2/6/15 s backoff) and applies ONLY to GET and HEAD, and only on 429/500/502/503/504. ⛔ Mutations are never retried. `actions/newversion` creates a draft, a file PUT uploads bytes and `actions/publish` is irreversible; a blind retry of a POST is how a SECOND orphaned draft gets made, and this cycle had already made the first — the 504 landed on the GET *after* a successful newversion POST.
★ GUARDED AND MUTATION-TESTED, not asserted: `scripts/tests/test_zenodo_api_retries_reads_and_never_mutations.py`, 15 tests covering both halves — reads recover, writes never repeat, 4xx is not retried, an exhausted retry does not read like a one-shot failure, and the backoff table covers the attempt bound. 4/4 mutations caught on a hardlink clone: retry-every-method, retry-4xx, retry-nothing (the original defect) and a short backoff table.

entries.what: ⛔⛔ THE SAME DEFECT AS AUT-PD-086, ON A LIVE ROUTE, AND IT IS THE WORSE DIRECTION. RT-JUNCTION-NEOANTIGEN is `status: blocked` + `pursue_now` + `next.cost: $0`, so it sits IN the queue looking healthy — and its next action is ALREADY DONE. It reads 'Regenerate patient-cd4-demo.json and the TAF15 panel at the corrected junction, then re-grade', and readiness.missing[0] says 'the class-II arm and every CD8∧CD4 figure are WITHHELD until it is'. ⛔ BOTH NAMED REGENERATIONS ARE COMMITTED AND ON THE TRANSCRIPT MODEL: patient-cd4-demo.json carries the corrected junction_context, source.grade EMITTABLE, n_alleles_screened 23, alleles_without_a_model []; the TAF15 panel carries coordinate_system TRANSCRIPT and grade EMITTABLE; hla-coverage.json records matches_corrected_seam true with a null banner. ★★ A FALSE 'WITHHELD' ON A LIVE ROUTE IS WORSE THAN A FALSE PARK: a false park hides work and the row goes quiet, which is at least visible AS silence; a false 'withheld' STOPS the work while leaving the row in the queue looking healthy, so an agent takes it, redoes finished work, and the false claim propagates to every reader. ⚠ NOT VERIFIED by the seat that found this: the third item in readiness.missing (vaccine_construct.py / coverage_scan.py) — coverage-scan.json is ABSENT and vaccine-construct.json carries no source block to grade a seam from, so establish that first rather than assuming it is also stale.  ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s93-falsewithheld, merged at 13105be5d). ALL THREE readiness.missing ENTRIES ARE FALSE, verified independently rather than inherited — and the sibling's description of the third was itself wrong in its premises: NO FILE NAMED coverage-scan.json HAS EVER EXISTED in this history (the tool emits coverage-curve.json and epitope-allele-matrix.json), so the reported 'absence' was the absence of a filename the tool does not use; and vaccine-construct.json DOES carry a graded seam block, named `_inputs.cd4_junction` rather than `source`. ⭐ THE DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION: epitope-allele-matrix.json records n_peptides 174, exactly the unique 8–11-mer set of the CORRECTED five-junction input, recomputed by the seat — so that scan ran on the repaired data. Stronger still, re-running vaccine_construct.py and coverage_scan.py offline reproduces both artifacts BYTE-FOR-BYTE. ⭐ ROUTE UNBLOCKED BUT NOT PARKED (status blocked → ready, pursue_now retained): one free step genuinely remains — the class-I PANEL is HLA-A/HLA-B only and the route's own table names HLA-C as the first extension — and parking it would have been the mirror of the defect this row exists to fix. ⛔ THE RE-GRADE DOES NOT MOVE THE ROUTE UP, and the numbers are pointed at rather than re-typed: class I public junction 8.51% (one allele) rising to 12.3% on the 34-allele scan; class I pooled 27.4–30.4%; class II 6.5% (44 binders, ONE strong, 23 alleles all scored); both arms 1.8%, a PRODUCT and so the smallest number on the route. The global coverage curve reaches NONE of 50/80/90/95% at any point. ⛔⛔ COLLATERAL AND WORSE THAN THE ROW ITSELF: the neoantigen paper asserted IN RUNNING PROSE, outside any marker, that the class-II helper alleles are DRB1*03:01/DRB1*07:01 covering 28.4% GLOBALLY — a pre-regeneration reading that appears NOWHERE in the committed artifact, whose two named alleles present no strong binder at the corrected seam, in a paper whose own banner says every number is quoted from a committed pipeline output. It overstates by ROUGHLY 4×. ⭐ AND THE CORRECTED READING MAKES THE PARAGRAPH'S OWN THESIS — that CD4 help is the limiting arm — STRONGER, which is why the argument was not rewritten, only the figures replaced with supersession markers. Root cause fixed at source: hla_coverage.py built its note as a HARDCODED COUNT beside an interpolated list ('only a 3-allele DR panel (' + 23 alleles), the list made dynamic when the panel widened and the number beside it left behind. ⛔ The revival trigger's first disjunct is already met ON ITS LETTER by a committed artifact while buying ~4 points of coverage — recorded as a defect in the trigger STRING and deliberately NOT rewritten, because sharpening a trigger in the cycle it fired in is what amendment_guard forbids.

entries.what:
⛔⛔ A CI TICK EMPTIED THE STEP-1 FAN-OUT MAP AND THE DEGRADER PAPER'S COMPLETENESS CLAIM NOW HAS NOTHING BEHIND IT. Measured 2026-08-27 by diffing the artifact across the commit that changed it, not inferred: at 1fd33bb `n_complete=18`, `n_computable=18`, `results` held 18 entries; at 91df57d ('step1 fan-out autoscale tick', 2026-08-27T09:36:35Z) `n_complete=0`, `n_computable=19`, `results=[]`. Eighteen computed RBFE edges left the committed map. ⚠ `nr4a3-degrader-paper.md:1426` still reads 'The congeneric map is COMPLETE at 18 computed edges of the 18 that are computable, in a 19-edge map', so a paper claim and its own artifact now disagree — which is what `test_pinned_figures_every_home[step1_fanout_edges_complete]` is red about, and it is RIGHT to be red.
⛔ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND MUST BE THE FIRST THING CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED EITHER WAY: whether the UNDERLYING per-edge results still exist (S3, the per-unit ddg.json files, a prior commit) and only this derived INDEX was clobbered, or whether the fan-out state itself was reset. Those have completely different remedies — regenerate the index, versus 18 edges of GPU spend to redo. ⛔ Do not 'fix' the red by editing the paper down to 0 until that is known; the paper may be the only surviving record of the count.
⚠ AND THE MECHANISM IS THE REAL BUG: a scheduled tick that can overwrite a committed results artifact with an empty one is a data-loss path, and it ran unattended. Whatever the recovery, the tick must not be able to reduce `n_complete` without saying so loudly.

entries.what:
⛔⛔ WITHDRAWN — THE DEFECT THIS ROW DESCRIBED DID NOT HAPPEN, AND THE ROW IS KEPT BECAUSE THE MISREADING IS THE FINDING.
⚠ SUPERSEDED, RETAINED (CLAUDE.md §1.2). This row read: *"A CYCLE CLAIMED AN ITEM, SKIPPED BOTH THE CADENCE STAMP AND THE RECEIPT, DIED IN FOUR MINUTES — AND ITS ROUTINE RUN IS RECORDED SUCCEEDED"*, and costed the damage at 16 hours of a parked free item. Every one of those clauses is false.
★ WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, from the committed receipts:
   CYC-0101-c95ec192 stamped `last_cycle_started_utc` at 00:17:22Z, claimed AUT-PROP-064 at 00:17:56Z, ran to 00:51:00Z, wrote its receipt, and advanced RT-VTE-PROPHYLAXIS.
   CYC-0102-c95ec192 continued the same session 00:44:00Z -> 01:00:00Z and advanced RT-EARLY-PALLIATIVE.
   The cadence gate was never wrong: unmodified, it reads `TOO SOON — 0.7 h since the last cycle (autonomy-state.json `last_cycle_started_utc`, 8:17 PM ET)`.
⛔ SO THE ONE REAL FINDING IS ABOUT THE READER, NOT THE LOOP: **A ROUTINE'S `last_run.finished_at` IS WHEN THE FIRED TURN COMPLETED, NOT WHEN THE SESSION STOPPED WORKING.** `list_triggers` reported finished_at 00:21:37Z for a cycle that ran until 00:51:00Z — a 30-minute truncation — so anyone judging delivery from that field sees every long cycle as a cycle that died. The error is systematic and runs in the ALARMING direction, which is worse than noise: it manufactures incidents.
⚠ AND THE SNAPSHOT WAS TAKEN SEVEN MINUTES INTO A THIRTY-FOUR-MINUTE CYCLE. `git ls-tree origin/main .../receipts | grep CYC-0101` returned 0 files because the receipt had not been PUSHED yet, not because it had not been written. CLAUDE.md §4, verbatim: an absent reading is not a reading of absence. The correct move was to re-read one cadence period later before filing anything, and it cost nothing to do.

entries._score_correction: 134.0 -> 40.0, and the -94.0 is not a re-derivation: THE ROW'S SUBJECT CHANGED. It was scored 134.0 as a delivery defect that parked free work and made the platform's SUCCEEDED signal meaningless. The committed receipts refuted every clause of that — CYC-0101 stamped at 00:17:22Z, ran to 00:51:00Z and advanced RT-VTE-PROPHYLAXIS — so what remains is a reader's caution about `last_run.finished_at`, which is worth recording and is not work. ⛔ Scored DOWN by the session that filed it, on evidence that arrived after it was filed; the direction is away from this session's own item, not toward it.
entries.resolution: ⭐ AND THE FIX WRITTEN FOR IT WAS REVERTED RATHER THAN KEPT. A change to `cadence.last_cycle_start` taking the LATER of the stamp and the newest `claimed_utc` was written, tested, mutation-tested and committed locally before the receipts landed and refuted the premise. It was never pushed. ⛔ IT WAS DROPPED EVEN THOUGH IT WORKED, because a guard added for an incident that did not occur is exactly the accretion `tier-budgets.json` exists to refuse — and it would have carried a false incident narrative in a load-bearing docstring, which the next session inherits as fact. The stamp was doing its job; a second witness to a working gate is not a fix, it is a cost.

entries.evidence: BUILT AND TESTED. Added `lease_arbitration()` to research/autonomy/continuity.py, plus a `--leases` CLI flag. entries.what:
READ ONE PAPER AND ASK ONE QUESTION. BixBench3's task 14 is built on 'RUNX2 inhibition disrupts a PAX3::FOXO1-RUNX2 feed-forward loop and dismantles oncogenic gene programs in fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma' — a transcription-factor-fusion sarcoma whose oncogenic program is dismantled by hitting a COFACTOR rather than the undruggable fusion. That is EMC's problem shape, and this repository has no vocabulary for it.
WHAT TO DO, all $0: (1) resolve and read the source paper (its raw data are public — a BixBench3 inclusion criterion — and it published >=4 ground-truth derived artifacts, also a criterion); (2) ask whether any EWSR1::NR4A3 cofactor forms an analogous feed-forward loop, and whether that is answerable from the EMC expression data ALREADY on disk rather than needing new data; (3) grade it against RT-FUSION-OUTPUT, RT-TXN-CDK and RT-PARTNER-STRAT — is it a variant of one of those, or a route they do not cover?
⛔ WEIGHT IT HONESTLY AND EXPECT A NULL. This is a paper TITLE in the appendix of an unrelated AI benchmark; nothing else has been read, PAX3::FOXO1 is not a FET fusion, and cross-fusion transfer is exactly the kind of analogy that reads as insight and dies on contact with the biology. The deliverable is a graded verdict either way — a clean 'no analogous loop is reported, and here is what would have shown one' is a full result under CLAUDE.md §0, not a failure. ⛔ DO NOT open a route on the title alone. entries.what: ⛔ THE CHAINED HANDOFF HAS A HARD CEILING OF EIGHT GENERATIONS, AND THIS SESSION IS THE EIGHTH. `research-loop` §3 tells a cycle at its session cap to create its own successor with `create_session`, and calls a loop that needs a human to start its next session 'not automated, just a longer fuse'. Measured 2026-08-27 (CYC-0020): that call now REFUSES — 'caller session is at lineage depth 8 (limit 8)'. Each handoff makes the child one generation deeper, so the chain was always going to terminate; nothing in the skill, the generator or the health checker knows the ceiling exists. ⚠ CORRECTED THE SAME HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF. CYC-0020 first recorded this as BLOCKING, on the reasoning that AUT-PROP-019/020 need a reviewer who did not author the text and no session could be created. ⛔ THAT WAS WRONG, AND research-loop §3 SAYS SO IN PLAIN TEXT: the blind seats of a hardening round are PARALLEL SUBAGENTS, not spawned sessions. A subagent starts with a fresh context and has never seen the authoring, which is exactly what 'blind' means here. The seats ran as five concurrent subagents at the governed width. ★ THE LESSON IS NOT ABOUT THIS CEILING: an agent that cannot use its FIRST choice of mechanism must enumerate the others before calling work blocked, and 'blocked' is a claim that needs evidence (CLAUDE.md §0). The depth ceiling is real and still worth fixing — it just never blocked this work. ⭐ THE BACKSTOP STILL HOLDS: the loop's PRIMARY continuation is the UI-created driver Routine (trig_01P9ZNSAw7rNLcKLBFYCwuHp, `13 */4 * * *`, enabled, repo attached, last run SUCCEEDED), which fires a FRESH session at lineage depth 0 every four hours. The chained handoff is the redundancy, not the mechanism. CYC-0020 also ran only ONE cycle of its permitted two, so it never owed a handoff at all. ⛔ THE LIVE RISK IS NARROW AND REAL: a session that REACHES its 2-cycle cap while at depth 8 cannot comply with §3, and `health.py`'s `cycles_are_sized` reads `handoff.child_session_id` — so it would score that session RED for failing to do something the platform forbids. ⭐ WHAT TO FIX: teach the handoff path to detect the refusal and fall back to the driver Routine explicitly (record that the Routine carries the next cycle, rather than leaving the field absent), and teach `cycles_are_sized` that a depth-refused handoff with a live driver Routine is GREEN. ⚠ A cycle may NOT fix this by disabling or re-arming the driver Routine — §7 forbids acting on a `created_via: http_api` Routine from outside it, and `fire_trigger` refuses it too.

Sensitivities are ordinal — verbatim, *"classified as (i) none, (ii) low to moderate and (iii) good to high"* — and AUC and IC50 are computed and **printed for nothing**. entries.what: ⛔ THE LEDGER'S RETRY BUDGET GOVERNS NOTHING, AND THE CODE'S OWN COMMENT SAYS THAT IS THE FAILURE IT WAS MEANT TO PREVENT. Measured by CYC-0015 while deciding whether to take an item showing attempts=6 against retry_budget=3: (1) priority.py line ~177 hardcodes score_inputs['fruitless_attempts'] = 0 and computes it from nothing, though priority-weights.json defines a `fruitless_attempts` term; (2) `attempts` is incremented in exactly ONE place, release_stale_claims — i.e. it counts EXPIRED LEASES, not fruitless work; (3) NOTHING anywhere decrements `retry_budget` (grep: the only writers are priority.py's default of 3 and the modalities work_ledger, a different ledger); (4) health.py's queue_is_takeable filters on `retry_budget > 0` and reports a `retry_budget_spent` list that is therefore ALWAYS EMPTY. priority.py's own line-307 comment: 'so a route could be retried forever and the scorer's fruitless_attempts penalty could never fire.' It cannot fire. ⭐ THE FIX HAS A PROVEN MODEL IN THIS REPOSITORY: research/modalities/work_ledger.py implements the progress-aware version and TESTS it — Entry.fruitless_attempts() counts backwards and stops at the last evidence-fingerprint change, _apply_retry_budget blocks at MAX_FRUITLESS_ATTEMPTS, and progress wipes the count ('a dispatch that WORKED costs nothing'). Port that semantics; do not invent one. ⚠ AND RECORD THE HONEST READING SO THE FIX IS NOT OVERSOLD: a progress-aware counter would NOT have penalised AUT-PROP-002, which moved last_evidence_utc every cycle. This defect did not cause the three-cycle stall CYC-0015 found; it is a separate governance instrument that is inert, and the next item it fails to stop will not announce itself either. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-28 by CYC-0056-schedule. A worktree seat ported work_ledger.py's progress-aware fruitless-attempt semantics into priority.py: a new `dispatch_log` field (stamped by claim.py at claim time with {utc, fingerprint_at_dispatch}) lets fruitless_attempts_count() count backwards through consecutive attempts made against the SAME evidence fingerprint (fingerprint(last_evidence_utc, blocked_evidence)), resetting to zero the moment evidence moves -- 'a dispatch that worked costs nothing', matching work_ledger.py's proven model. Feeds the already-declared but previously-unused `fruitless_attempts` weight; retry_budget is recomputed fresh every re-score (max(0, DEFAULT-count)) rather than never decremented. A spent budget is surfaced through continuity.py's `_retry_budget_spent()` (live-computed, wired into `_why_not_ready()` the same way as the stuck_clock exclusion added earlier this session for AUT-PROP-029) rather than trusting a possibly-stale on-disk field. health.py needed no changes -- queue_is_takeable/top_items already read retry_budget correctly; they were just never given a real number. PLACEMENT NOTE: apply_fruitless_attempts runs AFTER apply_session_penalties (not alongside apply_age_factor before it), deliberately, to avoid the exact prerequisite-assignment overwrite hazard AUT-PD-063 (landed concurrently by a different session, independently verified present on this base) had just fixed for age/blocked_with_evidence -- documented trade-off: a prerequisite inherits its parent's fruitless-attempts decay one re-score late. 22 new tests (18 in test_retries_that_learn_nothing_cost_something.py, 4 added to the continuity stuck_clock test file), 3-way mutation-tested. Independently re-verified before merging: full research/autonomy/tests + systems/tests suite (774 tests) run fresh on the merged tree by this session -- 774 passed, 1 skipped, matching the seat's own reported numbers exactly. HONEST CAVEAT PRESERVED, per the ledger item's own instruction: this does NOT explain the CYC-0015 three-cycle stall -- AUT-PROP-002 moved last_evidence_utc every cycle and a progress-aware counter would not have penalised it. This closes a separate, previously-inert governance instrument, nothing more. SCOPED DOWN (documented, not a gap): claim.py does not refuse claiming an already-spent row -- continuity.py's ready() already keeps it unoffered via the same read-side check, so the property holds without a second enforcement point.

entries.what:
✅ FIXED 2026-08-27 by claim.py's own author, the same hour it was filed. claim.py's Git.push() (research/autonomy/claim.py:79-80) runs `git push -q origin main`, which pushes whatever LOCAL BRANCH IS LITERALLY NAMED 'main' -- stale or unrelated to HEAD if the session's real work is on a differently-named branch (e.g. this repo's 'claude/dreamy-hawking-18pm7n' convention, which stays rebased onto origin/main and is pushed via `git push origin <branch>:main`). On such a session, claim.py's push always fails as a non-fast-forward (or pushes nothing new), so the module cannot actually arbitrate a claim there -- it silently degrades to reporting RETRY forever rather than CLAIMED. MEASURED 2026-08-27 (CYC-0028-moriokat, a subagent dispatched by CYC-0027's driver session): claim.py was tried first for AUT-PD-020, failed exactly this way, and the seat fell back to the manual fetch/verify/edit/commit/`push origin HEAD:main` sequence documented as claim.py's own manual fallback -- work completed correctly, but the module meant to make this race-safe took no part in it. FIX (not applied here, filed for a future cycle): push() should push HEAD, not the ref literally named 'main' -- `git push -q origin HEAD:main`, which is a fast-forward-safe compare-and-swap on the REMOTE ref regardless of what the local branch is named, exactly matching the module's own stated design intent.

⭐ APPLIED EXACTLY AS FILED: `Git.PUSH_REFSPEC = ("push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:main")`. The filing session's diagnosis and its proposed fix were both correct and are taken unchanged. ⛔⛔ THE PART WORTH KEEPING IS HOW IT SURVIVED ITS OWN TEST SUITE: nine tests, eight mutations, and a first real use that reported CLAIMED and pushed — all of it in the ONE configuration that hides the bug, because the author's local branch happened to be named `main`. Every test drove a `FakeGit` that never reaches a real refspec, so the argv was the single thing the suite could not see and the exact thing that was wrong. ⭐ The new test asserts on the argv itself rather than through the fake, which is the only level at which this class of defect is visible. ⚠ AND THE COST WHILE IT WAS OPEN IS THE SHAPE THE MODULE EXISTS TO PREVENT: on a `claude/<name>` branch it did not error loudly, it reported RETRY forever — so a seat trying to claim AUT-PD-020 fell back to the manual fetch/verify/edit/commit sequence and completed the work correctly, while the tool built to make that race-safe took no part in it. A tool that fails by degrading into the manual path it replaced is one nobody notices is broken.

entries.what: ⛔ THE DERIVED-ROW GENERATOR TURNS A ROUTE'S CONCLUSION INTO QUEUED WORK, so the queue offers rows whose own text says there is nothing to do. Measured 2026-08-28 by CYC-0053-3217966b immediately after the additive-score fix (a660303) corrected the ranking — THREE OF THE TOP FIVE ready rows are this shape, and the top row overall is: AUT-013 (172.0, `kind: experiment`, `state: queued`, `_derived: true`) reads "Treat as landscape context; the ex-vivo result is banked and NEEDS NO FURTHER LOOKUP"; AUT-074 (152.0) reads "Report it as a CLOSED LINE: elevated and pan-essential is not an opportunity"; AUT-025 (152.0) reads "KEEP REGISTERED for automatic re-grade when EMC expression data lands" — a row that is waiting on the outside world by construction. All three are derived from systems/graph, all three carry last_evidence_utc in early August, and all three have been offered as takeable work every cycle since. ⚠ THIS IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF THE DEFECT JUST FIXED, and it survives it: the scores are now honest and the STATE is not, so a corrected ranking still points a cycle at non-work. It is also AUT-PD-051's family (a row that is effectively finished still being offered), reached through the generator rather than through a missed closure. ⛔ DO NOT FIX BY HAND-EDITING THE ROWS — they are regenerated from the graph, so a hand edit is erased on the next priority.py --write and the lesson with it. ★ THE FIX BELONGS IN THE GENERATOR OR THE GRAPH: a route whose next action is a conclusion ("needs no further lookup", "closed line") or a registration waiting on the world ("keep registered for automatic re-grade") must derive a row in a parked or blocked state naming what it waits on, never `queued`. ⚠ AND THE HARD PART IS THE DISCRIMINATOR, not the state change: keying on phrases would be a grep over prose that the next re-wording defeats. Prefer a field on the graph node that says whether its next action is an ACTION, a CONCLUSION, or a REGISTRATION — and then the generator reads a field instead of guessing at English. Check whether systems/graph already carries something equivalent before adding one.  ✅ FIXED 2026-08-28 (CYC-0053-3217966b, seat s75-derivedstate, merged at 1eefaf77d). ⛔⛔ THE CLASS IS 39 ROWS, NOT THE 3 THIS ROW WAS FILED ON — half the derived queue, 36 of them `queued`: 23 CONCLUSION and 16 REGISTRATION-waiting-on-the-world, against 38 genuine ACTION rows. The measurement changed the fix from a patch to a state mapping, which is why the row demanded the enumeration first. ⭐ THE DISCRIMINATOR EXISTED ALREADY and no grep over English was needed: `state.status` on every route, a closed vocabulary in systems/CONVENTIONS.md §4.1 pinned by the schema, whose own definitions say there is no takeable step (`parked` = failed with today's tools, `closed` = conclusively unworkable, `delegated` = someone else's). The generator read NONE of it — only `next.blocked_on`, which 11 of 77 routes carry, so the other 66 were born queued BY CONSTRUCTION. Three rival discriminators were measured and refuted, including `next.cost == '$0'` which has no signal at all (all 32 are $0). Precision was chosen over recall because the errors are asymmetric: a miss keeps the status quo, a false park HIDES A LIVE ROUTE. Result: queued 129 → 101, parked 0 → 28; the ready list falls 92 → 65. Nothing is disposed of — the row keeps its id, its score and the route's own words, and a session's `done` still beats a re-derived `parked`. 12/12 mutations caught, after M2 SURVIVED the first version because the false-park test read the module's own set, so widening the set widened the test; the takeable statuses are now written out independently of the module and checked to partition the schema enum.

entries.what: ⛔⛔ `tests.yml` — THE WORKFLOW CLAUDE.md §6 NAMES AS *THE AUTHORITY* FOR BOTH LARGE SUITES — HAS NOT PRODUCED A VERDICT ON `main` FOR AT LEAST TWENTY MINUTES, AND ITS OWN CONFIG SAYS IT SHOULD. The workflow sets `group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, and carries a 12-line comment stating '`main` IS DELIBERATELY EXEMPT … every commit on it keeps its own per-commit verdict rather than inheriting the next one's'. Observed behaviour is the exact opposite. ★ THE FIX IS TO THE GROUP, NOT THE FLAG: give a run on `main` a group of its own (`github.run_id`) so main runs never queue against one another, and leave feature branches sharing a ref-keyed group so they still collapse to the tip. That preserves the stated intent of the existing comment exactly.

entries.evidence: MEASURED 2026-08-28 BY CYC-0068-7cda2d61, THREE INDEPENDENT WAYS, AND THE FIRST HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG. (1) TIMING: the nine most recent completed `tests` runs on `main` are all `cancelled`, and each is cancelled 1–3 s after the NEXT run on main is created — 8c14cc5 cancelled 20:24:23 as 3937db8 was created 20:24:22; 3937db8 cancelled 20:24:30 as e958d85 created 20:24:28; e958d85 cancelled 20:26:50 as d18f8dc created 20:26:49; d18f8dc cancelled 20:27:39 as 54aeece created 20:27:37; 54aeece cancelled 20:33:06 as 5bb4e86 created 20:33:05; 5bb4e86 cancelled 20:34:42 as 12a5f34 created 20:34:41. (2) THE DISCRIMINATING CASE: run 33207278897 on 86098c2 was `pending`, NOT running, when it was cancelled at 20:17:54 — so this is not `cancel-in-progress` firing, which only ever cancels a RUNNING run. (3) PLATFORM SEMANTICS, READ LIVE RATHER THAN REMEMBERED: a concurrency group holds at most one running and one pending run, so a third arrival EVICTS THE PENDING ONE whatever `cancel-in-progress` says. ⚠ MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS — that the expression evaluates to the string 'false' and is truthy — IS NOT WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS, and (2) is the observation that killed it. ⭐ CORROBORATING: `tests.yml` is the ONLY workflow in .github/workflows/ with an expression-valued `cancel-in-progress`; every other uses a literal. ⛔ CONSEQUENCE: this is the concrete mechanism behind health.py's `gates_green` reading NO-GATE-VERDICT for 47.2 h, and it means the two large suites — the ones preflight deliberately does NOT run, on the stated grounds that 'CI runs both on push and it is the authority' — have not actually gated any recent commit. ⭐ DONE 2026-08-28 by CYC-0068-7cda2d61: concurrency.group now gives a run on `main` a group of its own (github.run_id) while feature branches keep the shared ref-keyed group; cancel-in-progress is UNCHANGED because it was never the mechanism. Guarded by test_main_keeps_a_per_commit_verdict.py, written against the GROUP rather than the flag because asserting the flag would have passed throughout the outage; mutation-tested 4/4. ⭐ LIVE HALF NOW MEASURED: at 20:52Z, immediately after the push, TWO runs on `main` were `in_progress` simultaneously — 2334df9 (created 20:52:16) and 4cb2c64b (created 20:47:16, still alive) — where the old shared group would have evicted the second. ⛔ STILL NOT OBSERVED: that a run on main reaches a CONCLUSION. Coexistence is necessary, not sufficient, and `gates_verdict.py` needs a graded run before `gates_green` reads anything but NO-GATE-VERDICT.

entries.what: ⛔⛔ A ROW CARRYING `"score_inputs": null` CRASHED `priority.py --write` — STEP 3 OF EVERY CYCLE — AND THE CALENDAR PULLED THE TRIGGER, SO NO COMMIT LOOKS GUILTY. Measured 2026-08-29T00:02Z (CYC-0073-2e57571a). `apply_age_factor` wrote through `e.setdefault("score_inputs", {})["age_factor"] = f`, and `setdefault` RETURNS THE EXISTING VALUE when the key is present — so on `AUT-COV-001`, filed by CYC-0011 and sitting on the trunk for days, it evaluated `None["age_factor"] = f` and raised `TypeError: 'NoneType' object does not support item assignment`. ⭐ WHY IT FIRED WHEN IT DID, WHICH IS THE INTERESTING HALF. Two lines above, `prev` was ALREADY read defensively (`(e.get("score_inputs") or {})`), and the guard `if not f and not prev: continue` skipped this row for as long as its age factor rounded to zero. The date rolling from 08-28 to 08-29 made `f` non-zero for the first time, the row reached the write, and step 3 began failing on state no cycle had touched. A latent null plus a clock is a time bomb with no author. ⛔⛔ AND IT DEADLOCKED THE LOOP RATHER THAN MERELY FAILING IT — THE TWO FAILURES EACH BLOCKED THE OTHER'S FIX. With the re-score dead, every stored `score_inputs.age_factor` was stale against the new date, so `admissibility.check_write` refused EVERY ledger write as `refused_stale_input`. Observed directly: `claim.py --id AUT-PD-147` exited 1 with five `refused_stale_input` rows. So a cycle could not re-score (crash) and could not claim (refused), and step 4 of the contract was unreachable. ⭐ FIXED, AND THE CLASS CLOSED RATHER THAN THE INSTANCE. The write now type-checks instead of relying on `setdefault`; and the READ was hardened in the same edit, because `(x or {})` is a FALSINESS test wearing a type check's clothes — it survives None, '', 0 and [] and raises on a truthy non-dict (`'str' object has no attribute 'get'`). That second hole was found by this fix's own regression test, not by inspection. `AUT-COV-001` now normalises to `{'age_factor': 0.0714}` on the next write. ⚠ THIS IS A SURVIVOR OF AUT-PD-050, WHICH FIXED CRASHES IN THIS SAME FUNCTION. It survived because `null` is not `absent`: `setdefault` handles the absent key, which is the case anyone testing by hand reaches for, and there was no row with an explicit null until CYC-0011 wrote one. ★ EVIDENCE: 10 assertions in `research/autonomy/tests/test_a_null_score_inputs_does_not_stop_the_loop.py`, including one that re-scores the REAL committed ledger at today's date and at today+400 days — a synthetic row would not have caught this, because the row that broke the loop was real state nobody had touched. 5/5 mutations caught, including reverting each half of the fix independently. Full loop-instrument suite 570 passed.
entries.evidence: ✅ DONE 2026-08-29, commit f8eb2bd68 (fix) — and the claim that followed it is the proof the deadlock is broken: `claim.py --id AUT-PD-152` returned CLAIMED on attempt 1, where the same tool against AUT-PD-147 had exited 1 with five `refused_stale_input` rows twenty minutes earlier. ⛔ THE CLAIM CAME AFTER THE FIX, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS A DEPARTURE FROM CONTRACT STEP 4 WORTH NAMING RATHER THAN HIDING. Step 4 says claim before any work. The claim mechanism was the thing that was broken — `claim.py` writes the lease through `ledger_io.write_ledger`, which runs `admissibility.check_write`, which refused every write while the stored age factors were stale, and they were stale because the re-score that refreshes them was the crash. There was no ordering that claims first. The exposure this leaves is real and bounded: between the fix and the claim another session could have taken the row, and the answer to that is the push, which is the arbiter (AUT-PD-021). ⭐ TWO HOLES CLOSED, NOT ONE. The write no longer leans on `setdefault` (which returns the existing value, hence `None['age_factor'] = f`). The read no longer leans on `(x or {})`, which is a falsiness test wearing a type check's clothes — it survives None, '', 0 and [] and raises on a truthy non-dict. The second hole was found by the regression test written for the first, not by inspection. ★ 10 assertions in test_a_null_score_inputs_does_not_stop_the_loop.py, one of which re-scores the REAL committed ledger at today and at today+400 days — a synthetic row would not have caught this, because the row that broke the loop was real state nobody had touched. 5/5 mutations caught (each half of the fix reverted independently, plus prev-double-counting and the closed-row skip). Loop-instrument suite 570 passed; preflight green.

entries.what:
⛔ `dev-setup.sh` INSTALLS `libreoffice-writer` WITHOUT AN `apt-get update` FIRST, SO A STALE CONTAINER INDEX MAKES THE .docx CHAIN FAIL — AND THE SessionStart HOOK REPORTS 'DEV SETUP OK' OVER IT. Measured 2026-08-31 by CYC-0090-d7df5340, which paid for it.
★ THE CHAIN, EACH LINK A COMMAND. The image's package index is frozen at build time; the Ubuntu archive has since moved past 24.2.7-0ubuntu0.24.04.4, so the install returns `E: Failed to fetch .../libreoffice-writer_24.2.7-0ubuntu0.24.04.4_amd64.deb  404  Not Found` for four .debs. The block is deliberately non-fatal and writes its warning to stderr, so the hook's success line was printed over the failure. `regenerate_aso_chain.sh` then failed three steps — aso_priorart_evidence.py, build_submission_parts.py, build_submission_docx.py — with `Error: source file could not be loaded`, which points at the INPUT and is the exact misdirection dev-setup.sh's own comment block records having cost this repository three days.
⛔ SO THE DEFECT IS NOT THE MISSING PACKAGE — THAT WAS DIAGNOSED AND WRITTEN DOWN ON 2026-08-30, IN THIS FILE, ABOVE THE LINE THAT FAILS. It is that the automated remedy could not run and said nothing a reader would see. A probe that detects the condition, attempts the fix, fails, and reports OK is worse than no probe: the next session trusts it.
★ FIXED IN THIS COMMIT, one line: `apt-get update -qq` before the install, with sudo fallbacks on both halves. Measured working — the identical install then succeeded and build_submission_docx.py wrote the .docx.
⚠ WHAT IS NOT FIXED AND IS FILED RATHER THAN CLAIMED: the branch is still non-fatal by design (the ghostscript precedent, named in the block), so a future failure of this install is still only a stderr line under a green hook message. Making the hook surface its own warnings is a separate change to a separate file and is not taken here.

entries.what:
⛔⛔ THE READY-WORK STOP HOOK AND THE CADENCE GATE GIVE OPPOSITE ANSWERS FOR THE SAME SCHEDULED FIRE, AND NEITHER FILE KNOWS THE OTHER EXISTS. Measured 2026-09-03 by a scheduled-Routine session: `cadence.py --check` exited 3 ("TOO SOON — 3.9 h since the last cycle ... against a declared 8 h cadence") and the research-loop skill's own §1 table instructs, verbatim, "Exit immediately. Write no receipt, take no item, claim nothing." The session did exactly that and ended its turn with a one-line explanation and route_advanced: none.
⭐ `.claude/hooks/ready-work-at-turn-end.sh` then fired on that exact Stop and refused it: 154 free, unclaimed, unblocked ledger rows were sitting idle and nothing was observably running, so it demanded one of (1a) a worker running that should be claimed, (1b) a spawned session, (2) a genuine external block, or (3) start one — and it explicitly pre-empts the exact reasoning the session had just used: "A SCHEDULED ROUTINE IS NOT AN ANSWER ... naming a future scheduler is a deferral with a citation, not continuation."
⛔ THE CONFLICT IS REAL, NOT A MISREADING ON EITHER SIDE. `cadence.py`'s own docstring says its whole purpose is to make "a fire that arrives too soon exit[] in two tool calls instead of running a cycle" — i.e. this session's exact behaviour is the DESIGNED response to a too-frequent cron (`13 */4 * * *` against a declared 8-24h cadence). The Stop hook has no branch for "this stop IS the cadence gate working" — it only sees ready work and nothing running, which is indistinguishable, from its vantage point, from a session that simply declined to look.
★ NOT FIXED HERE: which side should yield is a design call (teach the hook to read cadence.py's exit code / a receipt-free cadence-skip marker before it fires, vs. teach cadence.py that a Stop-hook demand outranks the throttle) and changing either file from inside the cycle the tension blocked is exactly the self-serving edit §6's `amendment_guard` exists to catch. Filed for the record rather than resolved by fiat.
⚠ What this session actually did: answered the hook honestly (cadence-gated skip, evidenced by the exit-3 output), filed this entry as the $0 administrative act CLAUDE.md §6 sanctions for friction ("Improvement comes from RECEIPTS, never introspection. Hit friction → file a process_defect entry with the evidence"), and did NOT start a new cycle against the cadence throttle.

entries.what:
⛔⛔ TWO TEST FUNCTIONS IN `systems/tests/test_autonomy_health.py` HAD NOT RUN FOR A WEEK, AND NOTHING ANYWHERE SAID SO. Found 2026-09-03 while looking for a slot under the commit-loop tier ceiling, which stood at exactly 1400/1400.
★ THE MEASUREMENT, NOT AN INFERENCE: `ast` finds 77 `def test_` in that file; `pytest --collect-only -q` reports 75.
   test_an_unreadable_state_or_absent_cap_is_unmeasured_not_green   lines 896 AND 999
   test_the_cap_is_read_from_state_and_never_typed_in_the_checker   lines 903 AND 1004
The pair at 896/903 test `c_cycles_are_sized`; the pair at 999/1004 test `c_fanout_is_governed`. They are DIFFERENT tests of DIFFERENT conditions that happen to share a name, and Python binds a module-level name once — so the later definition silently replaced the earlier and the cycles-are-sized pair ceased to exist.
⛔ A SHADOWED TEST DOES NOT FAIL, IT STOPS EXISTING: nothing red, nothing reported skipped, no coverage number moves. And it is still PAID FOR — the tier budget counts source functions, so the ceiling was full of two guards measuring nothing.
⚠ WHICH TWO DIED MATTERS: the anti-defeat guard ('an unreadable state or absent cap is UNMEASURED, not green') and the one-fact-one-place guard ('the cap is read from state and never typed in the checker') — both on `cycles_are_sized`, the row CLAUDE.md §6 added precisely because the session-shape rule was measured by nothing.
entries.resolution:
Renamed the cycles-are-sized pair after their subject (`..._cycle_cap_...`); the file now collects 77 and passes 77. ★ AND THE CLASS IS GATED RATHER THAN THE INSTANCE: `scripts/tier_budget.py` already parses every test file to count it, so it now also reports any test name bound twice in one namespace (module body or class body) and `--check` EXITS NON-ZERO on one even when every tier is under its ceiling — detection without refusal is a report nobody acts on. It runs in the DEFAULT preflight tier, so it fires on the commit that creates the collision.
⚠ The guard is folded into `test_the_counter_counts_and_a_shadowed_test_is_not_a_test` rather than added as a new function, and that is said out loud in its docstring: the tier was AT its ceiling, `tier-budgets.json` names raising it as the LAST of three answers, and whether the counter's number is a number of tests that RUN is a property of that counter's own arithmetic — the same claim the test already made.
